docs.title: Commol
docs.text:
Commol builds, simulates and calibrates compartment models: amounts move between states (compartments) at rates you write as formulas. An amount can be a count, a mass or a concentration. You describe the model in Python; a Rust engine expands it over your stratifications, compiles every rate to machine code, and runs it or fits it to your data.

Before version 1.0

The API can change between minor versions (0.2 → 0.3). The changelog marks every change that breaks code as Breaking.

docs.title: How Commol works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[ModelBuilder] -->|build| B[Model]
    B --> C[Simulation]
    C -->|run| D[Results]
    B --> E[CalibrationProblem]
    E --> F[Calibrator]
    F -->|run| G[CalibrationResult]
    G -->|apply_calibration_parameters| B
  1. Build a Model with ModelBuilder: bins, parameters, transitions, stratifications and initial conditions. Commol validates it as you go.
  2. Simulate it with Simulation: one series per compartment and accumulator.
  3. Calibrate unknown values against observations with Calibrator, and write the result back into the model.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from commol import ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.99},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.01},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=100)

docs.text:
Back to Home

All notable changes to Commol will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• An ODE engine: a model built with engine="DifferentialEquations" runs in continuous time, dX/dt = Σ flows, integrated by diffsol (commol-differential). It has the same flows, outputs, accumulators, calibration, ensembles, reports and plots as a difference model. On [n, n + 1) a rate sees step = n and the continuous t. The engine restarts its integration at each integer when a rate reads step, and where t reaches a value a rate compares it with (t >= t_on), so the solver cannot step over a jump.
  • OdeSolver (method "tsit45" or "bdf", rtol, atol), the settings of the DifferentialEquations engine, stored in the model as Model.engine.settings and set with build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...).
  • One list of engines in the Rust engine (EngineType): each entry names the model kind it runs, validates its settings, and says the form of its equations and what a rate means (per_step or continuous). Python asks it through commol_rs.engine.EngineType instead of branching on engine names.
  • Simulation.run_at(at): the outputs at the given sorted positions. A differential model takes any position, such as 0.5.
  • SimulationResults: what Simulation.run and run_at return. A dict from output name to values, as before, with the positions in positions and the rows in rows().
  • The window grid as module functions: window_start, window_end, window_index and window_ends, beside windowed_totals.
  • A public Pydantic class rejects an unknown field and names it (extra="forbid" on every class of commol.__all__), so a misspelt or an old name is an error instead of being dropped.
  • Impulses: add_transition(..., impulse_at=[...]) or impulse_every=(period, offset) moves the rate (a fraction or an amount) at once at those steps, in both engines, before the flows of the step. print_equations lists impulses apart.
  • ModelBuilder(..., step_unit=...) (Model.step_unit): the unit of one step for the unit check, of any single dimension: the axis is the independent variable of the model, which need not be time (for example "meter"). Without it, the check infers the unit as before.
  • TimeScale.from_step_unit(unit), which raises for a unit that is not time.
  • One interface for every kind of model: ModelStructure, an abstract base class that the structure of each kind inherits. Simulation, Calibrator, ProbabilisticCalibrator, the reports and SimulationPlotter use only it, so another kind (for example an agent network) is a new subclass with its engines in the engine's list. CompartmentalStructure is the structure of a compartmental model. A subclass that misses a method cannot be made, and the error names the method.
  • An engine runs one model kind, and a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine and both kinds.
  • Each kind declares the values calibration may set besides parameter and factor (ModelStructure.calibration_value_types); a compartmental model accepts initial_condition. A type the kind does not accept raises an error that names the kind.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A position on the axis is a float everywhere, and the engine alone decides which positions its model type accepts: a difference model integer steps, a differential model any non-negative position. Its error names the observation, constraint, impulse transition or series parameter that holds a rejected position. The engine trait runs only at positions (run_at_positions_into_buffer); run(n) returns the grid it ran on.
  • The engine of a model and its settings are one field, Model.engine = {type, settings} (ModelEngine), which replaces Model.dynamics.typology. The builder takes the engine where it builds, so one builder builds the model for each engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both. A model file saved before has dynamics.typology and does not load: move it to "engine": {"type": …, "settings": null}.
Before Now builder.build(typology="DifferenceEquations") builder.build(engine="DifferenceEquations") model.dynamics.typology model.engine.type commol_rs.difference.DifferenceEquations(model), commol_rs.differential.DifferentialEquations(model) commol_rs.engine.Engine(model), the engine the model names - A model is a header, an engine and a structure: Model.structure, tagged in JSON by kind, replaces Model.population and Model.dynamics, and the transitions are held once. Model is generic in its structure class: ModelBuilder.build returns Model[CompartmentalStructure], and Model.from_json reads the class from the kind. The methods that only a compartmental model has moved to its structure. A model file saved before has population and dynamics and does not load: move the fields of population and dynamics.transitions into "structure": {"kind": "compartmental", …}. Before Now model.population.bins, .accumulators, .stratifications, .initial_conditions model.structure.bins, … model.dynamics.transitions (and model.population.transitions) model.structure.transitions model.initial_state() model.structure.initial_state() model.update_initial_conditions(…), update_stratification_fractions(…), update_compartment_fractions(…) model.structure.update_initial_conditions(…), … model.subgroup_population(…), model.get_conditioning_categories(…) model.structure.subgroup_total(…), model.structure.get_conditioning_categories(…) model.get_outputs_by_source() model.structure.outputs_by_source() model.get_uncalibrated_initial_conditions() model.structure.uncalibrated_values() commol.context.dynamics (Transition, StratifiedRate) commol.context.transition commol.context.engine.EngineType CompartmentalEngineType; ModelEngine.type is a str that the engine's list checks commol_rs.core.Model(population=…, dynamics=…) commol_rs.core.Model(structure=commol_rs.core.CompartmentalStructure(…)) commol_rs.model.initial_state(model), expanded_outputs, transition_flows they take a commol_rs.core.CompartmentalStructure commol_rs.calibration.check_initial_conditions check_model_values commol_rs.calibration.calibrate(…, initial_population_size, …) and the other calibration functions no initial_population_size: the engine knows it
  • applied_parameters_report returns parameters and the sections of the kind of the model; a compartmental model adds initial_conditions, with the same keys as before.
  • The Rust engine trait (SimulationEngine) is the same for every model kind: compartments, state (was population), set_initial_condition and output_labels moved to CompartmentalEngine (commol-model), and the engine resolves and writes the values of its kind (plan_values, apply_values). The initial-condition plan moved from commol-calibration to commol-model. The crates are not published.
  • Names of positions, lengths and counts, and names with more than one meaning. No old name is kept; an old keyword raises an error that names it.
Before Now ObservedDataPoint(step=…) ObservedDataPoint(at=…) ObservedDataPoint(window_steps=…) ObservedDataPoint(window=…) ObservedDataPoint(compartment="B") ObservedDataPoint(output="B") ObservedDataPoint(compartment="label", compartments=[…]) ObservedDataPoint(label="label", outputs=[…]) ObservedDataPoint(scale_id=…) ObservedDataPoint(factor_id=…) CalibrationParameter(parameter_type="scale"), CalibrationParameterType.SCALE "factor", CalibrationParameterType.FACTOR CalibrationConstraint(time_steps=…) CalibrationConstraint(at=…) NelderMeadConfig(initial_step=…) NelderMeadConfig(initial_simplex_size=…) Simulation.run_at(steps) Simulation.run_at(at) Simulation.windowed_totals(results, source_ids, window_steps, at_steps) Simulation.windowed_totals(results, ids, window, at) Simulation.total_series(results, source_ids), group_outputs(source_ids), outputs_for(source_id) ids, id windowed_totals(series, window_steps, at_steps) windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at) window_end_steps(window_steps, num_steps) window_ends(window, end) TimeScale.window_start, window_end, window_index commol.window_start, window_end, window_index simulation_report(…, steps, window_steps, …), series_report, accumulators_report, observed_report at, window SimulationPlotter.plot_series(step_to_label=…) position_label=…, which takes a float TimePattern (commol.api.time_patterns) AxisPattern (commol.api.patterns) TimePattern.window(start, end, amount) AxisPattern.interval(start, end, value) TimeSeriesValue, "time-series parameter" SeriesValue, "series parameter" EnsembleSolution.windowed_prediction_steps windowed_prediction_positions engine.current_step() engine.current_position() simulation.run(n, output_format="list_of_lists") simulation.run(n).rows()
  • Reports, windows, plots and ensemble statistics read a value at a position of the results, not at a list index, so a differential model windows and reports at non-integer positions once its results hold them. The report key scale_id is factor_id, and compartments is outputs.
  • EnsembleSolution has prediction_positions; its prediction series hold the unit grid and every observation position and window start.
  • Series parameters take (position, value) points with float positions. "linear" interpolates in t and "step_function" holds from any position; a differential engine restarts its integration at their points, so a "linear" series is a ramp, not a staircase. "pulse" keeps integer positions. A difference model gives the same results and rejects a point between integers.
  • AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp read t and take float bounds. A difference model gives the same results; in a differential model an interval opens at any position and a ramp is continuous.
  • A pattern parameter that the builder generates is named _series_<n> (was _ts_<n>).
  • The model compiler moved from commol-difference to the new crate commol-model, which both engines use; commol_rs.difference no longer has initial_state, expanded_outputs, transition_flows and check_names, which are in commol_rs.model. No public Python name changes.
  • SimulationPlotter.plot_series and plot_cumulative take series instead of bins. An entry is an output name or a bin or accumulator id; an id plots the sum of its outputs, so a bin of a stratified model can be plotted. There is no bins alias: rename the argument.
  • Every loss uses the observation weights the same way: "sse" is Σ w·r², "rmse" is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w) and "mae" is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. Before, "sse" squared the weight and "rmse" and "mae" ignored it. With every weight at 1 nothing changes. The ensemble central loss follows the same rule.
  • Simulation.run starts from the initial state at every call, so two calls give the same result. Before, a second run continued the first one. To continue a run, call simulation.engine.step().

  • Model.check_unit_consistency infers one step unit from the parameter units (day, week, step, …; step when there is none) and requires every flow to be exactly <bin unit>/<step unit>. A model in "1/step" now passes. Rates in two units of time, such as "1/day" and "1/week", are an error that names each parameter, because the engine converts nothing. Before, the check accepted any convertible unit and defaulted to day.

  • Nelder-Mead searches inside the bounds: it optimizes an unbounded coordinate and scores x = lo + (hi − lo)·(sin u + 1)/2. Its first simplex is set by NelderMeadConfig.initial_simplex_size (a fraction of each bound width, default 0.1), which replaces simplex_perturbation; there is no alias. Every Nelder-Mead result can change.

  • The library names what the compartments hold without assuming individuals: the state (the amount of every compartment), the amount (the value of one compartment), the total (their sum, which the initial fractions are taken of) and a subgroup total (the sum of the compartments with some categories). The total is a float, finite and greater than 0, so a model of a mass or a concentration can be stated; before, it was an int. The rate variable N is total and N_<cat>… is total_<cat>…, so N is a free id (a bin may be named N). AxisPattern takes a value. No old name is kept: a model file with population_size does not load, and the error names the field; rename it to total, and N to total in every rate, formula and constraint.

Before Now set_initial_conditions(population_size=…), InitialConditions.population_size: int, JSON key population_size set_initial_conditions(total=…), InitialConditions.total: float, JSON key total Rate, formula and constraint variables N, N_<cat>… (N_g1, N_g1_t1) total, total_<cat>… (total_g1, total_g1_t1) RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES = ("N", …) ("total", "step", "t", "pi", "e") InitialConditions.subgroup_population(…), CompartmentalStructure.subgroup_population(…) subgroup_total(…) InitialCompartment.population InitialCompartment.amount applied_parameters_report: row "N", group "population" row "total", group "total" AxisPattern.pulse(at, amount), pulses(at, amount), periodic(period, amount, offset), interval(start, end, amount) value instead of amount get_predefined_variable_units(stratifications, bin_unit) get_predefined_variable_units(subgroup_totals, bin_unit), with the names the engine gives commol_rs.engine.Engine.population Engine.state commol_rs.core.InitialConditions(population_size=…) InitialConditions(total=…) commol_rs.calibration.calibrated_initial_population calibrated_initial_state — commol_rs.model.subgroup_total_names(structure) Rust: CompartmentalEngine::population, population_size; DifferenceEquations::population, DifferentialEquations::population state, total

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Transition conditions: Transition.condition, the condition argument of ModelBuilder.add_transition, ModelBuilder.create_condition, the Condition and Rule types, and the LogicOperators and VariablePrefixes enums, in Python and in Rust. The engine never evaluated them, so a condition that was never true still moved population. Write the condition in the rate ("if(step > 30, k, 0)"), or use an AxisPattern or a stratified rate. A model file with a condition key raises an error that names it.
  • Simulation.run(..., output_format=...) and run_at(..., output_format=...): both return SimulationResults; use rows() for one row per position.
  • commol_core::integer_steps, SimulationEngine::run_into_buffer and run_at_steps_into_buffer; the Python checks that repeated the engine's rules on positions (check_steps_for_typology, the impulse check of Dynamics, the order check of Simulation.run_at).
  • The "weighted_sse" loss and LossConfig.weighted_sse(). Use "sse", which uses the weights.
  • commol.constants.ModelTypes. The names of the compartmental engines are the Literal commol.context.engine.CompartmentalEngineType.
  • Population and Dynamics, in Python (commol.context.population, commol.context.dynamics) and in Rust, and their PyO3 classes; the structure of a model is CompartmentalStructure.
  • Model.get_uncalibrated_initial_conditions, Model.initial_state, and the other methods of a compartmental model on Model: they are on model.structure (see Changed).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A differential model: on a piece of integration that ends where a rate jumps (a value t is compared with, a series point), the right-hand side sees t below the end. Before, the last solver step of the piece already saw the rate after the jump, so a rate of 0.5 that starts at 2.5 moved 3·10⁻⁸ of the state before 2.5.

  • CalibrationResult.converged is True only when the optimizer met its convergence test or target_cost. Before, every finished run reported True, also one that stopped at max_iterations.

  • Nelder-Mead from a start value of 0 builds a real simplex, and no longer stops at a bound where the clamped loss is flat. Before, the simplex was degenerate at 0, and could collapse on a bound and report converged=True.
  • The verbose Nelder-Mead run uses the configured simplex. Before, it always used a 10% perturbation.
  • Model.check_unit_consistency names every bin without a unit. Before, it failed with "'None' is not defined in the unit registry".
  • A Simulation follows its model: run and engine rebuild the engine when the model changed after the Simulation was created, for example with update_parameters or apply_calibration_parameters. Before, it used the old values, or failed with "Parameter index … not found" for a parameter that was None.
  • pi and e work in every transition rate, such as "pi * k * A". Before, outside a function argument, the simulation failed with "Variable 'pi' not found".
  • % (remainder) works as the only operator of a rate, as in "step % 7". Before, the rate was read as a parameter name.
  • A total_… variable that names no subgroup total, such as total_t1_g1 when group is declared before type, is a build error that lists the valid names. Before, a formula parameter or the engine gave it the value 0.
  • A bin or an accumulator id cannot be total, step, t, pi or e, and a bin cannot expand into a name that is also a total_<categories> subgroup total. Before, the engine variable hid such a bin, and the two sums shared one value.
  • A parameter id cannot be total, step, t, pi, e, an expanded compartment or a subgroup total. Before, only bin ids were rejected, and the parameter and the engine variable shared one value.
  • ModelBuilder.reset removes the accumulators, and ModelBuilder.clone copies them and the bin_unit. Before, reset kept the accumulators and a clone lost them.
  • An initial_condition id is resolved by the engine when the Calibrator or the ProbabilisticCalibrator is created. A category of a non-binary stratification now gives "needs a binary stratification" instead of "not found", and bin prefixes ("B_g1") and qualified categories ("group:g1") are accepted, as documented. Before, both were rejected as "not found".

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• The guide is rewritten and split into pages with one job each (building models, transitions, expressions, time patterns, units, simulations, and six calibration pages). Every example runs in CI, and every claim was checked against the engine. Behaviors that were described wrongly are now documented as they are, among them: a violated constraint replaces the loss with a penalty.
  • The API reference documents every public name, and Model, plotting and reports have their own pages.
  • The site publishes llms.txt and llms-full.txt for AI agents, and marks the pages of the dev version.
  • README.md is a short landing page with links to the documentation.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Per-compartment initial conditions: InitialConditions.compartment_fractions (Python and Rust) accepts overrides keyed by expanded compartment name, expressed as fractions of the total population and applied after the uniform expansion. Includes ModelBuilder.set_initial_conditions(compartment_fractions=...), Model.update_compartment_fractions, and Model.initial_state(), which returns each expanded compartment with its bin, categories and initial population as the engine builds it. The Rust engine is the single source of truth for the expansion and validates the overrides (unknown or repeated name, fraction outside 0.0..=1.0, total above population_size).
  • Rust commol_difference::initial_state and commol_calibration::calibrated_initial_population, exposed to Python. The calibration objective, the calibrated predictions and the model write-back share one implementation of how calibration values reach the engine.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: calibrated initial conditions no longer auto-calculate the last population-fraction value as the remainder of the population. The new CalibrationProblem.initial_condition_remainder names the compartment or bin that absorbs the difference; it is not calibrated and keeps its own split. Without it, values are applied as given and only an initial population above population_size is penalized. A single exact compartment, such as a composite state, can now be calibrated on its own.
  • Breaking: calibrated initial conditions are applied in fixed layers — bins, category splits, exact compartments, remainder — instead of in parameter order.
  • Breaking: a stratification category may be named with a qualified id (sex:female). A bare name that more than one stratification declares is rejected as ambiguous, in calibration and in update_stratification_fractions, and the report qualifies its rows. Category pairs come from the engine's compartment labels instead of parsing compartment names.
  • Breaking: get_category_fraction, subgroup_population and get_conditioning_categories resolve category ids like calibration: a qualified id (sex:female) selects its stratification and a bare name that more than one stratification declares raises instead of silently using the first one. get_conditioning_categories returns qualified ids for shared names.
  • Bin and bin-prefix initial-condition ids, and the remainder, resolve from the engine's compartment labels instead of name prefixes, so a bin A no longer covers the compartments of a bin A_x.
  • The Rust engine expands bins and accumulators in one function; the equation printer and unit checker use it (expanded_outputs) instead of their own Python expansion. The Rust ModelTypes gains DifferentialEquations, so any model definition can be expanded; the difference engine rejects it.
  • Breaking: update_bin_fractions / update_initial_conditions apply the same rule as construction: the bin fractions must sum to 1.0 after the update.

  • Breaking (Rust): SimulationEngine requires compartment_labels(). CalibrationProblem::fix_auto_calculated_parameters and get_parameter_fix_info are removed; applied_parameter_values returns the clamped values the objective scored, which is what results now report.

  • Breaking: transitions are planned by the Rust engine from compartment labels (bin and categories) instead of compartment names, in one planner shared by the simulation and print_equations. The printed equations are therefore the simulated ones: a per-capita rate is shown multiplied by its source (gamma * I), a transition without flows shows (no flows), and the compact form lists the flows of each transition.

  • Breaking: building a model rejects a stratified rate whose category conditions match no source compartment (use to to route into a stratification the source does not carry), a transition with several sources and a per-capita rate, a category transition without exactly one source and one target, and a flow that ends in categories no compartment has. These used to be skipped without notice.
  • Constraint aggregates (a bin or bin prefix in a constraint expression) are built from output labels, so a bin A no longer sums the outputs of a bin A_x.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A transition between bins no longer moves bins whose id starts with the source bin id: A -> B moved AB -> BB as well.
  • Transitions between the categories of a stratification (young -> old) are now simulated; the engine used to ignore them while print_equations showed them.

  • A transition with several sources or targets (A + B -> 2 C) now applies its flow to every source and target, as documented; the engine used to move only the first source to the first target.

  • The applied-parameters report now shows the effective head count for bin, stratification-category, and subgroup rows — the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment_fractions overrides — and reports each fraction as that head count over the declared population_size, so every row shares one denominator with N. An aggregate row written back as overrides no longer reports the stale pre-calibration value as calibrated, and a bin left uncalibrated keeps its null marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

  • A conditional-stratification category is calibrated as a fraction of its conditioning subgroup but reported as a fraction of the whole population, so the report rescales its interval by the subgroup's share of the population; the interval now brackets the reported fraction.
  • apply_calibration_parameters writes initial-condition values back so the model rebuilds the initial population the engine scored for them. Bin and category values update the fractions they declare, as the engine applied them; every compartment those fractions do not reproduce is pinned as a per-compartment override. The call computes the result before it changes the model, so a rejected value leaves the model unchanged.
  • population_size must be greater than zero, reported as a domain ValueError rather than a later ZeroDivisionError. update_bin_fractions re-applies the sum-to-1/conservation rule.
  • Calibrating a bare category name that two stratifications declare no longer builds an initial population larger than population_size: the engine used to split the overlapping pairs of both stratifications from one snapshot.
  • The PyO3 InitialConditions binding exposes population_size, bin_fractions, stratification_fractions and compartment_fractions with getters, and the _commol_rs stub declares only those real attributes (correcting the bin_fractions field name).
  • An initial-condition override that names an unknown compartment raises a ValueError when the model is built or updated, and a RuntimeError from the DifferenceEquations engine constructor.
  • The greedy ensemble search of probabilistic calibration takes its random starts from the shuffled part of the sample (argmin fork). The starts were biased towards low indices, so the same seed can now select a different ensemble.

• Initial release of Commol

  • Simulation runner with multiple output formats

docs.title: Model Structure
docs.text:
Back to API Reference

A Model is a tree of Pydantic models. ModelBuilder creates it, Model.to_json writes it, and the Rust engine reads the same structure from JSON (crates/commol-core/src/types/). Most users never build these types by hand; read this page to understand model files or to work on Commol.

A model has a header that every kind of model has, an engine, and a structure: the part of its kind, tagged in JSON by kind. The only kind is compartmental, which ModelBuilder builds.

Model                      name, description, version, step_unit
├── parameters: [Parameter]                (a value may be a SeriesValue)
├── engine: ModelEngine
│   ├── type: "DifferenceEquations" or "DifferentialEquations"
│   └── settings: OdeSolver | None          (settings of that engine; None: its defaults)
└── structure: CompartmentalStructure      (kind: "compartmental")
    ├── bins: [Bin]
    ├── accumulators: [Accumulator]
    ├── stratifications: [Stratification]
    │   └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
    ├── transitions: [Transition]          (impulse_at, impulse_every for impulses)
    │   └── stratified_rates: [StratifiedRate]
    │       └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
    └── initial_conditions: InitialConditions
        ├── bin_fractions: [BinFraction]
        ├── stratification_fractions: [StratificationFractions]
        │   └── fractions: [StratificationFraction]
        └── compartment_fractions: [CompartmentFraction]

In JSON the structure is an object with its kind and the fields of its class:

{
  "name": "Model",
  "parameters": [],
  "engine": {"type": "DifferenceEquations", "settings": null},
  "structure": {"kind": "compartmental", "bins": [], "...": "..."},
  "step_unit": null
}

Model itself is documented in Model API. The engine must run the kind of the structure: a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine and both kinds.

docs.title: Bin
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Defines a single bin (base category) in the compartmental model.

A bin represents a fundamental category before stratification. The combination of a bin with all stratifications produces the actual compartments.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Identifier of the bin.

name str

A descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.

unit str | None

The unit of measurement for this bin. If None, the bin will use the model-level bin_unit when specified.

Source code in commol/context/bin.py 
class Bin(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a single bin (base category) in the compartmental model.

    A bin represents a fundamental category before stratification. The combination
    of a bin with all stratifications produces the actual compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the bin.
    name : str
        A descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of measurement for this bin.
        If None, the bin will use the model-level bin_unit when specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(..., description="Identifier of the bin.")
    name: str = Field(..., description="Descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.")
    unit: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description="Unit of measurement for this bin.",
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Bin) and self.id == other.id

docs.title: Stratification
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Identifier of the stratification.

categories list[str]

List of the different stratification groups identifiers.

description str | None

A human-readable description of the stratification.

conditions list[StratificationCondition] | None

When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose already-applied stratification categories satisfy ALL conditions. Compartments that do not satisfy the conditions are kept without appending this stratification's categories.

May only reference stratifications declared before this one.

Source code in commol/context/stratification.py 
class Stratification(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        List of the different stratification groups identifiers.
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied stratification categories satisfy ALL conditions.
        Compartments that do not satisfy the conditions are kept without
        appending this stratification's categories.

        May only reference stratifications declared before this one.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the stratification.")
    categories: list[str] = Field(
        default=...,
        description="List of the different stratification groups identifiers.",
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the stratification."
    )
    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Conditions on previously-declared stratifications that must be "
            "satisfied for this stratification to expand a compartment."
        ),
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Stratification) and self.id == other.id

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_length(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not empty.
        """
        if not self.categories:
            raise ValueError(
                (f"Stratification '{self.id}' must have at least one category.")
            )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_uniqueness(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not repeated.
        """
        categories_set = set(self.categories)

        if len(categories_set) != len(self.categories):
            duplicates = [
                item for item in categories_set if self.categories.count(item) > 1
            ]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Categories for stratification '{self.id}' must not be repeated. "
                    f"Found duplicates: {list(set(duplicates))}."
                )
            )

        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_conditions_have_categories(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that stratification expansion conditions filter by category.
        """
        if self.conditions is None:
            return self

        for condition in self.conditions:
            if condition.category is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    (
                        f"Condition for stratification '{self.id}' referencing "
                        f"'{condition.stratification}' must include a category. "
                        "Category-less conditions are only valid for transition "
                        "target overrides."
                    )
                )

        return self

docs.title: StratificationCondition
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Specifies a category within a stratification for rate matching.

When to is set, the matched category in the source compartment is replaced with the to category in the target compartment name. This enables cross-category transitions within the same bin (e.g., aging).

Attributes:

Name Type Description stratification str

The ID of the stratification (e.g., "age", "location")

category str

The category within that stratification (e.g., "young", "urban")

to str | None

Target category override. When set, the target compartment will use this category instead of the source compartment's category for this stratification.

Source code in commol/context/stratification_condition.py 
class StratificationCondition(BaseModel):
    """
    Specifies a category within a stratification for rate matching.

    When ``to`` is set, the matched category in the source compartment is
    replaced with the ``to`` category in the target compartment name. This
    enables cross-category transitions within the same bin (e.g., aging).

    Attributes
    ----------
    stratification : str
        The ID of the stratification (e.g., "age", "location")
    category : str
        The category within that stratification (e.g., "young", "urban")
    to : str | None
        Target category override. When set, the target compartment will use
        this category instead of the source compartment's category for this
        stratification.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    stratification: str = Field(default=..., description="ID of the stratification")
    category: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Category within the stratification. When None, the condition acts as a "
            "target-only override: it does not filter source compartments but still "
            "contributes a 'to' category to the computed target compartment name."
        ),
    )
    to: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Target category override. When set, the target compartment uses "
            "this category instead of the source's for this stratification."
        ),
    )

Bases: BaseModel

Defines a global model parameter.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

The identifier of the parameter.

value float | str | SeriesValue | None

Value of the parameter. Can be: - float: A numerical constant value - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters, special variables (total, total_, step, t, pi, e), or contain mathematical expressions - SeriesValue: An empirical series evaluated via binary search - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use description str | None

A human-readable description of the parameter.

unit str | None

The unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "person"). If None, the parameter has no unit specified.

Source code in commol/context/parameter.py 
class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a global model parameter.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        The identifier of the parameter.
    value : float | str | SeriesValue | None
        Value of the parameter. Can be:
        - float: A numerical constant value
        - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
               special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e), or contain
               mathematical expressions
        - SeriesValue: An empirical series evaluated via binary search
        - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the parameter.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "person").
        If None, the parameter has no unit specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the parameter.")
    value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = Field(
        default=...,
        description=(
            "Value of the parameter. Can be a float (constant), "
            "str (formula), SeriesValue (empirical series), "
            "or None (requires calibration)."
        ),
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the parameter."
    )
    unit: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Unit of the parameter (e.g., '1/day', 'dimensionless', 'person').",
    )

    @field_validator("value")
    @classmethod
    def validate_value(
        cls, value: float | str | SeriesValue | None
    ) -> float | str | SeriesValue | None:
        """Validate the parameter value."""
        if value is None or isinstance(value, SeriesValue):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            return float(value)
        if not value.strip():
            raise ValueError("Formula cannot be empty")
        return value.strip()

    def is_calibrated(self) -> bool:
        """
        Check if the parameter has a value (is calibrated).

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if the parameter has a value, False if it needs calibration.
        """
        return self.value is not None

docs.title: SeriesValue
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

An empirical series for a parameter value.

Attributes:

Name Type Description data list[tuple[float, float]]

(position, value) points on the axis. Need not be pre-sorted; the engine sorts them.

mode str

How the series is read between its points: "pulse" (the value on the step of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only), "step_function" (the value of the last point at or before t), or "linear" (linear interpolation in t). The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferenceEquations model only integer steps.

Source code in commol/context/parameter.py 
class SeriesValue(BaseModel):
    """
    An empirical series for a parameter value.

    Attributes
    ----------
    data : list[tuple[float, float]]
        (position, value) points on the axis. Need not be pre-sorted; the
        engine sorts them.
    mode : str
        How the series is read between its points: ``"pulse"`` (the value on
        the step of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only),
        ``"step_function"`` (the value of the last point at or before ``t``),
        or ``"linear"`` (linear interpolation in ``t``). The engine decides
        which positions its model type accepts: a DifferenceEquations model
        only integer steps.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    data: list[tuple[float, float]]
    mode: str = Field(default="pulse", pattern="^(pulse|step_function|linear)$")

    @field_validator("data")
    @classmethod
    def validate_data(
        cls, value: list[tuple[float, float]]
    ) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
        """Validate series points before they reach the Rust engine."""
        if not value:
            raise ValueError("Series data must contain at least one point")

        positions: list[float] = []
        for position, point_value in value:
            if not (math.isfinite(position) and position >= 0):
                raise ValueError("Series positions must be finite and non-negative")
            if not math.isfinite(point_value):
                raise ValueError("Series values must be finite")
            positions.append(position)

        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
            raise ValueError("Series positions must be unique")

        return value

docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Defines a rule for system evolution.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Id of the transition.

source list[str]

The origin compartments.

target list[str]

The destination compartments.

rate str | None

Default mathematical formula, parameter name, or constant value for the flow. Used when no stratified rate matches. Numeric values are automatically converted to strings during validation.

Operators: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ or ** (power) Functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, min, max, if, etc. Constants: pi, e

Note: Both ^ and ** are supported for exponentiation (** is converted to ^).

Examples: - "beta" (parameter reference) - "0.5" (constant, can also be passed as float 0.5) - "beta * S * I / total" (mathematical formula) - "0.3 * sin(2 * pi * t / 365)" (time-dependent formula) - "2^10" or "2**10" (power: both syntaxes work)

stratified_rates list[StratifiedRate] | None

Stratification-specific rates. Each rate applies to compartments that match all specified stratification conditions.

class Transition(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a rule for system evolution.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Id of the transition.
    source : list[str]
        The origin compartments.
    target : list[str]
        The destination compartments.
    rate : str | None
        Default mathematical formula, parameter name, or constant value for the flow.
        Used when no stratified rate matches. Numeric values are automatically
        converted to strings during validation.

        Operators: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ or ** (power)
        Functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, min, max, if, etc.
        Constants: pi, e

        Note: Both ^ and ** are supported for exponentiation (** is converted to ^).

        Examples:
        - "beta" (parameter reference)
        - "0.5" (constant, can also be passed as float 0.5)
        - "beta * S * I / total" (mathematical formula)
        - "0.3 * sin(2 * pi * t / 365)" (time-dependent formula)
        - "2^10" or "2**10" (power: both syntaxes work)
    stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None
        Stratification-specific rates. Each rate applies to compartments that match
        all specified stratification conditions.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Id of the transition.")
    source: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Origin compartments.")
    target: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Destination compartments.")
    accumulators: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Cumulative event counters incremented by this transition flow.",
    )

    rate: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description=(
            "Default rate expression (fallback when no stratified rate matches). "
            "Can be a parameter reference (e.g., 'beta'), a constant (e.g., '0.5'), "
            "or a mathematical expression (e.g., 'beta * S * I / total'). "
            "Numeric values are automatically converted to strings during validation."
        ),
    )

    stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None = Field(
        default=None, description="List of stratification-specific rates"
    )

    per_compartment: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "When True, base compartment names in the rate expression "
            "are replaced with the specific stratified compartment name "
            "for each expanded transition flow."
        ),
    )

    impulse_at: list[float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Positions on the axis where the transition is an impulse: at each "
            "one, the rate is a fraction (per-capita) or an amount (absolute) "
            "moved at once. Between them the transition moves nothing."
        ),
    )

    impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "(period, offset): the transition is an impulse at offset, "
            "offset + period, offset + 2 * period, ..."
        ),
    )

    @property
    def is_impulse(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the transition is an impulse rather than a continuous flow."""
        return self.impulse_at is not None or self.impulse_every is not None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_impulse(self) -> Self:
        """Check the impulse schedule: one kind, valid positions and period."""
        if self.impulse_at is not None and self.impulse_every is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Transition '{self.id}': set impulse_at or impulse_every, not both."
            )
        if self.impulse_at is not None:
            if not self.impulse_at:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': impulse_at needs at least one position."
                )
            bad = [p for p in self.impulse_at if not math.isfinite(p) or p < 0]
            if bad:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': impulse positions must be finite "
                    f"and not negative, got {bad}."
                )
        if self.impulse_every is not None:
            period, offset = self.impulse_every
            if not (math.isfinite(period) and period > 0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': the impulse period must be "
                    f"positive, got {period}."
                )
            if not (math.isfinite(offset) and offset >= 0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': the impulse offset must be finite "
                    f"and not negative, got {offset}."
                )
        return self

    @field_validator("rate", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def validate_rate(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """
        Convert numeric rates to strings and perform security and syntax validation.
        """
        if value is None:
            return value
        try:
            validate_expression_security(value)
            commol_rs.core.MathExpression(value).validate()
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"Validation failed for rate '{value}': {e}")
        return value

class StratifiedRate(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a rate for specific stratification categories.

    Attributes
    ----------
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition]
        List of stratification-category pairs that must match
    rate : str
        Rate expression for compartments matching these conditions
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] = Field(
        default=..., description="Stratification conditions that must match"
    )
    rate: str = Field(
        default=..., description="Rate expression for matching compartments"
    )
    absolute: bool | None = Field(

            "When True, the flow is treated as absolute (not multiplied by the "
            "source amount). When None, inferred from whether the rate references "
            "any compartment variable."

    @field_validator("conditions")
    @classmethod
    def validate_not_empty(
        cls, v: list[StratificationCondition]
    ) -> list[StratificationCondition]:
        """Ensure at least one stratification condition is specified."""
        if not v:
            raise ValueError(
                "conditions must contain at least one stratification condition"
            )
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_unique_stratifications(self) -> Self:
        """Ensure no duplicate stratification IDs."""
        strat_ids = [sc.stratification for sc in self.conditions]
        if len(strat_ids) != len(set(strat_ids)):
            duplicates = [s for s in strat_ids if strat_ids.count(s) > 1]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Duplicate stratifications found: {list(set(duplicates))}. "
                    f"Each stratification can only be specified once per rate."
                )
            )
        return self

    @field_validator("rate", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def validate_rate(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Perform security and syntax validation on the rate expression."""
        try:
            validate_expression_security(value)
            commol_rs.core.MathExpression(value).validate()
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"Validation failed for rate '{value}': {e}")
        return value

class InitialConditions(BaseModel):
    """
    Initial conditions for a simulation.

    Attributes
    ----------
    total : float
        The sum of every compartment at the start, finite and greater than 0.
        It can be a count, a mass or a concentration.
    bin_fractions : list[BinFraction]
        List of bin fractions. Each item contains a bin id and
        its initial fractional size. Fractions can be None if they need calibration.
    stratification_fractions : list[StratificationFractions], optional
        List of stratification fractions. Each item contains a stratification id and
        its category fractions.
    compartment_fractions : list[CompartmentFraction], optional
        List of per-compartment overrides applied after the uniform expansion. Each
        item contains an expanded compartment name and the fraction of the total
        it holds.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    total: float = Field(
        ...,
        description="The sum of every compartment at the start, finite and > 0.",
    )
    bin_fractions: list[BinFraction] = Field(
        default=...,
        description=(
            "List of bin fractions. Each item contains a bin id and its initial "
            "fractional size. Fractions can be None if they need calibration."
        ),
    )
    stratification_fractions: list[StratificationFractions] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "List of stratification fractions. Each item contains a stratification id "
            "and its category fractions."
        ),
    )
    compartment_fractions: list[CompartmentFraction] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "List of per-compartment overrides applied after the uniform expansion. "
            "Each item contains an expanded compartment name and the fraction of the "
            "total it holds."
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("total")
    @classmethod
    def validate_total(cls, value: float) -> float:
        """Enforce a finite total greater than 0.

        Every fraction of a zero total is zero, and the report divides by the
        total, so a zero, negative or non-finite total is rejected as a domain
        error.
        """
        if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"total must be finite and greater than 0, got {value}.")
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_compartment_fractions_unique(self) -> Self:
        """Validate that each compartment appears at most once."""
        seen: set[str] = set()
        duplicates: set[str] = set()
        for compartment_fraction in self.compartment_fractions:
            name = compartment_fraction.compartment
            if name in seen:
                duplicates.add(name)
            seen.add(name)
        if duplicates:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Duplicate compartment fractions found: {sorted(duplicates)}."
            )
        return self

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_bin_fraction_total(candidate: Mapping[str, float | None]) -> None:
        """
        Enforce the bin-fraction conservation rule on a complete mapping.

        Uncalibrated (``None``) fractions floor the calibrated total strictly
        below 1.0 so they can be filled later. When every bin is calibrated,
        the fractions must sum to 1.0, because they are shares of a single
        total. Construction and updates apply the same rule, so an update
        never produces a definition that cannot be loaded again.

        Parameters
        ----------
        candidate : Mapping[str, float | None]
            Fraction of every bin.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the fractions break the rule.
        """
        calibrated = [value for value in candidate.values() if value is not None]
        if not calibrated:
            return
        total = sum(calibrated)
        uncalibrated = sum(1 for value in candidate.values() if value is None)

        if uncalibrated > 0:
            if total >= 1.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Calibrated bin fractions sum to {total:.4f}, but must be "
                    f"LESS than 1.0 to leave room for {uncalibrated} "
                    f"uncalibrated fraction(s). Calibrated fractions: "
                    f"{[item for item in candidate.items() if item[1] is not None]}"
                )
        elif not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-4):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Bin fractions must sum to 1.0, got {total:.4f}. "
                f"Fractions: {list(candidate.values())}"
            )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_calibrated_fractions_sum_to_one(self) -> Self:
        """
        Validate that bin fractions sum appropriately.

        Rules:
        - If some fractions are None (uncalibrated): calibrated ones must sum to LESS
            than 1.0
        - If all fractions are calibrated (no None): must sum to exactly 1.0
        - If all fractions are None: skip validation (will be set before simulation)
        """
        self._validate_bin_fraction_total(
            {bf.bin: bf.fraction for bf in self.bin_fractions}
        )
        return self

    def get_uncalibrated_bins(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Get list of bin IDs that have uncalibrated fractions (value = None).

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            List of bin IDs with uncalibrated initial conditions.
        """
        return [bf.bin for bf in self.bin_fractions if bf.fraction is None]

    def get_categories_with_fractions(self) -> set[str]:
        """
        Get the categories that have a declared initial fraction.

        Returns
        -------
        set[str]
            Category names collected from ``stratification_fractions``. A
            category declared on a stratification but absent from the initial
            conditions is not included.
        """
        return {
            fraction.category
            for stratification in self.stratification_fractions
            for fraction in stratification.fractions
        }

    def resolve_category(self, category: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve a category id to its stratification and its bare name.

        A qualified id (``sex:female``) names the stratification. A bare name
        must be declared by exactly one stratification.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A bare or qualified category id.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[str, str]
            The stratification id and the bare category name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        owner, name = self._owning_stratification(category)
        return owner.stratification, name

    def category_id(self, stratification: str, category: str) -> str:
        """
        Shortest id that names a category without ambiguity.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stratification : str
            Id of the stratification that declares the category.
        category : str
            Bare category name.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The bare name, or ``stratification:category`` when another
            stratification declares a category of the same name.
        """
        declaring = sum(
            any(fraction.category == category for fraction in item.fractions)
            for item in self.stratification_fractions
        )
        if declaring > 1:
            return f"{stratification}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{category}"
        return category

    def get_category_fraction(self, category: str) -> float:
        """
        Get the fraction of a category within the group it subdivides.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A category id, bare or qualified (``sex:female``).

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The declared fraction, relative to the group the category's
            stratification applies to rather than to the whole model.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        owner, name = self._owning_stratification(category)
        return next(
            fraction.fraction
            for fraction in owner.fractions
            if fraction.category == name
        )

    def subgroup_total(self, categories: Iterable[str] = ()) -> float:
        """
        Get the initial total of a subgroup.

        Category fractions are relative to the group their stratification
        applies to, so the fractions of a nested chain of categories multiply.
        Passing no categories gives the total.

        Parameters
        ----------
        categories : Iterable[str], optional
            Category ids, bare or qualified, forming a chain from the whole
            model down to the subgroup, outermost first.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The sum of the compartments of the subgroup at step 0.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        total = self.total
        for category in categories:
            total *= self.get_category_fraction(category)
        return total

    def _owning_stratification(
        self, category: str
    ) -> tuple[StratificationFractions, str]:
        """
        Return the stratification that declares a category, and its bare name.

        A qualified id (``sex:female``) names the stratification. A bare name
        must be declared by exactly one stratification.
        """
        stratification_id, separator, name = category.rpartition(CATEGORY_SEPARATOR)
        owners = [
            stratification
            for stratification in self.stratification_fractions
            if (not separator or stratification.stratification == stratification_id)
            and any(fraction.category == name for fraction in stratification.fractions)
        ]
        if len(owners) > 1:
            qualified = " or ".join(
                f"'{owner.stratification}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{name}'"
                for owner in owners
            )
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' is ambiguous: it is declared by "
                f"stratifications {[owner.stratification for owner in owners]}. "
                f"Qualify it as {qualified}."
            )
        if not owners:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available categories: {sorted(self.get_categories_with_fractions())}"
            )
        return owners[0], name

    def _apply_stratification_update(
        self,
        stratification: StratificationFractions,
        named: Mapping[str, float],
    ) -> None:
        """Write the fractions of a single stratification."""
        unnamed = [
            fraction.category
            for fraction in stratification.fractions
            if fraction.category not in named
        ]
        total = sum(named.values())

        if len(unnamed) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot update stratification '{stratification.stratification}': "
                f"categories {sorted(unnamed)} were left unnamed. At most one "
                f"category may be omitted, so that it can take the remaining "
                f"fraction."
            )
        if not unnamed and not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-6):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fractions for stratification '{stratification.stratification}' "
                f"must sum to 1.0, got {total:.6f}. Values: {dict(named)}"
            )
        if unnamed and total > 1.0 + 1e-6:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fractions for stratification '{stratification.stratification}' "
                f"sum to {total:.6f}, which would leave a negative fraction for "
                f"'{unnamed[0]}'. Values: {dict(named)}"
            )

        remainder = max(0.0, 1.0 - total)
        for fraction in stratification.fractions:
            fraction.fraction = named.get(fraction.category, remainder)

    def update_stratification_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Update stratification category fractions by category name.

        Categories belonging to several stratifications may be given in one
        call. A category name declared by more than one stratification must be
        qualified with its stratification, as in ``sex:female``. Within each
        stratification, at most one category may be omitted; the omitted
        category receives the remaining fraction so that the stratification
        sums to 1.0. When every category is given, the values
        must already sum to 1.0.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping category names, bare or qualified, to their new
            fraction values. Each value must lie between 0.0 and 1.0.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category is not found or is ambiguous, a value lies outside
            [0.0, 1.0], a stratification has more than one category omitted, fully
            specified
            values do not sum to 1.0, or the given values exceed 1.0.
        """
        for category, value in fractions.items():
            if not 0.0 <= value <= 1.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Fraction for category '{category}' must be between 0.0 and "
                    f"1.0, got {value}."
                )

        by_stratification: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        for category, value in fractions.items():
            owner, name = self._owning_stratification(category)
            by_stratification.setdefault(owner.stratification, {})[name] = value

        for stratification in self.stratification_fractions:
            named = by_stratification.get(stratification.stratification)
            if named is not None:
                self._apply_stratification_update(stratification, named)

    def update_compartment_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Upsert per-compartment overrides by expanded compartment name.

        A compartment already present in ``compartment_fractions`` has its
        fraction replaced; a new one is appended. Compartment names and the
        sum of the amounts depend on the model expansion, so they are validated
        by :meth:`~commol.context.model.Model.update_compartment_fractions`
        against the engine, not here.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping expanded compartment names to their new
            fraction of the total. Each value must lie between
            0.0 and 1.0.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a value lies outside ``[0.0, 1.0]``.
        """
        updated = {
            compartment: CompartmentFraction(compartment=compartment, fraction=value)
            for compartment, value in fractions.items()
        }
        existing = {override.compartment for override in self.compartment_fractions}
        self.compartment_fractions = [
            updated.get(override.compartment, override)
            for override in self.compartment_fractions
        ] + [
            override
            for compartment, override in updated.items()
            if compartment not in existing
        ]

    def update_bin_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float | None]) -> None:
        """
        Update bin fractions by bin ID.

        The candidate fractions are validated before any bin is mutated, so a
        rejected call leaves the initial conditions unchanged. The conservation
        rule of :meth:`validate_calibrated_fractions_sum_to_one` is re-applied
        to the resulting mapping: the bin fractions must sum to 1.0, while
        uncalibrated (``None``) bins reserve the remainder. To move an amount
        between bins, update every bin involved in one call.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float | None]
            Dictionary mapping bin IDs to their new fraction values.
            None values indicate bins that need calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a bin ID is not found in the initial conditions, or the
            resulting fractions violate the conservation rule.
        """
        known = {bf.bin for bf in self.bin_fractions}
        unknown = sorted(set(fractions) - known)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Bin(s) {unknown} not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available bins: {[bf.bin for bf in self.bin_fractions]}"
            )

        candidate = {bf.bin: bf.fraction for bf in self.bin_fractions}
        candidate.update(fractions)
        self._validate_bin_fraction_total(candidate)

        for bin_id, fraction in fractions.items():
            for bf in self.bin_fractions:
                if bf.bin == bin_id:
                    bf.fraction = fraction
                    break

def category_id(self, stratification: str, category: str) -> str:
    """
    Shortest id that names a category without ambiguity.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stratification : str
        Id of the stratification that declares the category.
    category : str
        Bare category name.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The bare name, or ``stratification:category`` when another
        stratification declares a category of the same name.
    """
    declaring = sum(
        any(fraction.category == category for fraction in item.fractions)
        for item in self.stratification_fractions
    )
    if declaring > 1:
        return f"{stratification}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{category}"
    return category

def get_category_fraction(self, category: str) -> float:
    """
    Get the fraction of a category within the group it subdivides.

    Parameters
    ----------
    category : str

    Returns

        The declared fraction, relative to the group the category's
        stratification applies to rather than to the whole model.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
    """
    owner, name = self._owning_stratification(category)
    return next(
        fraction.fraction
        for fraction in owner.fractions
        if fraction.category == name

def subgroup_total(self, categories: Iterable[str] = ()) -> float:
    """
    Get the initial total of a subgroup.

    Category fractions are relative to the group their stratification
    applies to, so the fractions of a nested chain of categories multiply.
    Passing no categories gives the total.

    Parameters
    ----------
    categories : Iterable[str], optional
        Category ids, bare or qualified, forming a chain from the whole
        model down to the subgroup, outermost first.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The sum of the compartments of the subgroup at step 0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
    """
    total = self.total
    for category in categories:
        total *= self.get_category_fraction(category)
    return total

def update_stratification_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
    """
    Update stratification category fractions by category name.

    Categories belonging to several stratifications may be given in one
    call. A category name declared by more than one stratification must be
    qualified with its stratification, as in ``sex:female``. Within each
    stratification, at most one category may be omitted; the omitted
    category receives the remaining fraction so that the stratification
    sums to 1.0. When every category is given, the values
    must already sum to 1.0.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fractions : Mapping[str, float]
        Dictionary mapping category names, bare or qualified, to their new
        fraction values. Each value must lie between 0.0 and 1.0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a category is not found or is ambiguous, a value lies outside
        [0.0, 1.0], a stratification has more than one category omitted, fully
        specified
        values do not sum to 1.0, or the given values exceed 1.0.
    """
    for category, value in fractions.items():
        if not 0.0 <= value <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fraction for category '{category}' must be between 0.0 and "
                f"1.0, got {value}."
            )

    by_stratification: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    for category, value in fractions.items():
        owner, name = self._owning_stratification(category)
        by_stratification.setdefault(owner.stratification, {})[name] = value

    for stratification in self.stratification_fractions:
        named = by_stratification.get(stratification.stratification)
        if named is not None:
            self._apply_stratification_update(stratification, named)

def update_compartment_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
    """
    Upsert per-compartment overrides by expanded compartment name.

    A compartment already present in ``compartment_fractions`` has its
    fraction replaced; a new one is appended. Compartment names and the
    sum of the amounts depend on the model expansion, so they are validated
    by :meth:`~commol.context.model.Model.update_compartment_fractions`
    against the engine, not here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fractions : Mapping[str, float]
        Dictionary mapping expanded compartment names to their new
        fraction of the total. Each value must lie between
        0.0 and 1.0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a value lies outside ``[0.0, 1.0]``.
    """
    updated = {
        compartment: CompartmentFraction(compartment=compartment, fraction=value)
        for compartment, value in fractions.items()
    }
    existing = {override.compartment for override in self.compartment_fractions}
    self.compartment_fractions = [
        updated.get(override.compartment, override)
        for override in self.compartment_fractions
    ] + [
        override
        for compartment, override in updated.items()
        if compartment not in existing
    ]

The conservation rule of :meth:validate_calibrated_fractions_sum_to_one is re-applied to the resulting mapping: the bin fractions must sum to 1.0, while uncalibrated (None) bins reserve the remainder. To move an amount between bins, update every bin involved in one call.

def update_bin_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float | None]) -> None:
    """
    Update bin fractions by bin ID.

    The candidate fractions are validated before any bin is mutated, so a
    rejected call leaves the initial conditions unchanged. The conservation
    rule of :meth:`validate_calibrated_fractions_sum_to_one` is re-applied
    to the resulting mapping: the bin fractions must sum to 1.0, while
    uncalibrated (``None``) bins reserve the remainder. To move an amount
    between bins, update every bin involved in one call.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fractions : Mapping[str, float | None]
        Dictionary mapping bin IDs to their new fraction values.
        None values indicate bins that need calibration.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a bin ID is not found in the initial conditions, or the
        resulting fractions violate the conservation rule.
    """
    known = {bf.bin for bf in self.bin_fractions}
    unknown = sorted(set(fractions) - known)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Bin(s) {unknown} not found in initial conditions. "
            f"Available bins: {[bf.bin for bf in self.bin_fractions]}"
        )

    candidate = {bf.bin: bf.fraction for bf in self.bin_fractions}
    candidate.update(fractions)
    self._validate_bin_fraction_total(candidate)

    for bin_id, fraction in fractions.items():
        for bf in self.bin_fractions:
            if bf.bin == bin_id:
                bf.fraction = fraction
                break

Bases: BaseModel

A time-varying expression usable as (or within) a transition rate.

Instances are created exclusively via the factory classmethods (pulse, periodic, window, etc.). Each instance may carry stratification conditions that restrict it to a specific sub-group via for_group.

Multi-group schedules are built by calling AxisPattern.add_group(...) directly on the class. The first call returns a new schedule; chain further add_group and set_default calls on the returned instance.

A AxisPattern is accepted directly by :meth:commol.api.model_builder.ModelBuilder.add_transition via the rate argument; no auxiliary conversion is required.

Examples:

>>> from commol import AxisPattern
>>> # Single pattern
>>> rate = AxisPattern.pulse(at=10, value=0.05)
>>> str(rate)
'(if(step == 10, 0.05, 0))'
>>> # Multi-group schedule
>>> rate = AxisPattern.add_group(
...     conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "cat1"}],
...     schedule=AxisPattern.pulse(at=10, value=0.05),
... ).add_group(
...     conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "cat2"}],
...     schedule=AxisPattern.pulse(at=10, value=0.02),
... )
