class ModelStructure(BaseModel, ABC):
    """
    The part of a model that depends on its kind.

    Each kind subclasses it and sets ``kind`` to a ``Literal`` default, its
    name in the engine's list of kinds. A subclass that does not implement an
    abstract method cannot be made: the error names the method.

    Attributes
    ----------
    kind : str
        Name of the model kind, the tag of the structure in JSON.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    kind: str

    _kinds: ClassVar[dict[str, type["ModelStructure"]]] = {}

    @classmethod
    def __pydantic_init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs: object) -> None:
        """Register a concrete subclass under its ``kind``."""
        super().__pydantic_init_subclass__(**kwargs)
        kind = cls.model_fields["kind"].default
        if inspect.isabstract(cls) or not isinstance(kind, str):
            return
        known = ModelStructure._kinds.get(kind)
        if known is not None and known.__qualname__ != cls.__qualname__:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Model kind '{kind}' is already the kind of {known.__qualname__}"
            )
        ModelStructure._kinds[kind] = cls

    @classmethod
    def of_kind(cls, kind: str) -> type["ModelStructure"]:
        """
        The structure class of a model kind.

        Parameters
        ----------
        kind : str
            Name of the kind, such as ``"compartmental"``.

        Returns
        -------
        type[ModelStructure]
            The subclass registered for it.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If no structure class has that kind.
        """
        structure = cls._kinds.get(kind)
        if structure is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown model kind '{kind}'. Known kinds: {sorted(cls._kinds)}"
            )
        return structure

    @abstractmethod
    def check_model(self, model: "Model[Self]") -> None:
        """
        Check the structure against the rest of its model.

        The model calls it when it is made, so a model that cannot be run as
        written is rejected then.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model that holds this structure.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the structure does not agree with the parameters or the engine.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def outputs_by_source(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        The output names of the model, grouped by the id they come from.

        Reports and plots name a group of outputs by this id and sum them.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Each id mapped to its output names, in engine order.
        """

    def series_label(self, series_id: str) -> SeriesLabel:
        """
        How a plot names a series and its unit.

        Parameters
        ----------
        series_id : str
            An output name or an id of `outputs_by_source`.

        Returns
        -------
        SeriesLabel
            The id itself and no unit, unless the kind knows better.
        """
        return SeriesLabel(series_id, None)

    def calibration_value_types(self) -> frozenset[CalibrationParameterType]:
        """
        Types of value of this kind that calibration may set.

        ``parameter`` and ``factor`` are not here: every kind accepts them.
        The engine's list of kinds declares the others.

        Returns
        -------
        frozenset[CalibrationParameterType]
            For example ``{"initial_condition"}`` for a compartmental model.
        """
        return frozenset(
            CalibrationParameterType(name)
            for name in commol_rs.engine.ModelKind(self.kind).value_types()
        )

    def uncalibrated_values(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Ids of the values of this kind that need calibration before a run.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Empty unless the kind has values left unset.
        """
        return []

    def with_calibrated_values(
        self,
        model: "Model[Self]",  # noqa: ARG002
        problem: "CalibrationProblem",  # noqa: ARG002
        values: Mapping[str, float],  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> Self:
        """
        The structure with the calibrated values of its kind written back.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model the problem was built on. It is not changed.
        problem : CalibrationProblem
            The problem, for the types of its parameters.
        values : Mapping[str, float]
            Calibrated value per parameter id.

        Returns
        -------
        Self
            A structure; this one when the kind sets no values of its own.
        """
        return self

    def report_sections(
        self,
        model: "Model[Self]",  # noqa: ARG002
        calibrated_ids: set[str],  # noqa: ARG002
        parameter_statistics: "Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None",  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> ReportSections:
        """
        Sections of this kind in a report of applied values.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model that holds the applied values.
        calibrated_ids : set[str]
            Ids that calibration set.
        parameter_statistics : Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None
            Ensemble spread per id, or None without an ensemble.

        Returns
        -------
        ReportSections
            Each section by its key in the report; none by default.
        """
        return {}

    def print_equations(
        self, model: "Model[Self]", output_file: str | None, format: str
    ) -> None:
        """
        Print the equations of the model.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            If the kind has no equations to print.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(f"A {self.kind} model has no equations to print")

    def check_unit_consistency(self, model: "Model[Self]", verbose: bool) -> None:
        """
        Check the units of the model.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            If the kind has no unit check.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(f"A {self.kind} model has no unit check")

    Attributes
    ----------
    kind : Literal["compartmental"]
        The model kind.
    bins : list[Bin]
        The states of the model. Stratifications expand each one into
        compartments.
    accumulators : list[Accumulator]
        Counters of the flow of the transitions that name them.
    stratifications : list[Stratification]
        Categorical subdivisions of the bins, in expansion order.
    transitions : list[Transition]
        Flows between bins, or between the categories of one stratification.
    initial_conditions : InitialConditions
        The total and the fractions the compartments start with.
    """

    kind: Literal["compartmental"] = "compartmental"

    bins: list[Bin]
    accumulators: list[Accumulator] = Field(default_factory=list)
    stratifications: list[Stratification]
    transitions: list[Transition]
    initial_conditions: InitialConditions

    @field_validator("bins")
    @classmethod
    def validate_bins_not_empty(cls, v: list[Bin]) -> list[Bin]:
        """Require at least one bin."""
        if not v:
            raise ValueError("At least one bin must be defined.")
        return v

    @field_validator("transitions")
    @classmethod
    def validate_transitions_not_empty(cls, v: list[Transition]) -> list[Transition]:
        """Require at least one transition."""
        if not v:
            raise ValueError("At least one transition must be defined.")
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_unique_ids(self) -> Self:
        """Validate that bin, stratification and transition ids are unique."""
        for label, ids in (
            ("bin", [item.id for item in self.bins]),
            ("stratification", [item.id for item in self.stratifications]),
            ("transition", [item.id for item in self.transitions]),
        ):
            if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
                duplicates = [item for item in set(ids) if ids.count(item) > 1]
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate {label} IDs found: {duplicates}")
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_bin_initial_conditions(self) -> Self:
        """Validate the bin fractions against the bins."""
        bin_fractions = {
            bf.bin: bf.fraction for bf in self.initial_conditions.bin_fractions
        }
        actual_bins = set(bin_fractions)
        expected_bins = {bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins}
        if actual_bins != expected_bins:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Initial bin fractions keys must exactly match bin ids. "
                f"Missing ids: {expected_bins - actual_bins}, "
                f"Extra ids: {actual_bins - expected_bins}."
            )

        # The sum is checked once every fraction has a value; InitialConditions
        # checks the uncalibrated case.
        calibrated = [f for f in bin_fractions.values() if f is not None]
        if len(calibrated) == len(bin_fractions):
            total = sum(calibrated)
            if not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-6):
                raise ValueError(f"Bin fractions must sum to 1.0, but got {total:.7f}.")
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_stratified_rates(self) -> Self:
        """Validate that stratified rates name stratifications and categories."""
        strat_map = {strat.id: strat for strat in self.stratifications}

        for transition in self.transitions:
            for idx, stratified_rate in enumerate(transition.stratified_rates or []):
                for condition in stratified_rate.conditions:
                    if condition.stratification not in strat_map:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"In transition '{transition.id}', stratified rate "
                            f"{idx}: Stratification "
                            f"'{condition.stratification}' not found. "
                            f"Available: {list(strat_map.keys())}"
                        )

                    # A condition without a category only redirects the target.
                    strat = strat_map[condition.stratification]
                    if (
                        condition.category is not None
                        and condition.category not in strat.categories
                    ):
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"In transition '{transition.id}', stratified rate "
                            f"{idx}: Category '{condition.category}' not found "
                            f"in stratification '{condition.stratification}'. "
                            f"Available: {strat.categories}"
                        )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_stratification_initial_conditions(self) -> Self:
        """Validate the stratification fractions against the stratifications."""
        strat_map = {strat.id: strat for strat in self.stratifications}
        actual_strat = {
            sf.stratification for sf in self.initial_conditions.stratification_fractions
        }
        expected_strat = set(strat_map)
        if actual_strat != expected_strat:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Initial stratification fractions keys must exactly match "
                f"stratification ids. Missing ids: {expected_strat - actual_strat}, "
                f"Extra ids: {actual_strat - expected_strat}."
            )

        for strat_fractions in self.initial_conditions.stratification_fractions:
            strat_id = strat_fractions.stratification
            strat_instance = strat_map[strat_id]
            fractions = {sf.category: sf.fraction for sf in strat_fractions.fractions}

            expected = set(strat_instance.categories)
            actual = set(fractions)
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Categories for stratification '{strat_id}' must exactly "
                    f"match defined categories in instance '{strat_instance.id}'. "
                    f"Missing categories: {expected - actual}, "
                    f"Extra categories: {actual - expected}."
                )

            total = sum(fractions.values())
            if not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-6):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Stratification fractions for '{strat_id}' must sum to 1.0, "
                    f"but got {total:.7}."
                )
        return self

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The interface of a model kind
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def check_model(self, model: "Model[Self]") -> None:
        """
        Check the structure against the parameters of its model.

        Parameter ids must not be engine variables or bin ids, every variable
        of a rate must be defined, transitions must move between bins or
        between the categories of one stratification, and the engine must
        plan every transition and build the initial state.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model that holds this structure.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If one of these checks fails.
        """
        self._check_parameter_names(model)
        engine_state.transition_flows(self)
        engine_state.check_names(model)
        if self.initial_conditions.compartment_fractions:
            engine_state.initial_state(self)
        self._check_formula_variables(model)
        self._check_transition_ids()

    def outputs_by_source(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        Map each bin and accumulator id to the output names it expands into.

        A bin or accumulator produces one output per combination of the
        stratification categories that apply to it. Without stratifications it
        produces a single output named after the id itself.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Bin and accumulator ids, each mapped to its output names in
            declaration order.
        """
        outputs: dict[str, list[str]] = {
            source_id: []
            for source_id in (
                *(bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins),
                *(accumulator.id for accumulator in self.accumulators),
            )
        }
        compartments, accumulators = engine_state.expanded_outputs(self)
        for output in (*compartments, *accumulators):
            outputs[output.source].append(output.name)
        return outputs

    def series_label(self, series_id: str) -> SeriesLabel:
        """
        The name and unit of a bin, for a plot of its series.

        Parameters
        ----------
        series_id : str
            A bin id, or any other series id.

        Returns
        -------
        SeriesLabel
            The bin's name and unit, or the id and no unit when no bin has it.
        """
        bin_item = next((b for b in self.bins if b.id == series_id), None)
        if bin_item is None:
            return SeriesLabel(series_id, None)
        return SeriesLabel(bin_item.name or series_id, bin_item.unit)

    def uncalibrated_values(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Ids of the bins whose initial fraction needs calibration.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Bin ids with a None fraction.
        """
        return self.initial_conditions.get_uncalibrated_bins()

    def with_calibrated_values(
        self,
        model: "Model[Self]",
        problem: "CalibrationProblem",
        values: Mapping[str, float],
    ) -> Self:
        """
        The structure with calibrated initial conditions written back.

        The written structure rebuilds the initial state the engine
        scored. Bin and category values update the fractions they declare.
        Every compartment those fractions do not reproduce, such as an exact
        compartment value or a value that overlaps a per-compartment override,
        is written as a per-compartment override.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model the problem was built on. It is not changed.
        problem : CalibrationProblem
            The problem, for its parameters and remainder.
        values : Mapping[str, float]
            Calibrated value per parameter id.

        Returns
        -------
        CompartmentalStructure
            A copy that holds the calibrated initial conditions.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the engine cannot resolve an initial-condition id or the
            remainder, or the initial amounts exceed the total.
        """
        from commol.context._model.calibration_write_back import (
            calibrated_initial_conditions,
        )

        initial_conditions = calibrated_initial_conditions(model, problem, values)
        return self.model_copy(update={"initial_conditions": initial_conditions})

    def report_sections(
        self,
        model: "Model[Self]",  # noqa: ARG002
        calibrated_ids: set[str],
        parameter_statistics: "Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None",
    ) -> ReportSections:
        """
        The ``initial_conditions`` section of a report of applied values.

        See :func:`commol.applied_parameters_report`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model that holds the applied values.
        calibrated_ids : set[str]
            Ids that calibration set.
        parameter_statistics : Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None
            Ensemble spread per id, or None without an ensemble.

        Returns
        -------
        ReportSections
            ``{"initial_conditions": ...}``.
        """
        from commol.context._model.report import initial_conditions_report

        return {
            "initial_conditions": initial_conditions_report(
                self, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
            )
        }

    def print_equations(
        self, model: "Model[Self]", output_file: str | None, format: str
    ) -> None:
        """Print the equations of the model; see `Model.print_equations`."""
        from commol.context._model.equations import EquationPrinter

        EquationPrinter(model).print_equations(output_file, format)

    def check_unit_consistency(self, model: "Model[Self]", verbose: bool) -> None:
        """Check the units of the model; see `Model.check_unit_consistency`."""
        from commol.context._model.units import UnitChecker

        UnitChecker(model).check_unit_consistency(verbose)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Initial conditions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def update_initial_conditions(
        self, bin_fractions: Mapping[str, float | None]
    ) -> None:
        """
        Update initial condition fractions for specified bins.

        Parameters
        ----------
        bin_fractions : Mapping[str, float | None]
            Dictionary mapping bin IDs to their new fraction values.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a bin ID in the dictionary doesn't exist in the model.
        """
        self.initial_conditions.update_bin_fractions(bin_fractions)

    def update_stratification_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Update initial stratification fractions for specified categories.

        Within each stratification, at most one category may be omitted; the
        omitted category receives the remaining fraction.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping category names to their new fraction values.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category doesn't exist in the model, a value lies outside
            [0.0, 1.0], a stratification has more than one category omitted, or
            the resulting fractions do not sum to 1.0.
        """
        self.initial_conditions.update_stratification_fractions(fractions)

    def update_compartment_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Upsert per-compartment initial condition overrides.

        A compartment already declared has its fraction replaced; a new one is
        appended. The engine validates the result before it is stored, so a
        rejected call leaves the structure unchanged.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping expanded compartment names to their new fraction
            of the total.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a name is not an expanded compartment of the model, a value lies
            outside ``[0.0, 1.0]``, or the resulting overrides make the initial
            amounts exceed the total.
        """
        candidate = self.initial_conditions.model_copy(deep=True)
        candidate.update_compartment_fractions(fractions)
        engine_state.initial_state(
            self.model_copy(update={"initial_conditions": candidate})
        )
        self.initial_conditions = candidate

    def initial_state(self) -> list[InitialCompartment]:
        """
        Expanded compartments and the amount each one starts with.

        The engine builds this state from the bin fractions, the stratification
        fractions and the per-compartment overrides; it is the state a
        simulation starts from.

        Returns
        -------
        list[InitialCompartment]
            One entry per expanded compartment, in engine order.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the per-compartment overrides are not valid for the structure.
        """
        return engine_state.initial_state(self)

    def get_conditioning_categories(self, stratification_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """
        Get the categories a stratification is conditioned on.

        An unconditional stratification subdivides the whole model and has
        no conditioning categories. A conditional one subdivides only the
        subgroup its conditions select, and its fractions are relative to that
        subgroup rather than to the whole model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stratification_id : str
            Id of a stratification of the model.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[str, ...]
            Ids of the categories selecting the subgroup this stratification
            subdivides, empty for an unconditional stratification. A category
            name another stratification also declares is qualified, as in
            ``sex:female``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the stratification is not found.
        """
        for stratification in self.stratifications:
            if stratification.id == stratification_id:
                return tuple(
                    self.initial_conditions.category_id(
                        condition.stratification, condition.category
                    )
                    for condition in (stratification.conditions or [])
                    if condition.category is not None
                )
        raise ValueError(
            f"Stratification '{stratification_id}' not found. Available: "
            f"{sorted(s.id for s in self.stratifications)}"
        )

    def subgroup_total(self, categories: Iterable[str] = ()) -> float:
        """
        Get the initial total of a subgroup.

        See
        :meth:`~commol.context.initial_conditions.InitialConditions.subgroup_total`.

        Per-compartment overrides are folded into the sum for every compartment
        the category chain selects, so the result matches the state the engine
        builds. Without overrides the declared fractions are multiplied.

        Parameters
        ----------
        categories : Iterable[str], optional
            Category ids, bare or qualified (``sex:female``), forming a chain
            from the whole model down to the subgroup, outermost first.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The sum of the compartments of the subgroup at step 0.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        selected = tuple(categories)
        initial_conditions = self.initial_conditions
        if not initial_conditions.compartment_fractions:
            return initial_conditions.subgroup_total(selected)
        resolved = [initial_conditions.resolve_category(c) for c in selected]
        return sum(
            compartment.amount
            for compartment in self.initial_state()
            if all(
                compartment.categories.get(stratification) == name
                for stratification, name in resolved
            )
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Checks against the model
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _check_parameter_names(self, model: "Model[Self]") -> None:
        """
        Check that parameter ids are not engine variables or bin ids.

        Expanded compartment names and subgroup totals are checked by the
        engine (``engine_state.check_names``).
        """
        bin_ids = {bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins}
        parameter_ids = {p.id for p in model.parameters}

        special = sorted(parameter_ids & set(RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES))
        if special:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Parameter IDs conflict with engine variables: {special}. "
                f"{', '.join(RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES)} are reserved. "
                f"Please rename the conflicting parameters."
            )

        conflicting_names = bin_ids & parameter_ids
        if conflicting_names:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Parameter IDs conflict with reserved compartment names: "
                f"{sorted(conflicting_names)}. "
                f"Bin IDs ({sorted(bin_ids)}) are reserved variables. "
                f"Please rename the conflicting parameters."
            )

    def _check_formula_variables(self, model: "Model[Self]") -> None:
        """Check that every variable of a rate expression is defined."""
        parameter_ids = {param.id for param in model.parameters}
        valid_identifiers = parameter_ids | self._structure_identifiers()

        for transition in self.transitions:
            rates = [("rate", transition.rate)] if transition.rate else []
            rates += [
                ("stratified_rate", stratified.rate)
                for stratified in transition.stratified_rates or []
            ]
            for context, rate in rates:
                self._check_rate_variables(
                    rate, transition.id, context, valid_identifiers, parameter_ids
                )

    def _structure_identifiers(self) -> set[str]:
        """Identifiers the structure and the engine define for rates."""
        category_ids = {
            cat for strat in self.stratifications for cat in strat.categories
        }
        return (
            {bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins}
            | category_ids
            | set(RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES)
            | self._subgroup_total_names()
            | self._full_compartment_names()
        )

    def _subgroup_total_names(self) -> set[str]:
        """Names of the subgroup totals the engine provides for rates."""
        return set(engine_state.subgroup_total_names(self))

    def _full_compartment_names(self) -> set[str]:
        """Returns all full stratified compartment names."""
        if not self.stratifications:
            return set()
        compartments, _ = engine_state.expanded_outputs(self)
        return {output.name for output in compartments}

    def _check_rate_variables(
        self,
        rate: str,
        transition_id: str,
        context: str,
        valid_identifiers: set[str],
        parameter_ids: set[str],
    ) -> None:
        """Check the variables of one rate expression."""
        variables = get_expression_variables(rate)
        undefined_vars = [var for var in variables if var not in valid_identifiers]
        if not undefined_vars:
            return
        bin_ids = {bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins}
        message = (
            f"Undefined variables in transition '{transition_id}' "
            f"{context} '{rate}': {', '.join(undefined_vars)}. "
            f"Available parameters: "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(parameter_ids)) if parameter_ids else 'none'}. "
            f"Available bins: "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(bin_ids)) if bin_ids else 'none'}."
        )
        if any(var.startswith(SUBGROUP_TOTAL_PREFIX) for var in undefined_vars):
            names = sorted(
                name
                for name in self._subgroup_total_names()
                if name.startswith(SUBGROUP_TOTAL_PREFIX)
            )
            message += (
                " Subgroup total names follow the declaration order of the "
                "stratifications. Available subgroup totals: "
                f"{', '.join(names) if names else 'none'}."
            )
        raise ValueError(message)

    def _check_transition_ids(self) -> None:
        """
        Check that each transition moves between bins, or between the
        categories of one stratification.
        """
        bin_ids = {bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins}
        category_to_stratification = {
            cat: strat.id for strat in self.stratifications for cat in strat.categories
        }
        categories_ids = set(category_to_stratification)
        bin_and_categories_ids = bin_ids | categories_ids

        for transition in self.transitions:
            transition_ids = set(transition.source) | set(transition.target)

            if not transition_ids.issubset(bin_and_categories_ids):
                invalid_ids = transition_ids - bin_and_categories_ids
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{transition.id}' contains invalid ids: "
                    f"{invalid_ids}. Ids must be defined in Bin ids "
                    f"or Stratification Categories."
                )

            is_bin_flow = transition_ids.issubset(bin_ids)
            is_stratification_flow = transition_ids.issubset(categories_ids)

            if not is_bin_flow and not is_stratification_flow:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{transition.id}' mixes id types. "
                    f"Found Bin ids ({transition_ids & bin_ids}) and "
                    f"Stratification Categories ids "
                    f"({transition_ids & categories_ids}). "
                    "Transitions must be purely Bin flow or purely "
                    f"Stratification flow."
                )

            if is_stratification_flow:
                parent_stratification_ids = {
                    category_to_stratification[cat_id] for cat_id in transition_ids
                }
                if len(parent_stratification_ids) > 1:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Transition '{transition.id}' is a Stratification flow "
                        f"but involves categories from multiple stratifications: "
                        f"{', '.join(parent_stratification_ids)}. A single "
                        f"transition must only move between categories belonging "
                        f"to the same parent stratification."
                    )

    }
    expected_strat = set(strat_map)
    if actual_strat != expected_strat:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Initial stratification fractions keys must exactly match "
            f"stratification ids. Missing ids: {expected_strat - actual_strat}, "
            f"Extra ids: {actual_strat - expected_strat}."
        )

    for strat_fractions in self.initial_conditions.stratification_fractions:
        strat_id = strat_fractions.stratification
        strat_instance = strat_map[strat_id]
        fractions = {sf.category: sf.fraction for sf in strat_fractions.fractions}

        expected = set(strat_instance.categories)
        actual = set(fractions)
        if actual != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Categories for stratification '{strat_id}' must exactly "
                f"match defined categories in instance '{strat_instance.id}'. "
                f"Missing categories: {expected - actual}, "
                f"Extra categories: {actual - expected}."
            )

        total = sum(fractions.values())
        if not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-6):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Stratification fractions for '{strat_id}' must sum to 1.0, "
                f"but got {total:.7}."
            )
    return self

def check_model(self, model: "Model[Self]") -> None:
    """
    Check the structure against the parameters of its model.

    Parameter ids must not be engine variables or bin ids, every variable
    of a rate must be defined, transitions must move between bins or
    between the categories of one stratification, and the engine must
    plan every transition and build the initial state.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        The model that holds this structure.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If one of these checks fails.
    """
    self._check_parameter_names(model)
    engine_state.transition_flows(self)
    engine_state.check_names(model)
    if self.initial_conditions.compartment_fractions:

    self._check_formula_variables(model)

def outputs_by_source(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """
    Map each bin and accumulator id to the output names it expands into.

    A bin or accumulator produces one output per combination of the
    stratification categories that apply to it. Without stratifications it
    produces a single output named after the id itself.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, list[str]]
        Bin and accumulator ids, each mapped to its output names in
        declaration order.
    """
    outputs: dict[str, list[str]] = {
        source_id: []
        for source_id in (
            *(bin_item.id for bin_item in self.bins),
            *(accumulator.id for accumulator in self.accumulators),
        )
    }
    compartments, accumulators = engine_state.expanded_outputs(self)
    for output in (*compartments, *accumulators):
        outputs[output.source].append(output.name)
    return outputs

def series_label(self, series_id: str) -> SeriesLabel:
    """
    The name and unit of a bin, for a plot of its series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series_id : str
        A bin id, or any other series id.

    Returns
    -------
    SeriesLabel
        The bin's name and unit, or the id and no unit when no bin has it.
    """
    bin_item = next((b for b in self.bins if b.id == series_id), None)
    if bin_item is None:
        return SeriesLabel(series_id, None)
    return SeriesLabel(bin_item.name or series_id, bin_item.unit)

def with_calibrated_values(
    self,
    model: "Model[Self]",
    problem: "CalibrationProblem",
    values: Mapping[str, float],
) -> Self:
    """
    The structure with calibrated initial conditions written back.

    The written structure rebuilds the initial state the engine
    scored. Bin and category values update the fractions they declare.
    Every compartment those fractions do not reproduce, such as an exact
    compartment value or a value that overlaps a per-compartment override,
    is written as a per-compartment override.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        The model the problem was built on. It is not changed.
    problem : CalibrationProblem
        The problem, for its parameters and remainder.
    values : Mapping[str, float]
        Calibrated value per parameter id.

    Returns
    -------
    CompartmentalStructure
        A copy that holds the calibrated initial conditions.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the engine cannot resolve an initial-condition id or the
        remainder, or the initial amounts exceed the total.
    """
    from commol.context._model.calibration_write_back import (
        calibrated_initial_conditions,
    )

    initial_conditions = calibrated_initial_conditions(model, problem, values)
    return self.model_copy(update={"initial_conditions": initial_conditions})

def update_compartment_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
    """
    Upsert per-compartment initial condition overrides.

    A compartment already declared has its fraction replaced; a new one is
    appended. The engine validates the result before it is stored, so a
    rejected call leaves the structure unchanged.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fractions : Mapping[str, float]
        Dictionary mapping expanded compartment names to their new fraction
        of the total.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a name is not an expanded compartment of the model, a value lies
        outside ``[0.0, 1.0]``, or the resulting overrides make the initial
        amounts exceed the total.
    """
    candidate = self.initial_conditions.model_copy(deep=True)
    candidate.update_compartment_fractions(fractions)
    engine_state.initial_state(
        self.model_copy(update={"initial_conditions": candidate})
    )
    self.initial_conditions = candidate

def get_conditioning_categories(self, stratification_id: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """
    Get the categories a stratification is conditioned on.

    An unconditional stratification subdivides the whole model and has
    no conditioning categories. A conditional one subdivides only the
    subgroup its conditions select, and its fractions are relative to that
    subgroup rather than to the whole model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stratification_id : str
        Id of a stratification of the model.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[str, ...]
        Ids of the categories selecting the subgroup this stratification
        subdivides, empty for an unconditional stratification. A category
        name another stratification also declares is qualified, as in
        ``sex:female``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the stratification is not found.
    """
    for stratification in self.stratifications:
        if stratification.id == stratification_id:
            return tuple(
                self.initial_conditions.category_id(
                    condition.stratification, condition.category
                )
                for condition in (stratification.conditions or [])
                if condition.category is not None
            )
    raise ValueError(
        f"Stratification '{stratification_id}' not found. Available: "
        f"{sorted(s.id for s in self.stratifications)}"
    )

def subgroup_total(self, categories: Iterable[str] = ()) -> float:
    """
    Get the initial total of a subgroup.

    See
    :meth:`~commol.context.initial_conditions.InitialConditions.subgroup_total`.

    Per-compartment overrides are folded into the sum for every compartment
    the category chain selects, so the result matches the state the engine
    builds. Without overrides the declared fractions are multiplied.

    Parameters
    ----------
    categories : Iterable[str], optional
        Category ids, bare or qualified (``sex:female``), forming a chain
        from the whole model down to the subgroup, outermost first.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The sum of the compartments of the subgroup at step 0.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
    """
    selected = tuple(categories)
    initial_conditions = self.initial_conditions
    if not initial_conditions.compartment_fractions:
        return initial_conditions.subgroup_total(selected)
    resolved = [initial_conditions.resolve_category(c) for c in selected]
    return sum(
        compartment.amount
        for compartment in self.initial_state()
        if all(
            compartment.categories.get(stratification) == name
            for stratification, name in resolved
        )
    )

class SimulationPlotter:
    """
    A facade for plotting simulation results using Seaborn.

    This class provides methods to visualize simulation results with automatic
    subplot organization, Seaborn styling, and support for overlaying observed data.

    Attributes
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The simulation instance that generated the results.
    results : SimulationResults
        Simulation results, with their positions on the axis.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        simulation: Simulation,
        results: SimulationResults,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the SimulationPlotter.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulation : Simulation
            The simulation instance that generated the results.
        results : SimulationResults
            Simulation results, such as those of ``Simulation.run`` or
            ``Simulation.run_at``. The x axis shows their positions.
        """
        self.simulation = simulation
        self.results = results
        self.bins = list(results.keys())

        logger.info(
            f"SimulationPlotter initialized with {len(self.bins)} bins "
            f"and {len(results.positions)} positions"
        )

    def plot_series(
        self,
        output_file: str | None = None,
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] | None = None,
        calibration_result: CalibrationResult
        | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult
        | None = None,
        config: PlotConfig | None = None,
        series: list[str] | None = None,
        show_legend: bool = True,
        position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
        tick_every: float | None = None,
        x_label: str = "Step",
        **kwargs: str | int | float | bool | None,
    ) -> "Figure":
        """
        Plot simulation results with one subplot per series.

        Creates a figure with subplots arranged in a grid, where each subplot shows
        the evolution of one series over time. Optionally overlays observed data
        points.
        If a ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided, plots confidence intervals.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output_file : str | None
            Path to save the figure. If None, figure is not saved (only returned).
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint] | None
            Optional observed data points to overlay on corresponding bin subplots.
            Model predictions with a factor_id will be scaled for plotting using
            factor values from the calibration_result, so observed values remain in
            their original units.
        calibration_result : CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None
            Optional calibration result. If ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided,
            plots the median prediction with confidence interval bands.
            Factor values are extracted from best_parameters (CalibrationResult) or
            the lowest-loss selected member (ProbabilisticCalibrationResult) to
            multiply model predictions for comparison with observed data.
        config : PlotConfig | None
            Configuration for plot layout and styling (figsize, dpi, layout,
            style, palette, context). If None, uses defaults.
        series : list[str] | None
            What to plot, one subplot each. An entry is an output name (an
            expanded compartment or accumulator, such as ``A_g1``) or a bin or
            accumulator id, which plots the sum of its outputs. An exact output
            name wins over an id. If None, plots every output.
        show_legend : bool
            Whether to show the legend on each subplot. Default True.
        position_label : Callable[[float], str] | None
            Turns a position on the axis into an x-axis tick label, such as a
            date. If None, the ticks show the position.
        tick_every : float | None
            Labels the plotted positions `tick_every` apart on the axis,
            counted from the first plotted position. If None, labels every
            plotted position.
        x_label : str
            The x-axis label. Default "Step".
        **kwargs : str | int | float | bool | None
            Additional keyword arguments passed to seaborn.lineplot().
            Common parameters: linewidth, alpha, linestyle, marker, etc.

        Returns
        -------
        Figure
            The matplotlib Figure object.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an entry of ``series`` is neither an output name nor a bin or
            accumulator id.
        """
        logger.info("Starting plot_series")

        config = config or PlotConfig()
        bins_to_plot = self._series_to_plot(series)

        self._apply_seaborn_style(config)
        factor_values = self._extract_factor_values(calibration_result)

        observed_by_bin = self._group_observed_data(observed_data)

        fig, axes = self._create_series_figure(config, bins_to_plot)
        self._plot_all_series_bins(
            axes,
            bins_to_plot,
            observed_by_bin,
            factor_values,
            calibration_result,
            kwargs,
            show_legend,
            position_label,
            tick_every,
            x_label,
        )
        self._finalize_series_plot(axes, bins_to_plot, output_file, config)

        return fig

    def plot_cumulative(
        self,
        output_file: str | None = None,
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] | None = None,
        calibration_result: CalibrationResult
        | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult
        | None = None,
        config: PlotConfig | None = None,
        series: list[str] | None = None,
        **kwargs: str | int | float | bool | None,
    ) -> "Figure":
        """
        Plot cumulative (accumulated) simulation results with one subplot per series.

        Creates a figure showing the running sum of each series over time.
        Useful for tracking totals, losses, or other accumulated quantities.
        If a ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided, plots confidence intervals.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output_file : str | None
            Path to save the figure. If None, figure is not saved (only returned).
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint] | None
            Optional observed data points to overlay (also shown as cumulative).
            Observed data points with a factor_id will be unscaled for plotting using
            factor values from the calibration_result.
        calibration_result : CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None
            Optional calibration result. If ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided,
            plots the median prediction with confidence interval bands.
            Factor values are extracted from best_parameters (CalibrationResult) or
            the lowest-loss selected member (ProbabilisticCalibrationResult) to
            unscale observed data for comparison with model predictions.
        config : PlotConfig | None
            Configuration for plot layout and styling (figsize, dpi, layout,
            style, palette, context). If None, uses defaults.
        series : list[str] | None
            What to plot, one subplot each: an output name or a bin or
            accumulator id, as in :meth:`plot_series`. If None, plots every
            output.
        **kwargs : str | int | float | bool | None
            Additional keyword arguments passed to seaborn.lineplot().
            Common parameters: linewidth, alpha, linestyle, marker, etc.

        Returns
        -------
        Figure
            The matplotlib Figure object.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an entry of ``series`` is neither an output name nor a bin or
            accumulator id.
        """
        logger.info("Starting plot_cumulative")

        config = config or PlotConfig()
        bins_to_plot = self._series_to_plot(series)

        self._apply_seaborn_style(config)
        factor_values = self._extract_factor_values(calibration_result)

        observed_by_bin = self._group_observed_data(observed_data)
        cumulative_observed = self._calculate_cumulative_observed(
            observed_by_bin, factor_values or {}
        )

        fig, axes = self._create_cumulative_figure(config, bins_to_plot)
        self._plot_all_cumulative_bins(
            axes, bins_to_plot, cumulative_observed, calibration_result, kwargs
        )
        self._finalize_cumulative_plot(axes, bins_to_plot, output_file, config)

        return fig

    def _apply_seaborn_style(self, config: PlotConfig) -> None:
        """Apply Seaborn styling configuration from PlotConfig."""
        if config.style:
            sns.set_style(config.style)
            logger.debug(f"Applied Seaborn style: {config.style}")

        if config.palette:
            sns.set_palette(config.palette)
            logger.debug(f"Applied Seaborn palette: {config.palette}")

        if config.context:
            sns.set_context(config.context)
            logger.debug(f"Applied Seaborn context: {config.context}")

    @staticmethod
    def _apply_x_labels(
        ax: "Axes",
        positions: Sequence[float],
        position_label: Callable[[float], str],
        tick_every: float | None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Label the x axis at the plotted positions `tick_every` apart.

        The tick grid is phased to the first plotted position rather than to
        position 0: for a windowed series the plotted positions are window
        ends, so anchoring at 0 would put ticks on positions that carry no
        plotted point and hand `position_label` a position outside the
        series' convention.
        """
        if tick_every is not None and positions:
            anchor = positions[0]
            ticks = [
                position
                for position in positions
                if same_position(
                    (position - anchor) / tick_every,
                    round((position - anchor) / tick_every),
                )
            ]
        else:
            ticks = list(positions)
        ax.set_xticks(ticks)
        ax.set_xticklabels(
            [position_label(position) for position in ticks], rotation=45, ha="right"
        )

    def _calculate_layout(self, num_bins: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """
        Calculate optimal subplot layout (rows, cols) for given number of bins.
        """
        if num_bins == 1:
            return (1, 1)
        elif num_bins == 2:
            return (1, 2)
        elif num_bins <= 4:
            return (2, 2)
        else:
            # For more bins, try to make a roughly square grid
            cols = math.ceil(math.sqrt(num_bins))
            rows = math.ceil(num_bins / cols)
            return (rows, cols)

    @staticmethod
    def _apply_windows(
        series: list[float],
        positions: Sequence[float],
        observed: list[ObservedDataPoint],
    ) -> tuple[list[float], list[float]] | None:
        """
        Return (ends, values) where each value is the increment of `series`
        over the window that closes at its end (:func:`commol.windowed_totals`).

        The simulation line covers every window end across the full series
        (:func:`commol.window_ends`), so the plot starts at the first window
        end rather than at the first observation.

        Returns None if no observed point has a window set.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the series has no value at a window end or start, such as a
            window of 2.5 on the integer positions of ``Simulation.run``.
        """
        window = next((p.window for p in observed if p.window), None)
        if window is None:
            return None
        ends = window_ends(window, positions[-1] if positions else 0.0)
        return ends, windowed_totals(series, positions, window, ends)

    def _group_observed_data(
        self, observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] | None
    ) -> dict[str, list[ObservedDataPoint]]:
        """
        Group observed data points by the label of their series.
        """
        if not observed_data:
            return {}

        grouped: dict[str, list[ObservedDataPoint]] = defaultdict(list)
        for point in observed_data:
            grouped[point.label].append(point)

        # Sort each group by position
        for compartment in grouped:
            grouped[compartment].sort(key=lambda p: p.at)

        logger.debug(
            f"Grouped {len(observed_data)} observed data points into "
            f"{len(grouped)} compartments"
        )

        return dict(grouped)

    def _series_to_plot(self, series: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
        """The series to plot, each checked to resolve to outputs."""
        if series is None:
            return list(self.bins)
        for series_id in series:
            self._series_components(series_id)
        return list(series)

    def _series_components(self, series_id: str) -> list[str]:
        """Output names whose sum is the series: itself, or a bin's outputs."""
        if series_id in self.results:
            return [series_id]
        try:
            return self.simulation.outputs_for(series_id)
        except KeyError:
            sources = sorted(
                self.simulation.model_definition.structure.outputs_by_source()
            )
            raise ValueError(
                f"'{series_id}' is neither an output nor a bin or accumulator id. "
                f"Outputs: {self.bins}. Bins and accumulators: {sources}"
            ) from None

    def _observed_component_ids(
        self,
        bin_id: str,
        observed: list[ObservedDataPoint],
    ) -> list[str]:
        for point in observed:
            if point.outputs:
                return point.outputs
        return self._series_components(bin_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _sum_series(
        results: dict[str, list[float]],
        component_ids: list[str],
    ) -> list[float]:
        missing = [
            component_id
            for component_id in component_ids
            if component_id not in results
        ]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"Missing result series for aggregate components: {missing}")
        return [
            sum(results[component_id][idx] for component_id in component_ids)
            for idx in range(len(results[component_ids[0]]))
        ]

    def _extract_factor_values(
        self,
        calib_result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None,
    ) -> dict[str, float] | None:
        """
        Extract factor values from calibration result.

        For CalibrationResult, returns best_parameters.
        For ProbabilisticCalibrationResult, returns median values for all parameters.
        The observed data factor_id decides which entries are used as factor values.
        """
        if calib_result is None:
            return None

        if isinstance(calib_result, CalibrationResult):
            return calib_result.best_parameters

        if isinstance(calib_result, ProbabilisticCalibrationResult):
            return calib_result.selected_ensemble.point_parameters

        return None

    @staticmethod
    def _model_factor_for_observed(
        observed: list[ObservedDataPoint],
        factor_values: dict[str, float],
    ) -> float:
        factor_ids = {point.factor_id for point in observed if point.factor_id}
        if not factor_ids:
            return 1.0
        if len(factor_ids) > 1:
            logger.warning(
                "Multiple factor_id values found for one plotted series; leaving "
                "model predictions unscaled."
            )
            return 1.0

        factor_id = next(iter(factor_ids))
        if factor_id not in factor_values:
            logger.warning(
                f"Factor parameter '{factor_id}' not found in calibration result; "
                "leaving model predictions unscaled."
            )
            return 1.0
        return factor_values[factor_id]

    @staticmethod
    def _apply_factor_to_series(values: list[float], factor: float) -> list[float]:
        if factor == 1.0:
            return values
        return [value * factor for value in values]

    def _create_series_figure(
        self, config: PlotConfig, bins_to_plot: list[str]
    ) -> tuple["Figure", list["Axes"]]:
        """
        Create figure and axes array for series plotting.
        """
        layout = config.layout or self._calculate_layout(len(bins_to_plot))
        rows, cols = layout
        figsize = (cols * 4.5, rows * 3.5 + 1.0)
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=figsize, dpi=config.dpi)

        # Ensure axes is always a flat array
        if layout[0] == 1 and layout[1] == 1:
            axes = [axes]
        else:
            axes = axes.flatten() if hasattr(axes, "flatten") else [axes]

        return fig, axes

    def _plot_all_series_bins(
        self,
        axes: list["Axes"],
        bins_to_plot: list[str],
        observed_by_bin: dict[str, list[ObservedDataPoint]],
        factor_values: dict[str, float] | None,
        calibration_result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None,
        kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
        show_legend: bool = True,
        position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
        tick_every: float | None = None,
        x_label: str = "Step",
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot series data for all bins across subplots.
        """
        for idx, bin_id in enumerate(bins_to_plot):
            if idx >= len(axes):
                break

            ax = axes[idx]

            if isinstance(calibration_result, ProbabilisticCalibrationResult):
                self._plot_bin_series_probabilistic(
                    ax,
                    bin_id,
                    observed_by_bin.get(bin_id, []),
                    factor_values or {},
                    calibration_result,
                    dict(kwargs),
                    show_legend,
                    position_label,
                    tick_every,
                    x_label,
                )
            else:
                self._plot_bin_series(
                    ax,
                    bin_id,
                    observed_by_bin.get(bin_id, []),
                    factor_values or {},
                    dict(kwargs),
                    show_legend,
                    position_label,
                    tick_every,
                    x_label,
                )

    def _finalize_series_plot(
        self,
        axes: list["Axes"],
        bins_to_plot: list[str],
        output_file: str | None,
        config: PlotConfig,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Finalize series plot by hiding unused subplots and saving.
        """
        for idx in range(len(bins_to_plot), len(axes)):
            axes[idx].set_visible(False)

        plt.tight_layout()

        if output_file:
            plt.savefig(output_file, dpi=config.dpi, bbox_inches="tight")
            logger.info(f"Series plot saved to {output_file}")

    def _create_cumulative_figure(
        self, config: PlotConfig, bins_to_plot: list[str]
    ) -> tuple["Figure", list["Axes"]]:
        """
        Create figure and axes array for cumulative plotting.
        """
        layout = config.layout or self._calculate_layout(len(bins_to_plot))
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
            layout[0], layout[1], figsize=config.figsize, dpi=config.dpi
        )

        # Ensure axes is always a flat array
        if layout[0] == 1 and layout[1] == 1:
            axes = [axes]
        else:
            axes = axes.flatten() if hasattr(axes, "flatten") else [axes]

        return fig, axes

    def _plot_all_cumulative_bins(
        self,
        axes: list["Axes"],
        bins_to_plot: list[str],
        cumulative_observed: dict[str, list[tuple[int | float, float]]],
        calibration_result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None,
        kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot cumulative data for all bins across subplots.
        """
        for idx, bin_id in enumerate(bins_to_plot):
            if idx >= len(axes):
                break

            ax = axes[idx]

            if isinstance(calibration_result, ProbabilisticCalibrationResult):
                self._plot_bin_cumulative_probabilistic(
                    ax,
                    bin_id,
                    cumulative_observed.get(bin_id, []),
                    calibration_result,
                    dict(kwargs),
                )
            else:
                cumulative_results = self._calculate_cumulative(bins_to_plot)
                self._plot_bin_cumulative(
                    ax,
                    bin_id,
                    cumulative_results[bin_id],
                    cumulative_observed.get(bin_id, []),
                    dict(kwargs),
                )

    def _finalize_cumulative_plot(
        self,
        axes: list["Axes"],
        bins_to_plot: list[str],
        output_file: str | None,
        config: PlotConfig,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Finalize cumulative plot by hiding unused subplots and saving.
        """
        for idx in range(len(bins_to_plot), len(axes)):
            axes[idx].set_visible(False)

        plt.tight_layout()

        if output_file:
            plt.savefig(output_file, dpi=config.dpi, bbox_inches="tight")
            logger.info(f"Cumulative plot saved to {output_file}")

    def _plot_bin_series(
        self,
        ax: "Axes",
        bin_id: str,
        observed: list[ObservedDataPoint],
        factor_values: dict[str, float],
        plot_kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
        show_legend: bool = True,
        position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
        tick_every: float | None = None,
        x_label: str = "Step",
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot the series of a single bin on given axes.
        """
        component_ids = self._observed_component_ids(bin_id, observed)
        series = self._sum_series(self.results, component_ids)
        windowed = self._apply_windows(series, self.results.positions, observed)
        if windowed is not None:
            positions, values = windowed
        else:
            positions = self.results.positions
            values = series
        values = self._apply_factor_to_series(
            values,
            self._model_factor_for_observed(observed, factor_values),
        )

        # Build parameters for lineplot
        params = {
            "x": positions,
            "y": values,
            "ax": ax,
            "label": "Simulation",
            "legend": show_legend,
        }
        params.update(plot_kwargs)

        # Plot simulation results as line
        sns.lineplot(**params)

        # Overlay observed data if available
        if observed:
            obs_positions = [p.at for p in observed]
            obs_values = [p.value for p in observed]
            sns.scatterplot(
                x=obs_positions,
                y=obs_values,
                ax=ax,
                label="Observed",
                color="red",
                s=30,
                alpha=0.7,
                zorder=5,
                legend=show_legend,
            )

        label = self.simulation.model_definition.structure.series_label(bin_id)
        unit_str = label.unit or ""
        bin_name = label.name

        ax.set_xlabel(x_label)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{unit_str}")
        ax.set_title(f"{bin_name}")
        if position_label:
            self._apply_x_labels(ax, positions, position_label, tick_every)
        if show_legend:
            ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    def _plot_bin_series_probabilistic(
        self,
        ax: "Axes",
        bin_id: str,
        observed: list[ObservedDataPoint],
        factor_values: dict[str, float],
        prob_result: ProbabilisticCalibrationResult,
        plot_kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
        show_legend: bool = True,
        position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
        tick_every: float | None = None,
        x_label: str = "Step",
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot the series of a single bin with probabilistic confidence intervals.
        """
        component_ids = self._observed_component_ids(bin_id, observed)
        missing = [
            component_id
            for component_id in component_ids
            if component_id not in prob_result.selected_ensemble.prediction_median
        ]
        if missing:
            logger.warning(
                f"Bin '{bin_id}' aggregate components not found in probabilistic "
                f"result predictions: {missing}"
            )
            return

        median_values = self._sum_series(
            prob_result.selected_ensemble.prediction_median,
            component_ids,
        )
        ci_lower = self._sum_series(
            prob_result.selected_ensemble.prediction_ci_lower,
            component_ids,
        )
        ci_upper = self._sum_series(
            prob_result.selected_ensemble.prediction_ci_upper,
            component_ids,
        )

        prediction_positions = prob_result.selected_ensemble.prediction_positions
        windowed_median = self._apply_windows(
            median_values, prediction_positions, observed
        )
        uses_memberwise_windowed_prediction = False
        if windowed_median is not None:
            positions, _ = windowed_median
            win_med = prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_median
            win_positions = prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_positions
            if win_med and bin_id in win_med:
                uses_memberwise_windowed_prediction = True
                plot_median = win_med[bin_id]
                positions = win_positions.get(bin_id, positions)
                plot_ci_lower = (
                    prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_ci_lower[bin_id]
                )
                plot_ci_upper = (
                    prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_ci_upper[bin_id]
                )
            elif win_med and all(
                component_id in win_med for component_id in component_ids
            ):
                uses_memberwise_windowed_prediction = True
                plot_median = self._sum_series(win_med, component_ids)
                positions = win_positions.get(component_ids[0], positions)
                plot_ci_lower = self._sum_series(
                    prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_ci_lower,
                    component_ids,
                )
                plot_ci_upper = self._sum_series(
                    prob_result.selected_ensemble.windowed_prediction_ci_upper,
                    component_ids,
                )
            else:
                _, plot_median = windowed_median
                # `observed` already yielded `windowed_median`, so it carries
                # a window and neither call returns None. The fallbacks keep
                # the unwindowed series, matching the outer non-windowed branch.
                windowed_ci_lower = self._apply_windows(
                    ci_lower, prediction_positions, observed
                )
                windowed_ci_upper = self._apply_windows(
                    ci_upper, prediction_positions, observed
                )
                plot_ci_lower = windowed_ci_lower[1] if windowed_ci_lower else ci_lower
                plot_ci_upper = windowed_ci_upper[1] if windowed_ci_upper else ci_upper
        else:
            positions = prediction_positions
            plot_median = median_values
            plot_ci_lower = ci_lower
            plot_ci_upper = ci_upper

        model_factor = (
            1.0
            if uses_memberwise_windowed_prediction
            else self._model_factor_for_observed(observed, factor_values)
        )
        plot_median = self._apply_factor_to_series(plot_median, model_factor)
        plot_ci_lower = self._apply_factor_to_series(plot_ci_lower, model_factor)
        plot_ci_upper = self._apply_factor_to_series(plot_ci_upper, model_factor)

        # Build parameters for lineplot (median)
        params = {
            "x": positions,
            "y": plot_median,
            "ax": ax,
            "label": "Median Prediction",
            "legend": show_legend,
        }
        params.update(plot_kwargs)

        # Plot median prediction
        sns.lineplot(**params)

        # Plot confidence interval as filled area
        ax.fill_between(
            positions,
            plot_ci_lower,
            plot_ci_upper,
            alpha=0.3,
            label="95% CI" if show_legend else "_nolegend_",
        )

        # Overlay observed data if available
        if observed:
            obs_positions = [p.at for p in observed]
            obs_values = [p.value for p in observed]
            sns.scatterplot(
                x=obs_positions,
                y=obs_values,
                ax=ax,
                label="Observed",
                color="red",
                s=30,
                alpha=0.7,
                zorder=5,
                legend=show_legend,
            )

        label = self.simulation.model_definition.structure.series_label(bin_id)
        unit_str = label.unit or ""
        bin_name = label.name

        ax.set_xlabel(x_label)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{unit_str}")
        ax.set_title(f"{bin_name}")
        if position_label:
            self._apply_x_labels(ax, positions, position_label, tick_every)
        if show_legend:
            ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    def _plot_bin_cumulative_probabilistic(
        self,
        ax: "Axes",
        bin_id: str,
        cumulative_observed: list[tuple[int | float, float]],
        prob_result: ProbabilisticCalibrationResult,
        plot_kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot cumulative data for a single bin with probabilistic confidence intervals.
        """
        component_ids = self._series_components(bin_id)
        ensemble = prob_result.selected_ensemble
        missing = [
            component_id
            for component_id in component_ids
            if component_id not in ensemble.prediction_median
        ]
        if missing:
            logger.warning(
                f"Series '{bin_id}' components not found in probabilistic result "
                f"predictions: {missing}"
            )
            return

        # Calculate cumulative values from the probabilistic predictions
        median_values = self._sum_series(ensemble.prediction_median, component_ids)
        ci_lower = self._sum_series(ensemble.prediction_ci_lower, component_ids)
        ci_upper = self._sum_series(ensemble.prediction_ci_upper, component_ids)

        # Calculate cumulative sums
        cumulative_median = np.cumsum(median_values).tolist()
        cumulative_ci_lower = np.cumsum(ci_lower).tolist()
        cumulative_ci_upper = np.cumsum(ci_upper).tolist()

        positions = ensemble.prediction_positions

        # Build parameters for lineplot (median)
        params = {
            "x": positions,
            "y": cumulative_median,
            "ax": ax,
            "label": "Median Prediction (Cumulative)",
        }
        params.update(plot_kwargs)

        # Plot cumulative median prediction
        sns.lineplot(**params)

        # Plot cumulative confidence interval as filled area
        ax.fill_between(
            positions,
            cumulative_ci_lower,
            cumulative_ci_upper,
            alpha=0.3,
            label="95% CI",
        )

        # Overlay cumulative observed data if available
        if cumulative_observed:
            obs_positions = [at for at, _ in cumulative_observed]
            obs_values = [value for _, value in cumulative_observed]
            sns.scatterplot(
                x=obs_positions,
                y=obs_values,
                ax=ax,
                label="Observed (Cumulative)",
                color="red",
                s=30,
                alpha=0.7,
                zorder=5,
            )

        label = self.simulation.model_definition.structure.series_label(bin_id)
        unit_str = label.unit or ""
        bin_name = label.name

        ax.set_xlabel("Step")
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{unit_str}")
        ax.set_title(f"{bin_name}")
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    def _calculate_cumulative(self, bins_to_plot: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        Calculate cumulative (running sum) for specified bins.
        """
        cumulative: dict[str, list[float]] = {}

        for bin_id in bins_to_plot:
            values = self._sum_series(self.results, self._series_components(bin_id))
            cumsum = []
            running_total = 0.0

            for value in values:
                running_total += value
                cumsum.append(running_total)

            cumulative[bin_id] = cumsum

        return cumulative

    def _calculate_cumulative_observed(
        self,
        observed_by_bin: dict[str, list[ObservedDataPoint]],
        factor_values: dict[str, float],
    ) -> dict[str, list[tuple[int | float, float]]]:
        """
        Calculate cumulative observed data (position, cumulative_value).
        Divides by the factor if the observation has a factor_id.
        """
        cumulative: dict[str, list[tuple[int | float, float]]] = {}

        for bin_id, points in observed_by_bin.items():
            cumsum = []
            running_total = 0.0

            for point in points:
                # Divide by the factor if the observation has a factor_id
                value = (
                    point.value / factor_values[point.factor_id]
                    if point.factor_id and point.factor_id in factor_values
                    else point.value
                )
                running_total += value
                cumsum.append((point.at, running_total))

            cumulative[bin_id] = cumsum

        return cumulative

    def _plot_bin_cumulative(
        self,
        ax: "Axes",
        bin_id: str,
        cumulative_values: list[float],
        cumulative_observed: list[tuple[int | float, float]],
        plot_kwargs: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | None],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Plot cumulative data for a single bin on given axes.
        """
        positions = self.results.positions

        # Build parameters for lineplot
        params = {
            "x": positions,
            "y": cumulative_values,
            "ax": ax,
            "label": "Simulation (Cumulative)",
        }
        params.update(plot_kwargs)

        # Plot cumulative simulation results
        sns.lineplot(**params)

        # Overlay cumulative observed data if available
        if cumulative_observed:
            obs_positions = [at for at, _ in cumulative_observed]
            obs_values = [value for _, value in cumulative_observed]
            sns.scatterplot(
                x=obs_positions,
                y=obs_values,
                ax=ax,
                label="Observed (Cumulative)",
                color="red",
                s=30,
                alpha=0.7,
                zorder=5,
            )

        label = self.simulation.model_definition.structure.series_label(bin_id)
        unit_str = label.unit or ""
        bin_name = label.name

        ax.set_xlabel("Step")
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{unit_str}")
        ax.set_title(f"{bin_name}")
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
