def plot_series(
    self,
    output_file: str | None = None,
    observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] | None = None,
    calibration_result: CalibrationResult
    | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult
    | None = None,
    config: PlotConfig | None = None,
    series: list[str] | None = None,
    show_legend: bool = True,
    position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
    tick_every: float | None = None,
    x_label: str = "Step",
    **kwargs: str | int | float | bool | None,
) -> "Figure":
    """
    Plot simulation results with one subplot per series.

    Creates a figure with subplots arranged in a grid, where each subplot shows
    the evolution of one series over time. Optionally overlays observed data
    points.
    If a ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided, plots confidence intervals.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output_file : str | None
        Path to save the figure. If None, figure is not saved (only returned).
    observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint] | None
        Optional observed data points to overlay on corresponding bin subplots.
        Model predictions with a factor_id will be scaled for plotting using
        factor values from the calibration_result, so observed values remain in
        their original units.
    calibration_result : CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | None
        Optional calibration result. If ProbabilisticCalibrationResult is provided,
        plots the median prediction with confidence interval bands.
        Factor values are extracted from best_parameters (CalibrationResult) or
        the lowest-loss selected member (ProbabilisticCalibrationResult) to
        multiply model predictions for comparison with observed data.
    config : PlotConfig | None
        Configuration for plot layout and styling (figsize, dpi, layout,
        style, palette, context). If None, uses defaults.
    series : list[str] | None
        What to plot, one subplot each. An entry is an output name (an
        expanded compartment or accumulator, such as ``A_g1``) or a bin or
        accumulator id, which plots the sum of its outputs. An exact output
        name wins over an id. If None, plots every output.
    show_legend : bool
        Whether to show the legend on each subplot. Default True.
    position_label : Callable[[float], str] | None
        Turns a position on the axis into an x-axis tick label, such as a
        date. If None, the ticks show the position.
    tick_every : float | None
        Labels the plotted positions `tick_every` apart on the axis,
        counted from the first plotted position. If None, labels every
        plotted position.
    x_label : str
        The x-axis label. Default "Step".
    **kwargs : str | int | float | bool | None
        Additional keyword arguments passed to seaborn.lineplot().
        Common parameters: linewidth, alpha, linestyle, marker, etc.

    Returns
    -------
    Figure
        The matplotlib Figure object.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an entry of ``series`` is neither an output name nor a bin or
        accumulator id.
    """
    logger.info("Starting plot_series")

    config = config or PlotConfig()
    bins_to_plot = self._series_to_plot(series)

    self._apply_seaborn_style(config)
    factor_values = self._extract_factor_values(calibration_result)

    observed_by_bin = self._group_observed_data(observed_data)

    fig, axes = self._create_series_figure(config, bins_to_plot)
    self._plot_all_series_bins(
        axes,
        bins_to_plot,
        observed_by_bin,
        factor_values,
        calibration_result,
        kwargs,
        show_legend,
        position_label,
        tick_every,
        x_label,
    )
    self._finalize_series_plot(axes, bins_to_plot, output_file, config)

    return fig

class PlotConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    Configuration for plot layout and styling.

    Attributes
    ----------
    figsize : tuple[float, float]
        Figure size in inches (width, height).
    dpi : int
        Dots per inch for figure resolution.
    layout : tuple[int, int] | None
        Subplot layout as (rows, cols). If None, automatically calculated based on
        number of bins.
    style : str | None
        Seaborn style preset. Must be a valid seaborn style value:
        "darkgrid", "whitegrid", "dark", "white", or "ticks".
        See: https://seaborn.pydata.org/generated/seaborn.set_style.html
    palette : str | None
        Seaborn color palette name. Must be a valid seaborn palette value:
        "deep", "muted", "bright", "pastel", "dark", "colorblind",
        or any matplotlib colormap like "Set1", "Set2", "tab10", etc.
        See: https://seaborn.pydata.org/tutorial/color_palettes.html
    context : str | None
        Seaborn context for scaling plot elements. Must be a valid seaborn context:
        "paper", "notebook", "talk", or "poster".
        See: https://seaborn.pydata.org/generated/seaborn.set_context.html

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # Direct configuration
    >>> config = PlotConfig(style="whitegrid", palette="Set2", context="talk")

    >>> # Using presets
    >>> config = PlotConfig.presentation()
    >>> config = PlotConfig.publication()
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    figsize: tuple[float, float] = Field(
        default=(12, 8),
        description="Figure size in inches (width, height)",
    )
    dpi: int = Field(
        default=100,
        description="Dots per inch for figure resolution",
    )
    layout: tuple[int, int] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Subplot layout as (rows, cols). If None, auto-calculated.",
    )
    style: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Seaborn style preset: 'darkgrid', 'whitegrid', 'dark', 'white', 'ticks'"
        ),
    )
    palette: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Seaborn color palette name (e.g., 'deep', 'Set2', 'colorblind')",
    )
    context: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Seaborn context: 'paper', 'notebook', 'talk', 'poster'",
    )

    @classmethod
    def presentation(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for presentations.

        Large figure size, high DPI, and "talk" context for readable text on slides.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with presentation-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(16, 10),
            dpi=150,
            style="whitegrid",
            context="talk",
            palette="colorblind",
        )

    @classmethod
    def publication(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for academic publications.

        Smaller figure size suitable for journal columns, high DPI for print quality,
        and minimal styling.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with publication-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(8, 6),
            dpi=300,
            style="ticks",
            context="paper",
        )

    @classmethod
    def notebook(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for Jupyter notebooks.

        Balanced defaults for interactive exploration.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with notebook-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(12, 8),
            dpi=100,
            style="whitegrid",
            context="notebook",
        )

Bases: BaseModel

Unified configuration for probabilistic calibration.

This configuration groups all settings for the probabilistic calibration workflow, which finds an ensemble of parameter sets with uncertainty quantification instead of a single optimal solution.

The workflow consists of: 1. Run: Multiple independent calibration runs 2. Evaluation Processing: Deduplication and filtering 3. Clustering: Group similar solutions 4. Representative Selection: Pick diverse solutions from clusters 5. Ensemble Selection: ensemble subset selection 6. Statistics: Calculate confidence intervals and coverage

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_runs int

Number of independent calibration runs to perform (default: 10). More runs provide better parameter space exploration but take longer.

evaluation_processing ProbEvaluationFilterConfig

Configuration for evaluation deduplication and filtering

clustering ProbClusteringConfig

Configuration for clustering calibration candidates

representative_selection ProbRepresentativeConfig

Configuration for selecting representatives from clusters

ensemble_selection ProbNsga2Config | ProbGreedyLocalSearchConfig

Configuration for the selected ensemble algorithm. NSGA-II is the default; use the greedy configuration to select the alternate backend.

confidence_level float

Confidence interval level (default: 0.95 for 95% CI). Must be in range (0.0, 1.0).

class ProbabilisticCalibrationConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    Unified configuration for probabilistic calibration.

    This configuration groups all settings for the probabilistic calibration
    workflow, which finds an ensemble of parameter sets with uncertainty
    quantification instead of a single optimal solution.

    The workflow consists of:
    1. Run: Multiple independent calibration runs
    2. Evaluation Processing: Deduplication and filtering
    3. Clustering: Group similar solutions
    4. Representative Selection: Pick diverse solutions from clusters
    5. Ensemble Selection: ensemble subset selection
    6. Statistics: Calculate confidence intervals and coverage

    Attributes
    ----------
    n_runs : int
        Number of independent calibration runs to perform (default: 10).
        More runs provide better parameter space exploration but take longer.
    evaluation_processing : ProbEvaluationFilterConfig
        Configuration for evaluation deduplication and filtering
    clustering : ProbClusteringConfig
        Configuration for clustering calibration candidates
    representative_selection : ProbRepresentativeConfig
        Configuration for selecting representatives from clusters
    ensemble_selection : ProbNsga2Config | ProbGreedyLocalSearchConfig
        Configuration for the selected ensemble algorithm. NSGA-II is the
        default; use the greedy configuration to select the alternate backend.
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence interval level (default: 0.95 for 95% CI).
        Must be in range (0.0, 1.0).
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    n_runs: int = Field(
        default=10, gt=0, description="Number of calibration runs to perform"
    )
    evaluation_processing: ProbEvaluationFilterConfig = Field(
        default_factory=ProbEvaluationFilterConfig,
        description="Configuration for evaluation processing",
    )
    clustering: ProbClusteringConfig = Field(
        default_factory=ProbClusteringConfig,
        description="Configuration for clustering calibration candidates",
    )
    representative_selection: ProbRepresentativeConfig = Field(
        default_factory=ProbRepresentativeConfig,
        description="Configuration for representative selection",
    )
    ensemble_selection: ProbNsga2Config | ProbGreedyLocalSearchConfig = Field(
        default_factory=ProbNsga2Config,
        description="Configuration for ensemble selection",
    )
    confidence_level: float = Field(
        default=0.95,
        gt=0.0,
        lt=1.0,
        description="Confidence interval level (e.g., 0.95 for 95% CI)",
    )
    include_ensemble_candidates: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description=(
            "Include the parameter sets and losses available to final ensemble "
            "selection in the calibration result."
        ),
    )

Bases: BaseModel

Configuration for processing calibration evaluations.

Controls deduplication and filtering of parameter sets from calibration runs before clustering and ensemble selection.

Attributes:

Name Type Description deduplication_tolerance float

Absolute tolerance for identifying duplicate parameter sets (default: 1e-6). Parameter sets within this tolerance are considered identical.

loss_percentile_filter float

Fraction (0.0, 1.0] of best solutions by loss to retain (default: 1.0). For example, 0.1 keeps only the best 10% of evaluations, filtering out poor-quality solutions that would widen confidence intervals.

min_evaluations_required int

Minimum number of unique evaluations required for analysis (default: 5). Calibration fails if fewer unique evaluations remain after deduplication.

evaluation_retention Literal['all', 'best_per_run', 'top_k_per_run']

Amount of optimizer history retained from each run before crossing the Python/Rust boundary.

top_k_per_run int | None

Number of evaluations retained per run when evaluation_retention is "top_k_per_run".

max_loss_ratio float | None

Optional maximum loss relative to the best retained evaluation. Set this to exclude optimizer states that are too poor to represent calibrated uncertainty.

tail_max_loss_ratio float | None

Optional broader maximum loss ratio for prediction-novel tail candidates. When enabled with tail_max_representatives, evaluations beyond max_loss_ratio but within this wider band may be admitted only if they add observed-prediction diversity.

tail_max_representatives int

Maximum number of additional prediction-novel tail representatives.

        Parameter sets within this tolerance are considered identical.
    loss_percentile_filter : float

        For example, 0.1 keeps only the best 10% of evaluations, filtering out
        poor-quality solutions that would widen confidence intervals.

            "Optional broader maximum loss ratio for prediction-novel tail "
            "candidates. When set with tail_max_representatives > 0, candidates "
            "outside max_loss_ratio but inside this band can be added after "
            "representative selection if they add observed-prediction diversity."
        ),
    )
    tail_max_representatives: int = Field(
        default=0,
        ge=0,
        description=(
            "Maximum number of additional prediction-novel tail representatives "
            "to add from tail_max_loss_ratio."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_evaluation_retention(self) -> Self:
        """Validate evaluation retention configuration."""
        if self.evaluation_retention == "top_k_per_run" and self.top_k_per_run is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "top_k_per_run must be specified when "
                "evaluation_retention='top_k_per_run'"
            )
        if (
            self.evaluation_retention != "top_k_per_run"
            and self.top_k_per_run is not None
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "top_k_per_run should only be set when "
                "evaluation_retention='top_k_per_run'"
            )
        if self.tail_max_representatives > 0 and self.tail_max_loss_ratio is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "tail_max_loss_ratio must be specified when "
                "tail_max_representatives > 0"
            )
        if self.tail_max_representatives > 0 and self.max_loss_ratio is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "max_loss_ratio must be specified when tail_max_representatives > 0"
            )
        if (
            self.max_loss_ratio is not None
            and self.tail_max_loss_ratio is not None
            and self.tail_max_loss_ratio < self.max_loss_ratio
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "tail_max_loss_ratio must be greater than or equal to max_loss_ratio"
            )
        return self

def ci_percentiles(confidence_level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Lower and upper percentile points of a two-sided confidence interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float]
        Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"confidence_level must be strictly between 0 and 1, got "
            f"{confidence_level}. Note this is a fraction, not a percentage: "
            f"use 0.95 for a 95% interval."
        )
    return (
        (1.0 - confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
        (1.0 + confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
    )

def member_statistics(
    per_member: EnsembleValues,
    confidence_level: float,
) -> dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]] | dict[str, float | list[float]]:
    """
    Spread of one quantity across the members of an ensemble.

    Each member must already be reduced to the quantity of interest, so that
    the reported interval is a percentile of member values.

    Parameters
    ----------
    per_member : Sequence[float] | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | NDArray
        One entry per ensemble member. Entries may be scalars, in which case
        every returned statistic is a scalar, or equal-length series, in which
        case every returned statistic is a series reduced across members at
        each position. A numpy array is accepted, but its rank is not visible
        to a type checker; pass a list of lists for a precise return type.
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]]
        Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
        ``max``. Scalar members give scalar statistics, series members give
        series statistics.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is out of range, or ``per_member`` is empty.
    """
    lower_percentile, upper_percentile = ci_percentiles(confidence_level)
    values = np.asarray(per_member, dtype=float)
    if values.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("per_member must hold at least one ensemble member.")

    return {
        "mean": np.mean(values, axis=0).tolist(),
        "median": np.percentile(values, 50.0, axis=0).tolist(),
        "ci_lower": np.percentile(values, lower_percentile, axis=0).tolist(),
        "ci_upper": np.percentile(values, upper_percentile, axis=0).tolist(),
        "min": np.min(values, axis=0).tolist(),
        "max": np.max(values, axis=0).tolist(),
    }

Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones. The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (ModelStructure.report_sections); a compartmental model adds initial_conditions.

Initial conditions of a compartmental model carry the effective value the engine builds from the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment overrides, its fraction as that value over the declared total, and the group it belongs to: total for bins and unconditional stratifications, and the conditioning categories for a conditional one. The total row is the declared total, with fraction 1.0. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a None fraction and None value as its "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

For a probabilistic result each entry gains an interval holding the ensemble spread. A parameter is in the unit it was calibrated in. An initial-condition entry is in the fraction the row reports: a conditional stratification's category is calibrated as a group fraction but reported over the total, so its interval is rescaled by the group's share of the total and brackets the reported fraction.

def applied_parameters_report(
    model: Model,
    result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float],
    problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None,
    parameter_statistics: Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
) -> AppliedParametersReport:
    """
    Report every parameter of a calibrated model, and the values of its kind.

    Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set
    it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones.
    The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind
    (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); a compartmental model adds
    ``initial_conditions``.

    Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a
    series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values.
    ``factor`` parameters have no place in the model, so they are reported from
    `problem` when it is given.

    Initial conditions of a compartmental model carry the effective
    ``value`` the engine builds
    from the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment overrides, its
    ``fraction`` as that value over the declared total, and the
    ``group`` it belongs to: ``total`` for bins and unconditional
    stratifications, and the conditioning categories for a conditional one.
    The ``total`` row is the declared total, with fraction 1.0. A bin left
    uncalibrated keeps a ``None`` fraction and ``None`` value as its "needs
    calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

    For a probabilistic result each entry gains an ``interval`` holding the
    ensemble spread. A parameter is in the unit it was calibrated in. An
    initial-condition entry is in the fraction the row reports: a conditional
    stratification's category is calibrated as a group fraction but reported
    over the total, so its interval is rescaled by the group's share of the
    total and brackets the reported fraction.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        The model carrying the applied values.
    result : CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | Mapping
        The calibration outcome, or a mapping of parameter id to value such as
        one ensemble member's parameters.
    problem : CalibrationProblem | None, optional
        The problem the result came from, used to report factor parameters.
    parameter_statistics : Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None, optional
        Ensemble spread per entry. Taken from `result` when it is a
        probabilistic result and this is not given.
    confidence_level : float | None, optional
        Confidence level the intervals describe. Taken from `result` when it is
        a probabilistic result and this is not given.

    Returns
    -------
    AppliedParametersReport
        Key ``parameters`` and the sections of the kind (``initial_conditions``
        for a compartmental model), preceded by ``confidence_level`` when there
        is one.
    """
    calibrated = calibrated_values(result)
    parameter_statistics, confidence_level = _ensemble_details(
        result, parameter_statistics, confidence_level
    )
    calibrated_ids = set(calibrated)

    parameters: dict[str, ParameterEntry] = {
        parameter.id: _parameter_entry(
            parameter.id, parameter.value, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
        )
        for parameter in model.parameters
        if isinstance(parameter.value, (int, float))
    }
    for factor_id in _factor_ids(problem):
        if factor_id in calibrated:
            parameters[factor_id] = _parameter_entry(
                factor_id, calibrated[factor_id], calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
            )

    report: dict[str, object] = {}
    # `confidence_level` leads the report, so it is written first.
    if confidence_level is not None:
        report["confidence_level"] = confidence_level
    report["parameters"] = parameters
    report.update(
        model.structure.report_sections(model, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics)
    )
    return cast(AppliedParametersReport, report)

class Simulation:
    """
    A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

    The engine follows the model: ``run`` and ``engine`` rebuild it when
    ``model_definition`` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built
    from, for example after ``Model.update_parameters``.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: Model):
        """
        Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind.
            None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

        """
        if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
            raise TypeError(
                f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
                f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
                "holds the structure of its kind, such as a CompartmentalStructure."
            )
        logging.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
        self.model_definition: Model = model
        self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())

    def _build_engine(self, model_json: str) -> None:
        """Build the engine and its output names from a model JSON."""
        self._model_json: str = model_json
        self._engine: "EngineProtocol" = build_engine(model_json)
        self._simulation_outputs: list[str] = self._engine.output_names
        logging.info(
            f"Simulation engine ready. Outputs: {len(self._simulation_outputs)}"
        )

    def _sync_engine(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild the engine when the model changed since it was built."""
        model_json = self.model_definition.model_dump_json()
        if model_json != self._model_json:
            logging.info("Model changed since the engine was built; rebuilding it.")
            self._build_engine(model_json)

    def _validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self, model: Model) -> None:
        """
        Validates that every parameter, and every value of the model kind, has
        a value (is calibrated).

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model to validate.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any parameter, or any value of the model kind such as an
            initial condition, has a None value.
        """
        uncalibrated_params = model.get_uncalibrated_parameters()
        uncalibrated_ics = model.structure.uncalibrated_values()

        errors = []
        if uncalibrated_params:
            errors.append(
                f"Parameters requiring calibration: {', '.join(uncalibrated_params)}"
            )
        if uncalibrated_ics:
            errors.append(
                f"Initial conditions requiring calibration: "
                f"{', '.join(uncalibrated_ics)}"
            )

        if errors:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot run Simulation: {'; '.join(errors)}. "
                f"Please calibrate these values before running a simulation."
            )

    def run(self, num_steps: int) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state on its default grid.

        Every call starts at position 0 with the current ``model_definition``,
        so two calls with the same model give the same result. To continue a
        run, call ``simulation.engine.step()``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: the results hold the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, and the positions.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value.
        """
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        self._engine.reset()
        logging.info(f"Running simulation for {num_steps} steps.")
        start = time.time()
        positions, rows = self._engine.run(num_steps)
        logging.info(f"Simulation complete. It took {time.time() - start} seconds.")
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows)

    def run_at(self, at: Sequence[float]) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state and reports at given positions.

        The positions are on the axis, the independent variable of the model.
        The engine decides which positions its model type reports at: a
        DifferentialEquations model at any finite, non-negative position, from
        the dense output of its solver; a DifferenceEquations model only at
        integer steps.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, and the positions.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, the positions are
            not sorted and unique, or the engine does not report at one of them;
            the message is the engine's.
        """
        positions = [float(position) for position in at]
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        self._engine.reset()
        rows = self._engine.run_at(positions)
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows)

    @property
    def engine(self) -> "EngineProtocol":
        """
        The engine for the current ``model_definition``.

        It is rebuilt, at step 0, when the model changed since it was built.
        Otherwise it is the same object, in the state the last ``run`` or
        ``step`` left it.
        """
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._engine

    @property
    def simulation_outputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of the columns returned by simulation runs."""
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._simulation_outputs

    def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
        """
        Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

        The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
        (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for a compartmental model, by
        bin and accumulator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            A source id, such as a bin id or an accumulator id.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Output names for that id, in the order the engine reports them.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If `id` is not a source of the model.
        """
        outputs = self.model_definition.structure.outputs_by_source()
        if id not in outputs:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{id}' is not a bin or accumulator of model "
                f"'{self.model_definition.name}'. Available: {sorted(outputs)}"
            )
        return outputs[id]

    def group_outputs(self, ids: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        Group output names by the bin or accumulator they belong to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Each id mapped to its output names, keeping the order given.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model.
        """
        return {id: self.outputs_for(id) for id in ids}

    def total_series(
        self,
        results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        ids: Iterable[str],
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
            Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One value per position of `results`.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        """
        names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
        missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
        if not names:
            return []
        return [
            sum(values)
            for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
        ]

    def windowed_totals(
        self,
        results: SimulationResults,
        ids: Iterable[str],
        window: float,
        at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : SimulationResults
            Simulation results, with their positions.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Accumulator ids whose outputs are summed before windowing.
        window : float
            Length of one window on the axis.
        at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
            Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete
            window of the results (:func:`commol.window_ends`). Pass the
            observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a
            calibration used.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One increment per window.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        ValueError
            If `window` is not positive, or the results have no value at the
            end or the start of a requested window.
        """
        return windowed_totals(
            self.total_series(results, ids), results.positions, window, at
        )

        None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

    """
    if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
        raise TypeError(
            f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
            f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
            "holds the structure of its kind, such as a CompartmentalStructure."
        )
    logging.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
    self.model_definition: Model = model
    self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())

def run(self, num_steps: int) -> SimulationResults:
    """
    Runs the simulation from the initial state on its default grid.

    Every call starts at position 0 with the current ``model_definition``,
    so two calls with the same model give the same result. To continue a
    run, call ``simulation.engine.step()``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    num_steps : int
        The number of steps: the results hold the positions
        ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulationResults
        One value per position for each output, and the positions.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a parameter or initial condition has no value.
    """
    self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
    self._sync_engine()
    self._engine.reset()
    logging.info(f"Running simulation for {num_steps} steps.")
    start = time.time()
    positions, rows = self._engine.run(num_steps)
    logging.info(f"Simulation complete. It took {time.time() - start} seconds.")
    return SimulationResults.from_rows(positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows)

def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
    """
    Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

    The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
    (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for a compartmental model, by
    bin and accumulator.

    Raises

    KeyError

def total_series(
    self,
    results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
    ids: Iterable[str],
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
        Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
    ids : Iterable[str]
        Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One value per position of `results`.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
        output is missing from `results`.
    """
    names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
    missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
    if not names:
        return []
    return [
        sum(values)
        for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
    ]

class SimulationResults(dict[str, list[float]]):
    """
    Values of every output at each position on the axis.

    A ``dict`` from output name to one value per position, so
    ``results["A"]``, ``json.dumps(results)`` and
    ``pandas.DataFrame(results)`` work as for any mapping. The positions the
    values were read at are in :attr:`positions`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, ascending. ``results[name][i]`` is the value of
        ``name`` at ``positions[i]``.
    """

    positions: list[float]

    def __init__(
        self,
        positions: Iterable[float],
        values: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Results at the given positions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Iterable[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        values : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None, optional
            One value per position for each output.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an output does not have one value per position.
        """
        super().__init__(
            {name: list(series) for name, series in (values or {}).items()}
        )
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        for name, series in self.items():
            if len(series) != len(self.positions):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Output '{name}' has {len(series)} values for "
                    f"{len(self.positions)} positions."
                )

    @classmethod
    def from_rows(
        cls,
        positions: Sequence[float],
        names: Sequence[str],
        rows: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
    ) -> "SimulationResults":
        """
        Results from one row of output values per position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        names : Sequence[str]
            Output names, in the order of each row.
        rows : Sequence[Sequence[float]]
            One row per position.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series per output name.
        """
        columns = list(zip(*rows)) if rows else [() for _ in names]
        return cls(positions, dict(zip(names, columns, strict=True)))

    def rows(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        Every output at each position, one row per position.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            ``rows()[i][j]`` is the value of the ``j``-th output, in key order
            (the order of ``Simulation.simulation_outputs``), at
            ``positions[i]``.
        """
        return [list(row) for row in zip(*self.values())] if self else []

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The positions and the values."""
        return f"SimulationResults(positions={self.positions!r}, {dict.__repr__(self)})"

def window_index(at: float, window: float) -> int:
    """
    Window a position belongs to.

    The exact inverse of :func:`window_end`, and the containing window for
    any position in between: ``max(ceil(at / window) - 1, 0)``. Position 0
    belongs to window 0. :func:`commol.api.reporting.observed_report` places
    each observation with this rule.

    Parameters
    ----------
    at : float
        A position on the axis.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Zero-based window index.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive or `at` is negative.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    if not at >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"at must not be negative, got {at}.")
    return max(math.ceil(_windows_in(at, window)) - 1, 0)

def window_ends(window: float, end: float) -> list[float]:
    """
    Positions closing each complete window up to a position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    end : float
        Last position covered, such as the last position of a run.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        ``window``, ``2 * window``, ... up to `end`. A trailing partial window
        is not included.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    count = math.floor(_windows_in(end, window)) if end > 0 else 0
    return [window_end(index, window) for index in range(count)]

def windowed_totals(
    series: Sequence[float],
    positions: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Amount a cumulative series gained over each window.

    Each value is the series at the end of the window minus the series at its
    start, ``at - window``: the same quantity a calibration compares an
    observation against when that observation sets ``window``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : Sequence[float]
        A cumulative series, one value per position.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions of the series, ascending, such as
        ``SimulationResults.positions``.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
        Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete window of
        the series (:func:`window_ends`). Pass the observation positions to
        reproduce exactly the values a calibration used.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One increment per requested position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive, a window starts before position 0, or the
        series has no value at the end or the start of a requested window.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    ends = (
        window_ends(window, positions[-1] if positions else 0.0)
        if at is None
        else list(at)
    )

    totals = []
    for end in ends:
        start = end - window
        if start < -POSITION_TOLERANCE * max(abs(end), 1.0):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Position {end} has no complete window of {window} before it."
            )
        totals.append(
            series[index_at(positions, end)]
            - series[index_at(positions, max(start, 0.0))]
        )
    return totals

docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Physical duration of one simulation step.

A model is defined purely in steps. Attaching a duration to a step makes it possible to express periods in physical units, and to convert durations and probabilities into the per-step rates a transition expects.

Units up to a week have a fixed length and are provided directly. Months and years vary in length and have no single definition in step terms; give them as an explicit number of days.

Warnings

rate_from_mean_duration and rate_from_probability return per-step probabilities for a DifferenceEquations model. A DifferentialEquations model needs a continuous rate instead: 1 / duration for a mean duration, and -ln(1 - p) / period for a probability p over a period (both in steps).

Name Type Description step_seconds float

Duration represented by one simulation step, in seconds.

Source code in commol/api/time_scale.py 
class TimeScale(BaseModel):
    """
    Physical duration of one simulation step.

    A model is defined purely in steps. Attaching a duration to a step makes it
    possible to express periods in physical units, and to convert durations and
    probabilities into the per-step rates a transition expects.

    Units up to a week have a fixed length and are provided directly. Months
    and years vary in length and have no single definition in step terms; give
    them as an explicit number of days.

    Warnings
    --------
    `rate_from_mean_duration` and `rate_from_probability` return per-step
    probabilities for a DifferenceEquations model. A DifferentialEquations
    model needs a continuous rate instead: ``1 / duration`` for a mean
    duration, and ``-ln(1 - p) / period`` for a probability ``p`` over a
    period (both in steps).

    Attributes
    ----------
    step_seconds : float
        Duration represented by one simulation step, in seconds.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    step_seconds: float = Field(
        gt=0.0, description="Duration of one simulation step, in seconds."
    )

    @classmethod
    def from_step_unit(cls, unit: str) -> "TimeScale":
        """
        Time scale whose step lasts one `unit`, such as ``"day"`` or ``"h"``.

        The axis of a model is its independent variable and need not be time
        (``step_unit="meter"``, for example); a time scale applies only when it
        is time.

        Parameters
        ----------
        unit : str
            Step unit of a model, of dimension time.

        Returns
        -------
        TimeScale
            A scale with ``step_seconds`` equal to one `unit`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `unit` is not a unit of time; the message names it.
        """
        from commol.utils.equations import ureg

        try:
            quantity = ureg.Quantity(1.0, unit)
        except Exception as error:
            raise ValueError(f"'{unit}' is not a unit: {error}") from error
        if quantity.dimensionality != ureg.second.dimensionality:
            raise ValueError(
                f"A TimeScale needs a step unit of time; '{unit}' has dimension "
                f"{quantity.dimensionality}. A model whose axis is not time has "
                f"no time scale."
            )
        return cls(step_seconds=float(quantity.to("second").magnitude))

    def steps_from_seconds(self, seconds: float) -> int:
        """
        Number of steps spanning a duration.

        Parameters
        ----------
        seconds : float
            Duration to convert.

        Returns
        -------
        int
            Steps spanning that duration.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the duration is not a whole number of steps.
        """
        steps = seconds / self.step_seconds
        rounded = round(steps)
        if not math.isclose(steps, rounded, rel_tol=0.0, abs_tol=1e-9):
            raise ValueError(
                f"A step of {self.step_seconds} seconds does not divide "
                f"{seconds} seconds into a whole number of steps (got {steps})."
            )
        return int(rounded)

    def steps_from_minutes(self, minutes: float) -> int:
        """Number of steps spanning `minutes` minutes."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(minutes * SECONDS_PER_MINUTE)

    def steps_from_hours(self, hours: float) -> int:
        """Number of steps spanning `hours` hours."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(hours * SECONDS_PER_HOUR)

    def steps_from_days(self, days: float) -> int:
        """Number of steps spanning `days` days."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(days * SECONDS_PER_DAY)

    def steps_from_weeks(self, weeks: float) -> int:
        """Number of steps spanning `weeks` weeks."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(weeks * SECONDS_PER_WEEK)

    @property
    def steps_per_hour(self) -> int:
        """Steps in one hour."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(SECONDS_PER_HOUR)

    @property
    def steps_per_day(self) -> int:
        """Steps in one day."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(SECONDS_PER_DAY)

    @property
    def steps_per_week(self) -> int:
        """Steps in one week."""
        return self.steps_from_seconds(SECONDS_PER_WEEK)

    def rate_from_mean_duration(self, duration_seconds: float) -> float:
        """
        Per-step rate of leaving a state with a given mean residence time.

        Returns ``1 - exp(-step_seconds / duration_seconds)``, the probability
        that an exponential process of that mean duration fires within one
        step.

        This is a rate for a DifferenceEquations model only. A
        DifferentialEquations model needs the continuous rate
        ``step_seconds / duration_seconds``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        duration_seconds : float
            Mean time spent in the state, in seconds.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Per-step rate, between 0 and 1.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `duration_seconds` is not positive.
        """
        if duration_seconds <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"duration_seconds must be positive, got {duration_seconds}."
            )
        return 1.0 - math.exp(-self.step_seconds / duration_seconds)

    def rate_from_probability(self, probability: float, period_steps: int) -> float:
        """
        Per-step rate equivalent to a probability over a longer period.

        Returns ``1 - (1 - probability) ** (1 / period_steps)``, the per-step
        rate that accumulates to `probability` over `period_steps` steps.

        This is a rate for a DifferenceEquations model only. A
        DifferentialEquations model needs the continuous rate
        ``-ln(1 - probability) / period_steps``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        probability : float
            Probability of the event over the whole period, between 0 and 1.
        period_steps : int
            Length of the period, in steps.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Per-step rate, between 0 and 1.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `probability` is outside [0, 1], or `period_steps` is not
            positive.
        """
        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"probability must be between 0 and 1, got {probability}.")
        if period_steps <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"period_steps must be positive, got {period_steps}.")
        return 1.0 - (1.0 - probability) ** (1.0 / period_steps)

docs.title: Codebase Guide
docs.text:
Back to Home

This guide helps you find the right code before you change Commol. It is an index for maintainers and AI agents, not an API reference: for the public API, see the User Guide and the API Reference.

These pages describe develop

The dev version of this site is built from develop and may describe unreleased code. The latest version is built from main.

docs.title: Who this is for
docs.text: Reader Use this guide to New maintainer Build the mental model before you touch files. Contributor Find the module that owns a behavior. Reviewer Check that a pull request changes the right layer. AI agent Start from AGENTS.md, then read these pages by path.

docs.title: 90-second mental model
docs.text:
Commol has three layers. The user writes a model in Python. Python validates it and serializes it to JSON. The Rust engine builds and runs it.

User code
  |
  v
py-commol/commol/api/        ModelBuilder, Simulation, Calibrator, reports
  |
  v
py-commol/commol/context/    Pydantic model: validation and serialization
  |
  |  Model.model_dump_json()
  v
py-commol/src/               PyO3 bindings (module commol.commol_rs._commol_rs)
  |
  v
crates/commol-core/          model types, expressions (Cranelift JIT), SimulationEngine trait
crates/commol-model/         expansion, initial state, flow planning, rates, derivatives
crates/commol-difference/    the discrete step: X += derivatives
crates/commol-differential/  the ODE engine: diffsol integrates derivatives
crates/commol-calibration/   loss, optimizers (argmin fork), ensembles

Golden rule: the Rust engine is the single source of truth. When Python needs to know how the engine expands, initializes, plans or simulates a model, it asks the engine through a binding. It never re-implements the rule.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

How code, comments, documentation and commits are written in Commol. The tools check some of these rules. The rest depend on the author and the reviewer.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Area Rule Checked by Python style Ruff, line length 88 ruff check, ruff format (pre-commit, CI) Python types Annotations on every signature; never Any ty check (pre-commit, CI) Python dead code No unused code; a name used only in a string annotation goes in py-commol/.vulture_allowlist.py vulture (pre-commit, CI) Rust style cargo fmt; no Clippy warnings pre-commit, CI (-D warnings) Rust docs Every public item documented (missing_docs); no broken doc links clippy and cargo doc (CI) Docstrings NumPy style on every public module, class, function and argument ruff rules D1 and D417 (pre-commit, CI) Comments Describe the code as it is Review Documentation Mandatory with every change: definition of done CI and review Doc examples Abstract names; every block runs pytest -m docs (CI) and review Tests One package per guide page; shared factories; every test checks a result Review; pytest 10 deprecations fail the run (filterwarnings) Commits type(scope): description Review

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
• Every function and method signature has type hints. Never use Any: use a precise type, a TypeVar, a Protocol or a union.
  • Public functions and methods have a NumPy-style docstring: a one-line summary, then Parameters, Returns and Raises as needed. Private helpers may use a one-line docstring.
  • Context data structures are Pydantic v2 models.
  • ModelBuilder methods return Self, so calls chain.
  • Log with the standard logging module.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
• Edition 2024.
  • Public items have rustdoc comments, and a new module starts with a //! summary.
  • Hot paths avoid allocation: reuse buffers, access by index, keep evaluation contexts alive.

docs.title: Comments and docstrings
docs.text:
Describe the code as it is now. Never describe how it came to be.

Do not write Write instead "This replaces the old prefix matching" "Matches compartments by label." "Previously this was computed in Python" Nothing: the history is in git. "This is what makes calibration work" The rule the caller must satisfy. "Kept in sync with builder.rs" A test that fails when they differ.

Design reasons and invariants that cross components go to Design decisions, not to the source.

docs.title: Documentation definition of done
docs.text:
Mandatory

Every change to this repository ships with the documentation it needs, in the agreed format and at the agreed quality. A change without it is not done, and its pull request is not merged. This applies to people and to agents, to features, fixes, refactors, dependency updates and CI changes.

docs.title: 1. Update the docs the change affects
docs.text:
If the change… Update Adds or changes a public Python name, argument, default or error Its docstring; a path entry in docs/api/ for a new name in commol.__all__; the guide page that uses it Changes model behavior (expansion, rates, initial conditions, simulation) The guide page in docs/guide/; Model structure if a type changes Changes calibration or ensembles guide/calibration.md or guide/probabilistic-calibration.md Changes an expression function or variable guide/mathematical-expressions.md Moves code, adds a module, or changes who owns what Repository map; AGENTS.md if a "If you need to…" row changes Adds or changes a rule that is not obvious from the code Design decisions, with the test that guards it Changes a workflow, a command, CI or the release AGENTS.md; docs/development/ Is visible to users docs/about/changelog.md, under [Unreleased] Adds or changes a public Rust item Its rustdoc comment

When in doubt, search docs/ and AGENTS.md for the changed name and update every match.

docs.title: 2. Use the agreed format
docs.text:
Pages

  • One page, one job. The title says the outcome.
  • Start with one paragraph (what it is, who it is for), then a quick path, then details, then a checklist or the next step.
  • Prefer tables, checklists and short sections to long prose.
  • Start every page with a link back to its index, and end it with previous/next links when it belongs to a sequence.

Text

  • Simple technical English: short sentences, one idea per sentence, active voice, the answer first.
  • Every claim about the code names the file, function or test behind it.
  • Describe the present. History belongs in git and in the changelog.

Examples

  • Use abstract names only: bins A, B, C; categories group1, cat1; parameters k1, alpha. No names from epidemiology, chemistry or any other field.
  • Every Python block runs, top to bottom within its page, in one namespace and from a temporary directory (py-commol/tests/docs/test_examples.py). Define what a block needs in an earlier block of the same page.

  • A block that cannot run alone (a signature, a fragment) is marked on the line just before its fence, with a reason:

    <!-- doc-test: skip: shows only the signature -->

Use the marker only when the block cannot run; never to hide a failing example.

Code documentation

  • Python: a NumPy-style docstring on every public function, method and class (Parameters, Returns, Raises).
  • Rust: a rustdoc comment on every public item; a //! summary at the top of every new module.
  • Comments follow Comments and docstrings.

docs.title: 3. Pass the quality checks
docs.text:
Check Command Enforced by The site builds with no broken internal link or anchor mkdocs build --strict (with validation: in mkdocs.yaml) CI (Documentation) External links answer lychee (.github/workflows/links.yaml) CI on documentation changes, weekly; not a required check The documentation examples run pytest -m docs (from py-commol/) CI (Code Quality) Every name in commol.__all__ has an API entry (… under docs/api/) pytest -m docs (tests/docs/test_reference.py) CI (Code Quality) Public Python modules, classes, functions and arguments have docstrings ruff check . (rules D1, D417, NumPy convention) pre-commit, CI Public Rust items have docs, without broken links #![warn(missing_docs)] in every crate (denied by clippy -D warnings); RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc pre-commit (clippy), CI The table in step 1 is complete for this change — Pull request checklist and review The format in step 2 is followed — Review

The pull request template repeats this checklist. A reviewer who finds a gap asks for it before approving.

docs.title: Writing for people and agents
docs.text:
The same pages serve both. An agent reads the Markdown source by path, so:

  • keep each page self-contained, with its links;
  • name files and functions exactly, in code format;
  • put the rule before the explanation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Where a Python test goes, how it builds its model, and what it must check. The tests live in py-commol/tests/.

docs.title: Layout: one package per guide page
docs.text:
A test goes in the package of the guide page that documents the behavior it checks, so "where is the test of X" has the same answer as "where is the guide of X". A pure-Python helper (utils/security.py, api/time_scale.py, api/probabilistic/) goes in the package of its feature. The exceptions are reference_models/, which checks published models across features (see Reference models), and model_kinds/, which runs a model kind that is not compartmental through every generic layer.

Package Tests of Guide page building/ The builder, parameters, stratifications, reserved names, save and load Building Models transitions/ Flows, $compartment, stratified rates, impulses Transitions rates/ Formulas, functions, variables, expression security Mathematical Expressions axis_patterns/ AxisPattern formulas, runs and schedules Axis Patterns initial_conditions/ Bin, stratification and compartment fractions; the initial state Building Models simulation/ Runs, run_at, results and their positions, differential models, outputs, the window grid and windowed totals, TimeScale Running Simulations units/ Unit checks and print_equations Units and Equations calibration/ One file per calibration page: test_problem.py, test_optimizers.py, test_constraints.py, test_observations.py, test_initial_conditions.py, test_write_back.py Model Calibration and its sub-pages probabilistic/ Ensembles, their selection and intervals Probabilistic Calibration reporting/ Reports Reports plotting/ SimulationPlotter Running Simulations docs/ The documentation examples and the API coverage (marker docs) — reference_models/ Published models against their stated results, one module per model family — (across features) model_kinds/ The test model kind (support/kinds.py) through a simulation, a calibration, a report and a plot; the check that an engine runs its kind. It needs the extension built with --features test-kind. — (across features; Design decisions) support/ No tests: the code the tests share —

Keep a test module under about 600 lines. When it grows past that, split it by topic inside its package.

docs.title: Models: use the factories
docs.text:
• Build models with the factories of tests/support/models.py: sir_builder, seir_builder and a_to_b_builder, and the special models override_builder, shared_category_builder and conditional_pathway_builder. A keyword overrides one part of the default model, so a test names only what it changes. build builds for difference equations; build_ode builds for differential equations, with the tight solver settings TIGHT by default; run builds and simulates.
  • Build a model by hand only when one test needs it and no factory keyword expresses it. A model that a second file needs goes to support/.
  • Fixtures: sir_model and sir_simulation (tests/conftest.py); truth and truth_run (tests/calibration/conftest.py). A fixture is function-scoped unless its cost is measured; a wider scope never holds an object a test can change. A class-scoped fixture is never an instance method (removed in pytest 10).

docs.title: Every test checks a result
docs.text:
A test compares a result with an oracle:

Oracle Example A value computed by hand in the test reference_run (tests/support/reference.py) evaluates the flows in plain Python, as the engine does: every flow from the state at the start of the step, no clamping. tests/rates/test_formulas.py compares whole trajectories with it. An analytic value A death rate d on every bin gives total(t) = total(0) (1 - d)^t (tests/transitions/test_compartment_placeholder.py). An invariant A total that the model keeps (assert_total_conserved); two paths that must agree, such as a bin id and the explicit sum of its compartments. What a stated result predicts about a run tests/support/oracles.py: final_size solves the final size relation, assert_threshold checks that an infection grows at a reproduction number of 1.05 and dies out at 0.95, settled reads a limit once doubling the horizon no longer moves it.

"It runs" is not a result. A test whose only check is that no exception occurs is allowed only when the exception is its subject, such as a validator that accepts a valid input.

docs.title: Tolerances
docs.text:
• assert_close(actual, expected, rel=…, abs=…) (tests/support/assertions.py) needs a stated tolerance, and reports the key and the index of the first difference.
  • ENGINE_REL = 1e-9 compares the engine with a hand computation of the same arithmetic: only the order of the floating-point operations differs.
  • ODE_REL = 1e-6 compares a differential model with a closed form, a final size or an equilibrium. flow_model solves with FINE (TIGHT with atol = 1e-12), so the error of a value near zero stays below its own size.
  • pytest.approx with its default (relative 1e-6) suits a single value computed by hand.
  • An optimizer result states the tolerance its convergence allows, for example abs=1e-5 for Nelder-Mead on noise-free data.

docs.title: Reference models
docs.text:
tests/reference_models/ shows that commol can state published models and computes their stated results. A module holds one model family and is named after its epidemiology (test_pulse_vaccination.py); a test checks one stated result (test_the_fixed_point_starts_the_periodic_orbit).

  • Attribution. The module docstring has a References section in the NumPy format with the original papers of the model and of its parameter values (authors, year, title, journal, DOI). A value or a result taken from a paper cites it in a comment next to the value. A model with no primary source is not added.
  • Independent oracle. The expected value comes from the stated result, computed with math or numpy: a closed form, a root of the final size relation, a spectral radius. A test never compares commol with commol. A quantity that commol does not output, such as a reproduction number, is checked through what it predicts about a run (tests/support/oracles.py).
  • Equations. To check that a model has the stated equations, increments reads its right-hand side at one state: a difference-equation step adds the flows of the state it starts from, and both engines compile the same flows.
  • Tolerances. ENGINE_REL for a discrete model, ODE_REL for a differential one; an asymptotic result is read with settled, and the test states its horizon.
  • Gaps. A model that commol cannot state, or computes wrong, gets a test marked xfail(strict=True, reason="F<n>: …") that names a finding of the task that added it, so a fix makes the test pass and forces the marker out.

To add a test, write the model with Flow and flow_model (tests/support/flows.py) from the initial value of each bin, compute the stated result in the test, and cite the papers.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commits: <type>(<scope>): <description>.

  • The scope is required.
  • The description is one short phrase, with no period.
  • No body, and no co-author or AI attribution lines.
  • Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore.
feat(transitions): add time-varying rates
fix(simulation): correct the total of a subgroup
docs(codebase): add repository map

See Development workflow for branches and merge methods.
