docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

The rules on this page are not obvious from the code, and breaking one gives results that are wrong but look correct. Each rule names where it lives and the test that guards it. Read the ones of your area before you change it.

Area Decisions Model kinds One interface for every kind, a model by composition Model structure Compartments, what they hold, stratification order, outputs, variable names Transitions and rates Rate semantics, stratified rates, formula parameters, JIT cache Initial conditions Subgroup totals, calibrated values Time Physical time, step unit, time inside a step, impulses, windowed observations Engines One right-hand side, solver Calibration Weights, Nelder-Mead bounds, simulations Results Confidence intervals, reports, model files Security Expressions

docs.title: One interface for every model kind
docs.text:
The layers that do not depend on how a model is built (Simulation, Calibrator, ProbabilisticCalibrator, the reports and SimulationPlotter) use only Model and the methods of ModelStructure (py-commol/commol/context/structure.py), and in Rust only the SimulationEngine trait (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs). What only a compartmental model has (bins, stratifications, initial conditions) is behind them: CompartmentalStructure (context/compartmental.py), and in Rust CompartmentalEngine and InitialConditionPlan (crates/commol-model/). A new kind, such as an agent network, is a new ModelStructure subclass with its engines in the list; nothing that exists changes.

Part Rule Why, against the alternative ModelStructure An abstract base class (Pydantic's metaclass derives from ABCMeta). A missing method fails when the object is made and names it; optional methods have a default. A typing.Protocol shows a missing method only under ty, or mid-run as an AttributeError, and gives no defaults. Engine kind Each entry of EngineType names the kind it runs. Model asks the list (check_kind) when it is made, and Engine::build asks it again; the error names the engine and both kinds. Without the check, a model of one kind reaches the engine of another and fails deep in its compilation. Values calibration sets parameter and factor are generic. Each kind declares the types of value of its own it accepts (ModelKind::value_types, which ModelStructure.calibration_value_types asks); the compartmental kind accepts initial_condition. The engine resolves and writes them (SimulationEngine::plan_values, apply_values). The calibration crate would know compartments, and a new kind could not calibrate values of its own without editing it. Report sections ModelStructure.report_sections adds the sections of a kind to applied_parameters_report (default: none); the compartmental kind adds initial_conditions. A check of the kind in reporting.py brings back a branch per kind. Expressions in constraints The engine names the values of an output row: output_names, state_outputs (their sum is total) and output_sums (a bin total, for a compartmental engine). The calibration would rebuild bin totals from compartment labels.

The test kind (tests/support/kinds.py, engine TestEngine in py-commol/src/test_kind.rs) is written only against the interface. The extension has it only when it is built with the cargo feature test-kind, as the tests and CI build it; a release build does not.

Guards: tests/model_kinds/ (a test model through a simulation, a calibration, a report and a plot; the kind check both ways), crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_model_values.rs (the calibration with an engine that is not compartmental: values through plan_values and apply_values, constraints through output_sums and state_outputs), py-commol/src/engine.rs::an_engine_rejects_a_model_of_another_kind, crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs::an_engine_rejects_a_model_of_another_kind.

docs.title: A model is a header, an engine and a structure
docs.text:
Model (Python context/model.py, Rust crates/commol-core/src/types/model.rs) is one class for every kind: name, description, version, step_unit, parameters, engine ({type, settings}) and structure, tagged in JSON by kind. In Python it is generic in its structure class: ModelBuilder.build returns Model[CompartmentalStructure], so model.structure.bins type-checks, and Model.from_json reads the class from the kind of the file. The engine is part of the model because it sets what a rate means. Transitions are held once, in the structure.

Inheritance (an abstract Model with a CompartmentalModel) gives direct access (model.bins) but two parallel hierarchies, of models and of builders, and the header repeated per kind; with composition, Simulation and Calibrator take one type.

Guards: crates/commol-core/src/types/model.rs (tests), tests/building/test_save_and_load.py, tests/model_kinds/test_interface.py::TestStructureInterface.

docs.title: Compartments are labels with a name
docs.text:
A compartment is a bin plus one category for each stratification that applies to it, in declaration order. Its name, {bin}_{category}_{category}…, is for display only. Its identity is its label: OutputLabels in crates/commol-model/src/labels.rs and CompartmentLayout in crates/commol-model/src/layout.rs.

Rule: never parse a compartment name or match it by prefix. Bin A and bin A_x both produce names that start with A_, and a conditional stratification gives some compartments fewer suffixes than others. Use CompartmentLayout::find or of_bin in Rust, and the labels that the engine queries return in Python.

docs.title: State, amount, total and subgroup total
docs.text:
The library names what the compartments hold without assuming individuals:

Term Meaning Where State The vector of the amount of every compartment CompartmentalEngine::state, Engine.state Amount The value of one compartment InitialCompartment.amount Total The sum of every compartment, accumulators excluded; the initial fractions are taken of it InitialConditions.total, the rate variable total (SPECIAL_VAR_TOTAL) Subgroup total The sum of the compartments with some categories subgroup_total, the rate variables total_<cat>… (SUBGROUP_TOTAL_PREFIX)

The total is a real number, finite and greater than 0, so a model of a count, a mass or a concentration can be stated. 0 is rejected: every fraction of it is zero, and the report divides by it (initial_state in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs, InitialConditions.validate_total).

Rule: use these four terms in code, docs and tests. AxisPattern takes a value, so "amount" means only the value of a compartment.

Why, against the alternatives:

Alternative Why not "population", "head count", N They assume individuals and an epidemiological convention (N = S + I + R). A reserved N takes a letter that other fields use for a bin, such as a nutrient. "mass" A unit, not a quantity of any unit. "stock" An economic term, new to the code. "content" Ambiguous in software. "size" Reads as a count, and clashes with the NSGA-II population_size. A function total(g1, t1) No reserved names, but the expression language has no text arguments (jit/ast.rs), so the parser, the JIT and the security check would change.

Guards: builder.rs tests a_real_total_starts_with_amounts_that_sum_to_it and a_total_that_is_not_finite_and_positive_is_a_build_error; tests/building/test_reserved_names.py::test_a_bin_named_n_builds_and_runs; tests/initial_conditions/test_bin_fractions.py::TestTotal.

docs.title: Stratification order is part of the model
docs.text:
expand in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs applies the stratifications in declaration order. A stratification with conditions only expands the compartments whose earlier categories satisfy all of them, so the result can be a non-uniform product. A condition may only reference a stratification declared before it (ModelBuilder.add_stratification checks this).

Rule: changing the order of add_stratification calls changes which compartments exist and what they are named.

docs.title: Outputs are resolved by label
docs.text:
CompartmentalStructure.outputs_by_source() maps each bin or accumulator id to its output names in engine order. It uses the engine expansion (expanded_outputs), so Simulation.outputs_for, group_outputs and total_series group outputs by label, not by name.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_outputs.py::TestOutputsBySource::test_expansion_matches_the_engine_output_names (order) and TestSourceIdSharingAPrefix (a bin and an accumulator that share a prefix).

docs.title: The engine owns the variable names
docs.text:
The engine sets one variable per expanded compartment and per subgroup total (total_<categories>, bin totals and partial bin totals). check_names in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs rejects a parameter id that is one of those names, a parameter, bin or accumulator id that is an engine variable (ENGINE_VARIABLES: total, step, t, pi, e), a bin whose compartments or bin totals read as a total_<categories> name (two sums would share one slot), and a total_… variable in a rate or a formula parameter that names no subgroup total. CompartmentalStructure.check_model calls it at build, and CompiledModel::try_from_model calls it again. subgroup_total_names lists the names; Python reads them through the binding commol_rs.model.subgroup_total_names (engine_state.subgroup_total_names) to check rates and give units.

Rule: never list these names in Python. Ask the engine.

Guards: builder.rs tests parameter_id_cannot_be_a_compartment_or_a_subgroup_total, subgroup_total_out_of_declaration_order_is_a_build_error and subgroup_total_names_follow_the_declaration_order, an_engine_variable_is_not_a_parameter_bin_or_accumulator_id and a_bin_name_that_reads_as_a_subgroup_total_is_rejected; tests/building/test_reserved_names.py; tests/rates/test_expressions.py::TestSubgroupTotals::test_every_name_the_engine_provides_is_accepted_in_a_rate.

docs.title: Absolute and per-capita rates
docs.text:
The flow planner (plan_transition_flows in crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs) decides for each flow whether the rate is absolute or per-capita:

Case Rate is Flow per step A stratified rate sets absolute As set — The rate references a compartment, a bin total, total or a total_… variable Absolute rate The transition has no source Absolute rate Otherwise Per-capita rate × source

A transition with several sources and a per-capita rate is rejected, because it has no single source to multiply. print_equations shows the planned flows, so a per-capita rate prints as k1 * A.

Guard: tests/transitions/test_flows.py.

docs.title: The most specific stratified rate wins
docs.text: For each compartment, the stratified rate whose conditions match it with the largest number of conditions wins (helpers.rs). On a tie, the first one in the list wins. If none matches, the transition's default rate applies. Building a model fails if a stratified rate matches no compartment that the transition starts from.

docs.title: Formula parameters are evaluated every step, in order
docs.text: Parameters with a formula are evaluated again at each step, in the order they were declared (simulation.rs). A formula can use the value of an earlier formula from the same step. Declare parameters in dependency order.

docs.title: Compiled expressions are cached globally
docs.text:
JIT_CACHE in crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/mod.rs maps each preprocessed formula to one compiled function for the life of the process. The same formula always runs the same machine code, so results are reproducible.

Rule: do not invalidate or bypass the cache.

docs.title: Subgroup totals compose down the condition chain
docs.text:
The fractions of a conditional stratification are relative to the subgroup that its conditions select, not to the total. Subgroup totals therefore multiply along the chain: total × fraction(group1) × fraction(cat1). InitialConditions.subgroup_total owns this; CompartmentalStructure.subgroup_total and CompartmentalStructure.get_conditioning_categories delegate to it.

Guard: tests/simulation/test_outputs.py::TestSubgroupTotal compares the result with the state the engine starts from.

docs.title: Calibrated initial conditions are applied in layers
docs.text:
InitialConditionPlan in crates/commol-model/src/initial_conditions.rs applies calibrated values in a fixed order: bins, category splits, exact compartments, and then the remainder named by CalibrationProblem.initial_condition_remainder. Both compartmental engines resolve and write initial conditions through it (SimulationEngine::plan_values and apply_values), and the calibration writes every value through the engine (ValueWriter in crates/commol-calibration/src/values.rs), so the objective, the predictions and the write-back (configured_engine, then the binding calibrated_initial_state) agree by construction. CompartmentalStructure.with_calibrated_values (context/_model/calibration_write_back.py) writes the values back as fractions, and pins as per-compartment overrides every compartment that the fractions cannot reproduce.

Guards: tests/calibration/test_write_back.py::TestApplyCalibrationParameters::test_applied_model_reproduces_the_loss_the_optimizer_scored; crates/commol-model/tests/initial_conditions.rs (the layers, the remainder and the targets of an id). See also Per-compartment initial conditions.

docs.title: Physical time is not in the model
docs.text:
A Model records no step length: rates are per step and periods are step counts. The axis of a model is its independent variable, whatever quantity it is (time is one case), so the engines never ask which dimension it has. Model.step_unit is optional and only the unit check reads it. TimeScale (api/time_scale.py) holds the length of a step of time and converts durations and probabilities; the window grid is in api/windows.py. Conversions raise when a period is not a whole number of steps, instead of rounding. Months and years are absent on purpose, because they have no fixed length in steps. TimeScale applies only when that variable is time: TimeScale.from_step_unit raises for a step unit that is not time.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_time_scale.py::TestFromStepUnit, tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestWindowGrid.

docs.title: One step unit in the unit check
docs.text:
The engine applies every flow once per step and converts no value between units. So UnitChecker._step_unit (context/_model/units.py) uses one step unit: the declared Model.step_unit, of any single dimension (check_step_unit), or else the one unit of time that the parameter units use (step when there is none). check_equation_units requires every flow to be equal to <bin unit>/<step unit>, and every impulse to <bin unit>, not only convertible to it (utils/equations.py, same_unit). Inference never takes a unit that is not time: a parameter in 1/(item·meter) may be a density, not a rate along the axis, so the check does not guess.

Rule: never accept a convertible unit as equal. 1/week and 1/day in one model would apply a weekly rate every day.

Guards: tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestStepUnit, tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestAxisUnit.

docs.title: Time inside a step
docs.text:
A differential model integrates in continuous time, but on [n, n + 1) its rates see step = n: t is continuous, step is the floor of t. A rate that reads step or a "pulse" series (and so AxisPattern.pulse, pulses, periodic) is therefore constant on its unit interval. When the right-hand side reads one of them (CompiledModel::depends_on_step), the engine ends a piece of integration at every integer, so each jump of the rate is the start of a piece (breakpoints in crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs).

A "step_function" or "linear" series reads t (SeriesParameter::evaluate), so it holds or interpolates from any position. The engine ends a piece at each of its points (CompiledModel::series_points), where the series jumps or bends. A difference engine reads t = step, so it gives the same values as before, and it rejects a point between integers.

A rate can also jump where t reaches a value it compares t with (t >= t_on, and so AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp). The compiler collects those values when they read only numbers, pi, e and parameters that do not change during a run (time_thresholds in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs), and the engine evaluates them with the current parameters and ends a piece there. Without that, an adaptive solver whose rate is 0 before a short window grows its step and steps over the window. A comparison with the state is a state event, which the engine does not detect.

On a piece [start, end) the right-hand side sees t no larger than the float just below end (RightHandSide::last_t). A Runge–Kutta step evaluates the right-hand side at the end of its interval; without the limit, a value that jumps at end would already act on the last step of the piece.

Whether an expression reads step comes from reads_variable, not from get_variables: get_variables leaves out the special variables, because it lists the variables a model must define.

Consequence: a per-capita pulse p moves p of its source in a difference model and 1 − e^(−p) in a differential model. An impulse moves p in both. The alternative, step = t, makes a pulse step == n true on a set of zero length, so it would never act.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_differential.py::TestTimeInsideAStep, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::a_pulse_rate_is_a_constant_rate_on_its_unit_interval, a_rate_reads_the_step_of_its_unit_interval, a_rate_that_switches_on_t_acts_only_on_its_window, a_linear_series_matches_the_integral_of_its_interpolant, a_step_function_series_holds_from_a_position_between_steps, crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs::a_comparison_of_t_with_a_fixed_value_is_a_threshold, tests/axis_patterns/test_pattern_runs.py::TestDifferentialIntegration.

docs.title: Impulses come before the flows of their step
docs.text:
At step n the state jumps first, then the flows of the step run from the new state, in both engines (CompiledModel::apply_impulses). Every jump of one step is computed from the state before any of them. The output at n shows the state after the jump. With the other order, the differential output at n would show the state before the jump and the difference output the state after it, so the two engines would disagree at the output steps. A difference model needs integer impulse steps; a differential model stops its integration at each impulse step and restarts from the new state, so diffsol needs no event.

Guards: tests/transitions/test_impulses.py::TestJump, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::an_impulse_moves_its_fraction_at_once_in_both_engines.

docs.title: Windowed observations
docs.text:
An observation at at with window = W is compared with output(at) - output(at - W), anchored at its own position. The Rust loss and windowed_totals (api/windows.py) must give the same number, and so must the ensemble statistics (StatisticsCalculator._member_window_value). Window w covers (w · W, (w + 1) · W]; window_index places a position with max(ceil(at / W) − 1, 0), and observed_report calls it.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss (the loss at the generating parameters is zero), tests/reporting/test_simulation_report.py::test_observed_report_places_each_observation_by_window_index and tests/probabilistic/test_calibrator.py::test_windowed_bands_are_taken_at_the_observation_positions.

docs.title: The engine owns positions
docs.text:
A position on the axis is an f64 in every engine call and a float in every public Python name (at); a length is window or period; a count of steps keeps num_steps. The SimulationEngine trait (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs) runs only at positions (run_at_positions_into_buffer); run(n) runs on the grid the engine builds, grid(n), and returns it. Each engine says which positions its model type accepts (check_position): a difference engine non-negative integers, a differential engine any finite, non-negative position. The engine checks every position where it receives it, and its message names the object that holds a rejected one: the observation or constraint (check_positions in crates/commol-calibration/src/calibration_problem.rs), the impulse transition or series parameter (DifferenceEquations::from_compiled).

Rule: Python passes positions on and shows the engine's message. It never checks whether a model type accepts a position.

Guards: crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_positions.rs, crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs::integer_positions_are_accepted_and_others_rejected, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::a_difference_engine_names_a_series_point_between_steps, tests/calibration/test_observations.py::TestPositionsAndTypology.

docs.title: Results carry their positions
docs.text:
Simulation.run and run_at return SimulationResults (api/results.py): a dict from output name to values, with the positions in positions and the rows in rows(). A dict keeps results["A"], json.dumps and pandas.DataFrame(results) working; a reserved key could clash with an output name. Windows, reports, plots and ensemble statistics read a value at a position (index_at, which matches within a relative 1e-9), never at a list index, so a model type that reports between integers fits them. The ensemble trajectories hold StatisticsCalculator.positions: the unit grid and every observation position and window start.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_runs.py::TestResults, tests/reporting/test_simulation_report.py::TestNonIntegerPositions, tests/plotting/test_plotter.py::TestDifferentialModel, tests/probabilistic/test_differential.py.

docs.title: One list of engines
docs.text:
EngineType (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs) is the one list of model types. An entry is an engine, named by its type (DifferenceEquations, DifferentialEquations), and it names the model kind it runs (today only compartmental). Each entry validates its settings and says the form of its equations and the meaning of a rate (per_step or continuous). Engine::build (py-commol/src/engine.rs) builds the engine of an entry. A model holds its engine and the settings of that engine, Model.engine = {type, settings}, because the engine sets what a rate means, so a saved model reproduces its runs.

Python asks the list (commol_rs.engine.EngineType): it builds the engine, prints the left-hand side of an equation and checks settings through it, and never branches on an engine name. It keeps the names of the compartmental engines only as the Literal CompartmentalEngineType (context/engine.py), for static typing and completion of ModelBuilder.build; a test checks that it equals the compartmental entries of the list. ModelEngine.type is a str that the list checks, so a model can name an engine of any kind. Generating the Literal from Rust would need a code-generation step for two names; the test catches the same drift. The entry names its model kind, so another kind (for example an agent network) adds entries, not a second meaning of the type; see One interface for every model kind.

The builder takes the engine and its settings where it chooses the engine, build(engine, settings=None), so one builder builds a model for each engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both.

Guards: crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs (tests), py-commol/src/engine.rs::every_entry_builds_its_engine_and_runs, tests/building/test_engine.py.

docs.title: One right-hand side, two engines
docs.text:
CompiledModel::derivatives (crates/commol-model/src/system.rs) computes every flow from one snapshot of the state: it is the right-hand side dX/dt = Σ flows. The difference engine adds it once per step (X(n + 1) = X(n) + derivatives(n, X(n))); the differential engine integrates it. Neither engine has flow logic of its own, so both run the same model. Accumulators are state components: a difference step adds the counted flows, a differential engine integrates them.

Guard: crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs::one_step_adds_the_derivatives_exactly.

docs.title: The solver is diffsol
docs.text:
The differential engine keeps no numerical method of its own: diffsol (pinned to a minor version, ~0.17.1) solves the system with tsit45 or bdf. bdf takes the Jacobian-vector product by finite differences (RightHandSide::jac_mul), one extra right-hand-side evaluation, because a symbolic derivative of every rate would be new numerical code. The matrix is dense (nalgebra) below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and sparse (faer) from there; diffsol finds the sparse pattern by passing NaN through J·v. Solver settings live in the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces a run.

Guards: crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs (bdf_solves_a_stiff_model_within_the_tolerance, a_large_stiff_model_uses_the_sparse_path).

docs.title: One meaning of an observation weight
docs.text:
LossConfig::term and LossConfig::finish in crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs compute every loss: sse is Σ w·r², rmse is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w), mae is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. The optimizer (calibration_problem.rs), the ensemble central loss (probabilistic/ensemble/mod.rs) and Python (central_fit_loss, through LossConfig.aggregate) all call them.

Rule: never write a loss formula elsewhere. The central-fit gate compares the ensemble loss with the optimizer loss, so both must measure the same way.

Guards: types.rs loss_tests; ensemble::tests::central_loss_uses_observation_weights_in_every_metric; tests/probabilistic/test_selection.py::test_central_fit_loss_uses_weights_in_every_metric.

docs.title: Nelder-Mead searches inside the bounds
docs.text:
The objective clamps values to their bounds, so the loss is flat outside them, and a simplex that crosses a bound collapses there. Nelder-Mead therefore searches an unbounded u and scores x = lo + (hi − lo)·(sin u + 1)/2 (SineTransform and BoundedProblem in optimization.rs). Its evaluations and its result are recorded in x. converged is true only for SolverConverged and TargetCostReached (optimization::converged).

Rule: report and record values in x, never in u. Every optimizer run, the verbose one included, goes through optimize_observed.

Guards: optimization::tests; tests/calibration/test_optimizers.py.

docs.title: A Simulation follows its model
docs.text:
Simulation keeps the JSON its engine was built from. run, engine and simulation_outputs compare it with model_dump_json() and rebuild the engine when it differs (Simulation._sync_engine), and run resets the engine first. Calibrator takes simulation.engine when it is created, so the check is in the property, not only in run.

Guard: tests/simulation/test_runs.py.

docs.title: One confidence-interval convention
docs.text:
ci_percentiles (api/probabilistic/intervals.py) is the only place that turns a confidence level into percentiles. member_statistics reduces each ensemble member to the quantity of interest first, and then takes percentiles across members. Taking percentiles first gives a band that describes no member.

Rule: every new interval goes through these two functions.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
api/reporting.py returns blocks of data, not documents: simulation_report (observed values, series, accumulators) and applied_parameters_report (calibrated parameters, and the sections of the model kind: initial_conditions for a compartmental model).

  • A single run and an ensemble differ only at the leaves (ReportLeaf).
  • The key order of each entry is part of the contract, because it changes saved JSON files.
  • Labels and summary figures belong to the caller, because they carry domain vocabulary.

Guard: tests/reporting/.

docs.title: Model files are written in full
docs.text: Model.to_json writes every field, nulls included. Dropping nulls is not round-trip safe: an uncalibrated Parameter.value or BinFraction.fraction would lose a required key and fail to reload. render_json (context/_model/serialization.py) keeps files readable by writing long numeric arrays on one line. It is internal on purpose: an output format in the public API becomes a compatibility promise.

docs.title: Public models forbid unknown fields
docs.text:
Every public Pydantic class sets model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid"). An unknown field, such as a misspelt or an old name (window_steps), raises a ValidationError that names it, instead of being dropped with no error.

Guard: tests/building/test_unknown_fields.py.

docs.title: Every user expression is validated
docs.text:
Rate expressions (context/dynamics.py) and calibration constraints (context/calibration.py) pass through validate_expression_security (utils/security.py) before they reach the engine. The limits are in SecurityConfig.

Rule: any new field that accepts an expression must call it.

docs.title: Maintainer Playbook
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Use this page before you make or review a change. It turns the Repository map and the Design decisions into checklists.

docs.title: Every change
docs.text:
1. Read the user-facing page of the feature in the User Guide.
  2. Find the owner in the Repository map.
  3. Read the tests next to that code before you change it.
  4. Make the change in the narrowest owner.
  5. Run both test suites (see AGENTS.md).
  6. Update the documentation as the mandatory definition of done requires.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• Do not duplicate an engine rule in Python. Add a binding instead, and call it from context/_model/engine_state.py.
  • Do not identify compartments by name. Use labels (see Compartments are labels).
  • Do not drop invalid input silently. Reject it with a message that names the transition, compartment or parameter.
  • Do not change saved formats by accident. Model JSON and report key order are part of the contract.
  • Do not trust odd/ as specification. It records past work; the code and this guide describe the present.

docs.title: Model structure (bins, stratifications, accumulators)
docs.text:
• [ ] Change the Rust type in crates/commol-core/src/types/ and the Pydantic model in py-commol/commol/context/ together.
  • [ ] Update the PyO3 binding and _commol_rs.pyi if the type crosses the boundary.
  • [ ] Update expansion in builder.rs (expand) if compartments change.
  • [ ] Check that test_expansion_matches_the_engine_output_names still passes.
  • [ ] Update Building models and Model structure.

docs.title: Transitions and rates
docs.text:
• [ ] Plan the flows in flows.rs; reject what cannot be simulated.
  • [ ] Check the rate semantics.
  • [ ] Add a case to tests/transitions/test_flows.py, and check print_equations.
  • [ ] Update Building models.

docs.title: Expressions (functions, variables)
docs.text:
• [ ] Change crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/, including the JIT (jit/) and its tests.
  • [ ] Add a new function to SAFE_FUNCTIONS in utils/security.py.
  • [ ] Update Mathematical expressions.

docs.title: Initial conditions
docs.text:
• [ ] Change the Pydantic validation in context/initial_conditions.py and the engine rule in builder.rs (initial_state).
  • [ ] Check that CompartmentalStructure.initial_state() reports the new state.
  • [ ] If calibration can set it, update initial_conditions.rs in commol-model (InitialConditionPlan) and the write-back (context/_model/calibration_write_back.py).
  • [ ] Check that test_applied_model_reproduces_the_loss_the_optimizer_scored still passes.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep the loss and the constraints in calibration_problem.rs, and use only SimulationEngine there: a rule of one model kind goes behind plan_values, apply_values or output_sums of its engines.
  • [ ] Convert new options in api/calibrator.py and api/probabilistic/calibration_runner.py.
  • [ ] Check that tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss still passes if the loss changes.
  • [ ] Update Calibration and, for ensembles, Probabilistic calibration.

docs.title: Model type (engine)
docs.text:
To add an engine to the list:

  • [ ] Add the entry to EngineType in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs and to ALL. The compiler then names every match to complete in that file: its name, its model kind, its settings (EngineSettings, parsed and validated with deny_unknown_fields), the left-hand side of its equations and the meaning of a rate.
  • [ ] Write the engine in its own crate and implement SimulationEngine (for a compartmental engine, also CompartmentalEngine from commol-model); try_from_model rejects a model of another engine.
  • [ ] Add a variant to Engine in py-commol/src/engine.rs: its arm in build, engine_type, dispatch!, plan_values and apply_values (and compartmental! for a compartmental engine). Add the crate to py-commol/Cargo.toml.
  • [ ] For a compartmental engine, add the name to the CompartmentalEngineType Literal in context/engine.py; if the engine has settings, add their Pydantic class to EngineSettings.
  • [ ] Run the tests of crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs, py-commol/src/engine.rs and tests/building/test_engine.py; they run every entry of the list.
  • [ ] Say what a rate means for it in the guides, and add it to Model structure and Running simulations.

docs.title: Model kind
docs.text:
To add a kind of model, such as an agent network (see One interface for every model kind):

  • [ ] Add the kind to ModelKind in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs and to its ALL: its name and the types of value calibration may set (value_types).
  • [ ] Add the structure of the kind to crates/commol-core/src/types/ and a variant to ModelStructure (structure.rs). The compiler names every match to complete, such as Model::compartmental.
  • [ ] Add its engines to the list, as in Model type (engine); each names the new kind. Each engine implements SimulationEngine: plan_values and apply_values resolve and write the values of the kind, and state_outputs and output_sums name what an expression reads.
  • [ ] Add a variant to EngineValuePlan in py-commol/src/engine.rs.
  • [ ] Write a ModelStructure subclass in py-commol/commol/context/, with kind as a Literal default. Implement check_model and outputs_by_source; override series_label, uncalibrated_values, with_calibrated_values, report_sections, print_equations and check_unit_consistency when the kind has them. Import the module in context/__init__.py, so Model.from_json reads the kind.
  • [ ] Give the kind a builder in api/ that returns Model[YourStructure]. Do not change Simulation, Calibrator, the reports or the plotter: if one of them needs something of the kind, add a method to ModelStructure with a default.
  • [ ] Copy the tests of tests/model_kinds/ for the new kind, and run the Rust and Python suites.
  • [ ] Add the kind to Model structure, the Mental model and a guide page.

docs.title: PyO3 bindings
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep logic out of py-commol/src/: convert types and call the crate.
  • [ ] Update _commol_rs.pyi.
  • [ ] Rebuild with maturin develop --release --features test-kind before you run pytest: the tests need the test model kind.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep the key order of existing entries.
  • [ ] Put a section that only one model kind has in its ModelStructure.report_sections, not in api/reporting.py.
  • [ ] Use member_statistics and ci_percentiles for ensemble values.
  • [ ] Update tests/reporting/.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• [ ] Let Dependabot propose the update; it groups updates monthly.
  • [ ] For a major update that needs code changes, open your own pull request and close the Dependabot one with a link to it.
  • [ ] The argmin dependency is a fork (MUNQU/argmin, branch development): change the fork first, then update Cargo.lock.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: • [ ] Follow Release process.

docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The change lives in the owner that the Repository map names.
  • [ ] No engine rule is re-implemented in Python.
  • [ ] The change meets the documentation definition of done: the affected docs are updated, in the agreed format, and the doc checks pass.
  • [ ] Every new claim in the docs names a file, function or test.
  • [ ] The tests that guard the touched design decisions still pass.

docs.title: Mental Model
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Commol builds compartment models from a declarative definition and runs them as difference equations or as ordinary differential equations. Python owns the user-facing API and validation; Rust owns every rule about how a model becomes numbers. A model has a kind (today only compartmental) and an engine that runs that kind; the generic layers work with any kind.

docs.title: What Commol is
docs.text: It is Evidence A Python library with a fluent builder py-commol/commol/api/model_builder.py A validated, serializable model definition: a header, an engine and the structure of its kind py-commol/commol/context/ (Pydantic): model.py, structure.py, compartmental.py Generic layers that work with any model kind Simulation, Calibrator, reports and plots use only ModelStructure; Rust calibration uses only SimulationEngine (see Design decisions) One model compiler for both engines: expansion, flows, rates, the right-hand side crates/commol-model/ A Rust difference-equations engine crates/commol-difference/ A Rust ODE engine on diffsol crates/commol-differential/ A JIT compiler for rate expressions crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/jit/ (Cranelift) A calibration toolkit: optimizers, constraints, ensembles crates/commol-calibration/, py-commol/commol/api/calibrator.py, probabilistic_calibrator.py

docs.title: What Commol is not
docs.text: It is not Boundary A domain library It knows bins, categories and rates, not diseases or drugs. Domain vocabulary belongs in user scripts. A numerical-methods library The differential engine delegates the integration to diffsol; Commol keeps no ODE method of its own (see Design decisions). A clock A model has no physical time: rates are per step and periods are step counts, and the axis is the independent variable of the model, whatever quantity it is. TimeScale converts at the edges (see Design decisions). A rule engine for transitions A transition has no condition. A rate expresses a gate, such as if(A > 0, k, 0) (see Mathematical expressions), and stratified rates set a rate per category.

docs.title: Model kind and engine
docs.text:
Term What it is Where Model kind How a model is built: its structure. compartmental: bins expanded over stratifications, joined by transitions. ModelKind (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs); ModelStructure and its subclasses in Python Engine How a model of a kind advances along the axis, and what a rate means: DifferenceEquations, DifferentialEquations. EngineType, the one list (engine.rs); Model.engine

Each engine runs one kind. A model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made.

docs.title: How a model flows through the layers
docs.text:
ModelBuilder ... .build(engine)    -> commol.context.Model[CompartmentalStructure]
                                      (Pydantic validation; the engine's list
                                      checks model.engine and its kind)
Simulation(model)                  -> engine_state.build_engine(model JSON)
                                   -> commol_rs.core.Model.from_json(...)
                                   -> commol_rs.engine.Engine(...): the engine
                                      model.engine.type names (EngineType list),
                                      after it checks the kind of model.structure
                                   every compartmental engine compiles it with commol-model (CompiledModel):
                                        expand bins and stratifications into compartments
                                        build the initial state
                                        plan the transition flows and compile the rates
                                        derivatives(step, t, X) = Σ flows
Simulation.run(n) / run_at(at)     -> difference: X += derivatives, once per step
                                      differential: diffsol integrates derivatives
Calibrator(simulation, problem)    -> commol_rs.calibration.calibrate(engine, ...):
                                      parameters by id; values of the kind, such as
                                      initial conditions, through the engine

The same model functions also answer questions about a compartmental structure without a simulation: CompartmentalStructure.initial_state(), print_equations and the unit checker call initial_state, transition_flows and expanded_outputs of commol_rs.model through py-commol/commol/context/_model/engine_state.py.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
These hold for every change. A pull request that breaks one needs a design discussion first.

  • Rust is the single source of truth. Python asks the engine how a model expands, which state it starts with, and which flows it has. It never keeps a second implementation of those rules.
  • Compartments are identified by labels, not by names. A compartment is a bin plus one category per applied stratification (OutputLabels, CompartmentLayout). Code never parses a compartment name or matches it by prefix: bin A and bin A_x must never be confused.
  • A model that cannot be simulated as written is rejected when it is built. The flow planner returns an error instead of dropping a transition.
  • Stratification declaration order is part of the model. Stratifications expand in declaration order, and a conditional stratification may only reference stratifications declared before it.
  • Results are reproducible. The same formula always runs the same compiled code (global JIT cache), and calibrations accept a seed.
  • What the user saves, the engine reloads. Model.to_json writes every field, and calibrated values written back to a model reproduce the state the optimizer scored.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Name the user-facing behavior first.
  • [ ] Find the layer that owns it in the Repository map.
  • [ ] If Python needs an engine rule, add or use a binding instead of re-implementing it.
  • [ ] Read the tests next to that code before you add new patterns.

Back to Codebase Guide

Use this page when you know what to change but not where it belongs.

docs.title: Rust crates
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here crates/commol-core/src/types/ The model data types shared by all crates and serialized from Python: Model (header, engine, structure), ModelStructure (one variant per kind, tagged by kind), CompartmentalStructure (compartmental.rs), Transition (transitions.rs), InitialConditions, …; test_kind.rs only with the test-kind feature. Engine behavior. crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs EngineType, the one list of engines (model types): per entry, the model kind it runs (ModelKind, with the value types it accepts, ModelValueType), its settings and their validation, the form of its equations and the meaning of a rate. ModelEngine, the engine and settings of a model. The engines themselves. crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/ Parsing, preprocessing and evaluation of rate expressions; the Cranelift JIT and its global cache (jit/). Model-specific variables. crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs The SimulationEngine trait, for an engine of any kind: runs at positions (check_position), outputs (output_names, state_outputs, output_sums), parameters, reset, and the values of its kind (plan_values, apply_values, ValuePlan); Trajectory, check_positions. What calibration needs from any engine. Code for one engine or one kind. crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs Expansion of bins and accumulators over stratifications (expand, expand_compartments, expand_accumulators), the initial state (initial_state), name checks (check_names), the subgroup total names (subgroup_total_names), impulse schedules and the compilation into CompiledModel (try_from_model). Flow planning; stepping. crates/commol-model/src/layout.rs CompartmentLayout: compartments in engine order with their labels, and lookups by bin and categories. Name parsing. crates/commol-model/src/labels.rs OutputLabels (bin and categories of an output) and output_sums (bin totals and partial totals). Name parsing. crates/commol-model/src/engine.rs CompartmentalEngine: what a compartmental engine gives besides SimulationEngine (compartments, labels, state, total, set_initial_condition). Code for one engine. crates/commol-model/src/initial_conditions.rs How initial-condition values reach a compartmental engine (InitialConditionPlan: resolution, layers, remainder); both engines' plan_values and apply_values use it. Parameter values. crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs Transition flow planning (plan_transition_flows) and its description for Python (describe_flows). Rate evaluation at run time. crates/commol-model/src/helpers.rs Stratified-rate resolution and rate rewriting helpers. New public API. crates/commol-model/src/rates.rs Evaluation of a compiled rate: fast path, JIT with resolved slots, evalexpr fallback. Flow logic. crates/commol-model/src/system.rs The right-hand side CompiledModel::derivatives, impulses (apply_impulses, impulse_positions) and the accessors both engines use. Time stepping. crates/commol-model/src/types.rs CompiledModel, compiled flows, impulse schedules, series lookup (SeriesParameter). Python types. crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs DifferenceEquations: the discrete step (state += derivatives), impulses at integer steps, the positions it accepts (integers), and its SimulationEngine and CompartmentalEngine implementations. Model compilation. crates/commol-differential/src/lib.rs DifferentialEquations: state, output positions, impulses, and its SimulationEngine and CompartmentalEngine implementations. Numerical methods. crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs The integration with diffsol: pieces between breakpoints, the finite-difference J·v, dense or sparse matrices (SPARSE_THRESHOLD). Model compilation. crates/commol-calibration/src/calibration_problem.rs Loss, constraints, the objective function, and the position check that names an observation or constraint (check_positions). It uses only SimulationEngine. Optimizer setup; anything of one model kind. crates/commol-calibration/src/values.rs How calibrated values reach any engine: parameters by id, values of the model kind through the engine (ValueWriter, check_model_values, configured_engine). How a kind resolves its values. crates/commol-calibration/src/optimization.rs Nelder-Mead and particle swarm setup on the argmin fork. Loss definitions. crates/commol-calibration/src/probabilistic/ Parallel calibration runs, deduplication, clustering and ensemble selection (NSGA-II). Statistics for reports.

docs.title: PyO3 bindings
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here py-commol/src/core.rs Bindings of the model types (Model, CompartmentalStructure, …). Logic. py-commol/src/model.rs The queries of commol_rs.model on a compartmental structure: initial_state, expanded_outputs, transition_flows, subgroup_total_names; and check_names on a model. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/engine.rs commol_rs.engine: Engine::build, which checks the kind and builds the engine an EngineType entry names, and the Python classes Engine (any engine, built from a model), EngineType (the list, for Python to ask) and ModelKind. Engine logic. py-commol/src/test_kind.rs TestEngine, the engine of the test model kind; only with the test-kind feature. Anything a release needs. py-commol/src/calibration.rs Calibration types and functions; each takes an Engine. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/commol/commol_rs/_commol_rs.pyi The type stub of the extension. Update it with every binding change. —

docs.title: Python package (py-commol/commol/)
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here api/model_builder.py The fluent ModelBuilder. Validation rules that belong to the model. api/simulation.py Simulation: runs (run, run_at), output grouping through ModelStructure.outputs_by_source. Expansion rules; which positions a model type accepts; anything of one model kind. api/results.py SimulationResults (values with their positions), index_at, sample. Engine rules. api/calibrator.py, api/probabilistic_calibrator.py Calibration entry points and conversion to Rust types. Loss or optimizer logic. api/probabilistic/ Ensemble statistics, normalization and confidence intervals (intervals.py). New interval conventions outside ci_percentiles. api/reporting.py simulation_report and applied_parameters_report, with the sections the structure adds (ModelStructure.report_sections). Domain vocabulary; sections of one model kind. api/patterns.py, api/time_scale.py, api/windows.py Rates that change along the axis (AxisPattern), step/physical-time conversion, the window grid and windowed totals. Physical time inside the model. api/plotter.py Plots of results. Computation of results. context/ The Pydantic model: fields, validation, JSON I/O, update methods. Engine rules. context/model.py Model: the header, the engine and the structure of any kind, generic in its structure class (Model[CompartmentalStructure]). Anything of one model kind. context/structure.py ModelStructure, the interface every model kind gives the generic layers, and its registry of kinds. Code of one kind. context/compartmental.py CompartmentalStructure: bins, stratifications, transitions and initial conditions, their validation, and the compartmental side of the interface. Generic code. context/transition.py Transition and StratifiedRate. — context/engine.py ModelEngine (Model.engine: the engine type and its settings), OdeSolver, and the names of the compartmental engines as the Literal CompartmentalEngineType. Settings validation or engine meanings: ask commol_rs.engine.EngineType. context/_model/engine_state.py The only Python access to the engine queries, and build_engine, which builds the engine the model names. Python re-implementations of them. context/_model/ (other files) Internals of a compartmental model: equation printer, unit checker, calibration write-back, the initial_conditions report section (report.py); JSON rendering of any model. Public API. context/report_entry.py The ensemble spread of a report entry (Interval, entry_interval), for every kind. — utils/security.py Validation of every user expression (SecurityConfig limits). Expression evaluation. utils/equations.py Dimensional analysis with pint. —

docs.title: Other paths
docs.text: Path Owns py-commol/tests/ Python tests: one package per page of the user guide (building/, transitions/, rates/, axis_patterns/, initial_conditions/, simulation/, units/, calibration/, probabilistic/, reporting/, plotting/, docs/); reference_models/, published models checked against their stated results; model_kinds/, the test model kind through every generic layer; and support/ with the shared model factories, the test kind (kinds.py), the flow models, the reference solver, the oracles and the assertions. See Tests. crates/*/tests/, #[cfg(test)] modules Rust tests. docs/ This site. docs/codebase/ is for maintainers; the rest is for users. odd/ Task records and review ledgers of past work. History, not specification. .github/workflows/ CI: code quality, build, docs, release.

docs.title: Placement rule
docs.text:
Place code at the narrowest owner that can hold it:

  1. A rule about how a model becomes numbers → a Rust crate.
  2. Type conversion between Python and Rust → py-commol/src/.
  3. Validation of user input → the Pydantic model in context/.
  4. User-facing workflow → api/.
  5. Presentation (reports, plots) → api/reporting.py, api/plotter.py.
