docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Back to Model Calibration

Two functions turn a calibrated model and a run into plain dictionaries, ready for JSON: applied_parameters_report (what the model holds and what calibration set) and simulation_report (what a run produced, next to the observations). Both work for a single calibration and for an ensemble, with the same layout.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
import json

from commol import (
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    ModelBuilder,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    Simulation,
    applied_parameters_report,
    simulation_report,
    windowed_totals,
)

def model(k1: float | None):
    return (
        ModelBuilder(name="Reported")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
        .add_parameter(id="k1", value=k1)
        .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
        .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
        .add_transition(
            id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total", accumulators=["cum_ab"]
        )
        .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
        .set_initial_conditions(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions=[
                {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.99},
                {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.01},
                {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
            ],
        )
        .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
    )

ends = [7, 14, 21, 28]
truth = Simulation(model(0.4)).run(num_steps=28)
observed_data = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=end, output="cum_ab", value=count, window=7)
    for end, count in zip(ends, windowed_totals(truth["cum_ab"], truth.positions, 7, ends))
]
problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=observed_data,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k1", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0)
    ],
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=500),
)

calibrated = model(None)
result = Calibrator(Simulation(calibrated), problem).run()
calibrated.apply_calibration_parameters(result, problem)

applied = applied_parameters_report(calibrated, result, problem)
print(json.dumps(applied["parameters"]["k2"]))  # {"value": 0.1, "calibrated": false}

simulation = Simulation(calibrated)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=28)
run_report = simulation_report(
    simulation,
    results,
    at=ends,
    window=7,
    num_windows=4,
    observed_data=observed_data,
    accumulators=["cum_ab"],
)
print(sorted(run_report))  # ['accumulators', 'observed', 'series']

docs.title: applied_parameters_report
docs.text:
applied_parameters_report(model, result, problem=None, parameter_statistics=None, confidence_level=None) lists every number the calibrated model holds, and whether calibration set it. The parameters section is the same for every kind of model; the structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (ModelStructure.report_sections). A compartmental model adds initial_conditions:

{
  "parameters": {
    "k1": {"value": 0.4, "calibrated": true},
    "k2": {"value": 0.1, "calibrated": false}
  },
  "initial_conditions": {
    "total": {"group": "total", "fraction": 1.0, "value": 1000.0, "calibrated": false},
    "A": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.99, "value": 990.0, "calibrated": false},
    "B": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.01, "value": 10.0, "calibrated": false},
    "C": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.0, "value": 0.0, "calibrated": false}
  }
}
Argument Meaning model The model after apply_calibration_parameters. result A CalibrationResult, a ProbabilisticCalibrationResult, or an {id: value} mapping. problem Optional. Adds the factor parameters, which the model does not hold. parameter_statistics, confidence_level Optional. Taken from a probabilistic result when not given. Entry Rule Parameters Only numeric parameters: formulas and series are inputs, not fitted values. total The declared total, with fraction 1.0. Initial-condition value The amount the engine builds, overrides included. Initial-condition fraction That amount over total, so every row shares one denominator. group "total", or the conditioning categories for a conditional stratification. An uncalibrated bin (None fraction) fraction and value are null. A probabilistic result Each entry gains an interval block, and the report starts with confidence_level.

The key order of each entry is fixed (value, calibrated, then interval; group, fraction, value, calibrated, then interval), so saved JSON files stay comparable.

docs.title: simulation_report
docs.text:
simulation_report(simulation, results, at, window, num_windows, observed_data=(), accumulators=(), ensemble_runs=None, confidence_level=None) reports a run on one axis of windows. It reads each value at a position of the results (results.positions), so it works for any model type: a differential model reports at non-integer positions once the results hold them (Reporting at any position).

Block Content observed For each observation label: values, padded to num_windows, so it lines up with windowed index for index. An observation goes to the window that holds its position (window_index). weights, outputs and factor_id appear when a series uses them. series Each compartment output sampled at at accumulators For each accumulator: total (its final value), windowed (the gain in each window that ends within the results, as the loss compares it) and cumulative (sampled at at); each reading as a total and by_output Argument Meaning results SimulationResults of run or run_at. at The positions where series and cumulative readings are sampled; each must be a position of the results (ValueError otherwise). window, num_windows The window axis of observed and windowed. observed_data The observations to report next to the run. accumulators The accumulator ids to report. ensemble_runs, confidence_level One SimulationResults per ensemble member. Every number becomes a {mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max} block; the layout does not change.

The report holds only these blocks. Add your own envelope around them, such as a run label or summary figures in your domain's terms:

document = {"kind": "calibration", "at": ends, **run_report}
print(json.dumps(document)[:30])

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The model passed to applied_parameters_report already has the calibrated values.
  • [ ] problem is passed when there are factor parameters.
  • [ ] at, window and num_windows match the observations, and the results hold every position the report reads.

docs.title: Running Simulations
docs.text:
Back to Home

Simulation runs a built Model in the Rust engine and returns its outputs: one series per compartment and per accumulator, with the positions on the axis they were read at. This page covers running a model, reading and aggregating its outputs, running it in continuous time as differential equations, and plotting them.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total", accumulators=["cum_ab"]
    )
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.1},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

print(simulation.simulation_outputs)  # ['A', 'B', 'C', 'cum_ab']
print(f"C at step 100: {results['C'][-1]:.0f}")

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
Member Returns What it does Simulation(model) — Builds the engine for the model. A model with uncalibrated parameters can be built, but not run. run(num_steps) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state, with the model as it is now, and reports at the positions 0, 1, …, num_steps. Raises ValueError if a parameter is still None. run_at(at) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state and reports at the given sorted positions only. The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferentialEquations model any non-negative position, such as 0.5; a DifferenceEquations model only integer steps. Otherwise ValueError, with the engine's message. See Differential equations. simulation_outputs list[str] The output names, in engine order: compartments first, then accumulators. outputs_for(id) list[str] The outputs of one bin or accumulator. group_outputs(ids) dict[str, list[str]] The outputs of several bins or accumulators, keyed by id. total_series(results, ids) list[float] The sum of all outputs of the given ids, at each position of the results. windowed_totals(results, ids, window, at=None) list[float] What the given accumulators gained in each window. engine engine The underlying Rust engine, for the model as it is now: the engine model.engine.type names (engine.engine_type). engine.step() advances it one step; engine.reset() returns it to the initial state.

Every run starts again from the initial state, so two calls with the same model give the same result (Simulation.run resets the engine first). To continue a run step by step, use the engine:

first = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
again = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(again["A"] == first["A"])  # True: it started again

simulation.engine.step()  # step 11, from where the last run stopped
print(simulation.engine.state[0] < first["A"][-1])  # True: A keeps falling

The engine follows the model. When the model changed after the Simulation was created, for example with update_parameters or apply_calibration_parameters, run and engine rebuild the engine from the model as it is now (Simulation._sync_engine compares model_dump_json() with the JSON the engine was built from):

model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.0})
frozen = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(frozen["A"][10] == frozen["A"][0])  # True: k1 = 0 stops A → B
model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.3})

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
run and run_at return SimulationResults (py-commol/commol/api/results.py): a dict from output name to one value per position, so results["A"], json.dumps(results) and pandas.DataFrame(results) work as for any mapping. The positions the values were read at are in results.positions.

Member Shape Use for results[name] [value at positions[0], …] Reading one output, plotting results.positions [0.0, 1.0, …, n] for run(n); the requested positions for run_at Reading a value at a position, windows, reports results.rows() [[every output at positions[0]], …], in simulation_outputs order Matrix operations, export

run(num_steps) holds num_steps + 1 positions: position 0 is the initial state.

rows = results.rows()

print(results.positions[:3])  # [0.0, 1.0, 2.0]
print(len(rows))              # 101
print(len(rows[0]))           # 4: A, B, C and cum_ab
print([round(value) for value in rows[0]])  # [900, 100, 0, 0]

docs.title: Accumulators
docs.text:
An accumulator output starts at 0 and only grows: it is the total that its transitions have moved since step 0. Here cum_ab is everything that has moved from A to B, so A plus cum_ab stays at the initial A:

print(round(results["A"][-1] + results["cum_ab"][-1]))  # 900

docs.title: Stratified outputs
docs.text:
With stratifications, every bin and accumulator has one output per combination of categories, named {id}_{category}_{category}… in the order the stratifications were declared.

stratified = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stratified")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(id="type", categories=["t1", "t2"])
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k", accumulators=["cum_ab"])
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
        stratification_fractions=[
            {
                "stratification": "group",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "g1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "g2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            },
            {
                "stratification": "type",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "t1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "t2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            },
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

stratified_simulation = Simulation(stratified)
stratified_results = stratified_simulation.run(num_steps=50)

print(stratified_simulation.outputs_for("B"))
# ['B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2', 'B_g2_t1', 'B_g2_t2']
print(stratified_simulation.group_outputs(["A", "cum_ab"])["cum_ab"])
# ['cum_ab_g1_t1', 'cum_ab_g1_t2', 'cum_ab_g2_t1', 'cum_ab_g2_t2']

docs.title: Totals by bin
docs.text:
total_series sums every output of the ids you give, at each position:

total_b = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["B"])
total_ab = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["A", "B"])
print(round(total_ab[-1]))  # 1000: A and B hold the whole total

Do not select outputs by name prefix

[k for k in results if k.startswith("B_")] also matches an accumulator named B_events, and, with conditional stratifications, outputs may have fewer suffixes than their siblings. outputs_for, group_outputs and total_series use the model structure, so neither case can go wrong.

docs.title: Totals by category
docs.text:
To select compartments by category, use their labels from CompartmentalStructure.initial_state(): each entry has name, bin and categories.

in_g1 = [
    compartment.name
    for compartment in stratified.structure.initial_state()
    if compartment.categories.get("group") == "g1"
]
print(in_g1)  # ['A_g1_t1', 'A_g1_t2', 'B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2']

total_g1 = [
    sum(stratified_results[name][step] for name in in_g1)
    for step in range(len(stratified_results[in_g1[0]]))
]
print(round(total_g1[-1]))  # 500: g1 started with half of the total

docs.title: Windowed totals
docs.text:
windowed_totals turns a cumulative output into the amount it gained in each window of length window on the axis. Window w covers (w · window, (w + 1) · window], and each value is the output at the end of the window minus the output at its start. Both must be positions of the results.

per_week = stratified_simulation.windowed_totals(
    stratified_results, ["cum_ab"], window=7
)
print(len(per_week))  # 7: the complete windows of a 50-step run
Argument Meaning ids Accumulator ids; their outputs are summed first. window The window length on the axis. Must be positive. at The positions where windows close. By default, every complete window of the results (window_ends). Pass observation positions to get the values a calibration compares against.

The window grid and the same reduction work on any series with the module-level functions of py-commol/commol/api/windows.py:

Function Returns window_start(i, window), window_end(i, window) The positions that bound window i: i · window and (i + 1) · window window_index(at, window) The window that holds a position, max(ceil(at / window) − 1, 0); the inverse of window_end. Reports place observations with it. window_ends(window, end) Every complete window end up to end windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at=None) The gain of a series over each window 
from commol import window_end, window_ends, window_index, windowed_totals

print(window_ends(window=7, end=30))                       # [7, 14, 21, 28]
print(window_end(0, 7), window_index(7, 7), window_index(7.5, 7))  # 7 0 1
print(windowed_totals([0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28], range(8), 3))  # [6, 15]

A window need not be a whole number of steps: see Reporting at any position.

docs.title: Differential equations
docs.text:
A model built with engine="DifferentialEquations" runs in continuous time. The engine (crates/commol-differential/) integrates dX/dt = Σ flows(t, X) with the ODE solver diffsol. The flows are the same as in a difference model: the same transitions, rates, accumulators, outputs, calibration, reports and plots. Only the way the engine advances changes.

import math

from commol import OdeSolver

ode_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Decay")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1", accumulators=["moved"])
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
    )
    .build(
        engine="DifferentialEquations",
        settings=OdeSolver(method="tsit45", rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8),
    )
)

ode = Simulation(ode_model)
at = ode.run_at([0, 0.5, 2.25])
print(round(at["A"][2], 3), round(1000 * math.exp(-0.1 * 2.25), 3))  # 798.516 798.516
print(round(ode.run(num_steps=10)["moved"][10], 1))  # 632.1: the integral of the flow

docs.title: Solver settings
docs.text:
OdeSolver holds the settings of the DifferentialEquations engine. They are part of the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces its runs. Pass them where you choose the engine, build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...), so one builder can build the model for each engine with its own settings; without them the defaults apply. The DifferenceEquations engine takes no settings: the engine rejects settings of another engine with an error that names both (ValidationError).

Field Default Meaning method "tsit45" "tsit45": explicit Runge–Kutta 5(4), for non-stiff models. "bdf": backward differentiation formulas, for stiff models (rates of very different speeds). rtol 1e-6 Relative tolerance of each state component. atol 1e-6 Absolute tolerance of each state component, in the unit of the bins.

bdf builds its Jacobian from a finite-difference Jacobian-vector product. It uses a dense matrix below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and a sparse one from there (crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs).

docs.title: Time inside a step
docs.text:
On [n, n + 1) a rate sees step = n and the position t, which moves continuously. A rate that reads step, a "pulse" series or a pulse pattern (AxisPattern.pulse, pulses, periodic) is constant on its unit interval, and the engine restarts the integration at each integer where such a rate can jump. A per-capita pulse p on step n acts as the constant rate p for one unit: it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source, not p as in a difference model. To move a fraction at once, use an impulse.

A "step_function" or "linear" series and the patterns AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp read t, so they change at any position, and the engine restarts the integration at their points and bounds. In a difference model t equals step, so they give the same results as a rate that reads step.

A rate can also jump where t reaches a value that it compares t with, such as if(t >= t_on, beta, 0). The engine restarts the integration there too, so the solver cannot step over a short window. This works when the value reads only numbers, pi, e and parameters with a constant or calibrated value, and t is one side of the comparison: write t >= 10, not t - 10 >= 0. A jump that depends on the state, such as if(t >= A, ...), is not found.

TimeScale.rate_from_mean_duration and rate_from_probability give per-step probabilities for difference models. A differential model needs the continuous rate; see Steps and physical time.

from commol import AxisPattern

pulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Pulse")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate=AxisPattern.pulse(at=2, value=0.2))
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
    )
)
ode_pulse = Simulation(pulse_model.build(engine="DifferentialEquations")).run(num_steps=3)
print(round(ode_pulse["A"][2] - ode_pulse["A"][3], 1))  # 181.3 = 1000 (1 − e^−0.2)

docs.title: Reporting at any position
docs.text:
run_at(at) reports at sorted positions on the axis, from the dense output of the solver. Observations (ObservedDataPoint.at), windows (ObservedDataPoint.window) and constraint positions (CalibrationConstraint.at) may lie between integers for a differential model: the calibration reads the engine at those positions (Observations). A difference model reports only at integer steps; the engine rejects any other position and names the object that holds it.

Windows, reports and plots read a value at a position of the results, so a window of 2.5 works once the results hold its ends:

ends = window_ends(window=2.5, end=10)    # [2.5, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0]
ode_windows = ode.run_at([0.0, *ends])
gained = ode.windowed_totals(ode_windows, ["moved"], window=2.5)
print([round(value, 1) for value in gained])  # [221.2, 172.3, 134.2, 104.5]

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text:
SimulationPlotter(simulation, results) draws one subplot per output with seaborn, and returns the matplotlib Figure:

from commol import PlotConfig, SimulationPlotter

plotter = SimulationPlotter(simulation, results)  # the results of the first run
plotter.plot_series(output_file="series.png")
plotter.plot_cumulative(output_file="cumulative.png")

plotter.plot_series(
    output_file="custom.png",
    config=PlotConfig(figsize=(16, 10), dpi=150, style="whitegrid", palette="Set2", context="talk"),
    series=["B", "C"],
    x_label="Week",
    tick_every=10,
    position_label=lambda at: f"w{int(at) // 7}",
    linewidth=2.5,
    alpha=0.8,
)
Argument Default Meaning output_file None Where to save the figure. None only returns it. series None (every output) What to plot, one subplot each: an output name (B_g1) or a bin or accumulator id (B), which plots the sum of its outputs (Simulation.outputs_for). An exact output name wins. An unknown entry raises ValueError. observed_data None ObservedDataPoints to draw on the subplot of their label, at their positions (a differential model may observe between integers). An observation with a window draws the windowed line, which reads the results at every window end and start (ValueError when the results do not hold one). calibration_result None With a probabilistic result, draws the median and the confidence band; factor parameters are applied to the observations. config PlotConfig() Figure size, dpi, layout and seaborn style. show_legend True plot_series only. x_label, tick_every, position_label "Step", every plotted position, the position plot_series only. Label the x axis, for example in weeks. The x axis shows results.positions. other keyword arguments — Passed to seaborn.lineplot, such as linewidth or alpha. PlotConfig field Default Values figsize (12, 8) Inches (width, height) dpi 100 Resolution layout None (automatic) (rows, columns) style None "darkgrid", "whitegrid", "dark", "white", "ticks" palette None A seaborn palette or matplotlib colormap, such as "Set2" context None "paper", "notebook", "talk", "poster"

To compare with observations:

from commol import ObservedDataPoint

observed = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=10, output="B", value=45.2),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=20, output="B", value=78.5),
]
plotter.plot_series(output_file="with_data.png", observed_data=observed)

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

A transition moves an amount at every step: from its source compartments to its target compartments, at the rate you give. This page documents ModelBuilder.add_transition completely: rates, several sources, transitions between categories, stratified rates, impulses, and what build checks.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Transitions")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.1},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

model.print_equations()  # shows every flow as the engine computes it

docs.title: add_transition
docs.text: Argument Type Default Meaning id str required The identifier. source list[str] required Bins (or one category) that lose the flow. [] means the flow enters the system. target list[str] required Bins (or one category) that gain the flow. [] means the flow leaves the system. rate str, float, AxisPattern or None None The rate formula; see Rates. With stratified_rates, the fallback rate. None with no stratified rate gives a transition with no flows. stratified_rates list[dict] \| None None Rates for some categories; see Stratified rates. per_compartment bool \| None None Replaces bin names in the rate with each flow's own compartment; see per_compartment. accumulators list[str] \| None None Accumulators that count the flow; see Building Models. impulse_at list[float] \| None None Makes the transition an impulse at these steps; see Impulses. impulse_every tuple[float, float] \| None None (period, offset): an impulse at offset, offset + period, …; see Impulses.

docs.title: Rates
docs.text: A rate is a formula (a string), a number, or a AxisPattern. A formula can use parameters, compartments, bin totals, total, step, constants and functions; see Mathematical Expressions.

docs.title: Absolute and per-capita rates
docs.text:
The engine decides for each flow whether its rate is the flow itself or a rate per member of the source:

Case Kind Flow per step The rate names a compartment, a bin total, total or a total_… variable Absolute rate The transition has no source Absolute rate A stratified rate sets "absolute": True or False As set — Otherwise Per-capita rate × source Rate Kind Flow from B to C "k2" Per-capita k2 * B "k2 * B" Absolute k2 * B "k1 * A * B / total" Absolute k1 * A * B / total "0.5" with source=[] Absolute 0.5 enters the target

print_equations() prints every flow after this decision, so a per-capita rate appears multiplied by its source.

docs.title: Time-dependent rates
docs.text:
A formula may use step (or t), the current step:

seasonal = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Seasonal")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365)) * A * B / total",
    )
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.99}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.01}],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

For pulses, windows, ramps and schedules per group, use Axis Patterns.

docs.title: Several sources or targets
docs.text:
A transition with several sources or targets moves one flow, like a reaction: every entry in source loses it and every entry in target gains it. A bin listed twice loses or gains it twice. The rate must be absolute.

reaction = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Reaction")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.001)
    .add_transition(id="reaction", source=["A", "B"], target=["C", "C"], rate="k * A * B")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.5},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.5},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)
reaction.print_equations()
# A loses k * A * B, B loses k * A * B, C gains 2 * (k * A * B)

docs.title: The $compartment placeholder
docs.text:
For independent flows with one formula, write $compartment in the rate. The builder creates one transition per source (or per target), named {id}__{compartment}, with $compartment replaced by that compartment:

outflow = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Outflow")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="mu", value=0.01)
    .add_transition(
        id="outflow",
        source=["A", "B", "C"],
        target=[],
        rate="mu * $compartment * (1 + 0.1 * $compartment / total)",
    )
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.4},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.3},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.3},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

for transition in outflow.structure.transitions:
    print(transition.id, transition.rate)
# outflow__A mu * A * (1 + 0.1 * A / total)
# outflow__B mu * B * (1 + 0.1 * B / total)
# outflow__C mu * C * (1 + 0.1 * C / total)
Rule Otherwise Several sources with one or no target, or several targets with one or no source ValueError: the mapping would be ambiguous At least two sources or two targets ValueError: write the compartment name instead A rate is given ValueError

stratified_rates may also use $compartment; each generated transition gets its own copy.

docs.title: Transitions between categories
docs.text:
When source and target are categories of one stratification, the transition moves amounts between them in every bin:

moving = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Moving")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="move", source=["g1"], target=["g2"], rate="k")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.5}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.5}],
        stratification_fractions=[
            {
                "stratification": "group",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "g1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "g2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)
moving.print_equations()
# move (g1 -> g2):  A_g1 -> A_g2: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2: k * B_g1

A category transition needs exactly one source and one target category. If the target category is split by a conditional stratification, every flow must say which of its categories it enters, with a to condition (see Redirecting the target with to); otherwise build raises.

docs.title: per_compartment
docs.text:
With stratifications, a bin id in a rate means the total of the bin. In a flow from A_g1, "k * A" uses A_g1 + A_g2. per_compartment=True replaces each source and target bin id with the flow's own compartment:

Flow rate="k * A" with per_compartment=True A_g1 -> B_g1 k * A (the total) k * A_g1 A_g2 -> B_g2 k * A (the total) k * A_g2 
own_compartment = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Per compartment")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k * A", per_compartment=True)
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.5}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.5}],
        stratification_fractions=[
            {
                "stratification": "group",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "g1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "g2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)
own_compartment.print_equations()
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k * A_g1   and   A_g2 -> B_g2: k * A_g2

It applies to the fallback rate and to every stratified rate, and only to transitions between bins.

docs.title: Stratified rates
docs.text:
stratified_rates gives some categories their own rate. Each entry has conditions and a rate, and may set absolute:

group_rates = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Group rates")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2", "g3"])
    .add_parameter(id="k_g1", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="k_g2", value=0.10)
    .add_parameter(id="k_default", value=0.05)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k_default",
        stratified_rates=[
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}], "rate": "k_g1"},
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}], "rate": "k_g2"},
        ],
    )
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=900,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
        stratification_fractions=[
            {
                "stratification": "group",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "g1", "fraction": 0.3},
                    {"category": "g2", "fraction": 0.3},
                    {"category": "g3", "fraction": 0.4},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)
group_rates.print_equations()
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k_g1 * A_g1,  A_g2 -> B_g2: k_g2 * A_g2,  A_g3 -> B_g3: k_default * A_g3
Entry key Type Meaning conditions list[dict] All must match the source compartment (AND). rate str or float The rate for matching compartments. absolute bool, optional Forces the rate to be absolute or per-capita. Condition key Meaning stratification The stratification id. category Optional. The category the source must have. to Optional. The category the target gets instead; see below.

Which rate applies: for each source compartment, the entry that matches with the most conditions wins; on a tie, the first one in the list. With no match, the fallback rate applies. With three stratifications and one entry for g2, t1, v2:

Source compartment Conditions matched Rate A_g2_t1_v2 3 of 3 The entry A_g2_t1_v1 not all Fallback A_g1_t1_v1 not all Fallback

docs.title: Redirecting the target with to
docs.text:
A condition with category filters the source. A condition with to changes the target category. A condition with only to filters nothing, so it can send the flow into a stratification that the source does not have:

redirect = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Redirect")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(
        id="subtype",
        categories=["s1", "s2"],
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}],
    )
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="move",
        source=["g1"],
        target=["g2"],
        stratified_rates=[{"conditions": [{"stratification": "subtype", "to": "s1"}], "rate": "k"}],
    )
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.5}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.5}],
        stratification_fractions=[
            {
                "stratification": "group",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "g1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "g2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            },
            {
                "stratification": "subtype",
                "fractions": [
                    {"category": "s1", "fraction": 0.5},
                    {"category": "s2", "fraction": 0.5},
                ],
            },
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)
redirect.print_equations()
# A_g1 -> A_g2_s1: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2_s1: k * B_g1

docs.title: Limiting when a transition runs
docs.text: A transition runs at every step. To limit a flow, write the condition in the rate with if, as in "if(step > 30, k, 0)", or use a AxisPattern, a series parameter or a stratified rate. A comparison alone is a boolean, so "k * (step > 30)" is rejected.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text:
An impulse moves its amount at once, at given steps, and nothing between them. Give the steps with impulse_at=[…] or impulse_every=(period, offset). The rate is then a fraction of the source (per-capita) or an amount (absolute), with the same rules, sources, targets, stratified rates and accumulators as any transition.

impulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Impulses")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved by the impulse")
    .add_parameter(id="p", value=0.25)
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="jump", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="p", impulse_at=[1], accumulators=["moved"])
    .add_transition(id="flow", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

jumped = Simulation(impulse_model).run(num_steps=2)
print([round(a, 1) for a in jumped["A"]])  # [1000.0, 675.0, 607.5]
print(jumped["moved"][2])  # 225.0: a quarter of the 900 left at step 1
Rule In both engines Order At step n the state jumps first; then the flows of the step run from the new state. The output at n shows the state after the jump (CompiledModel::apply_impulses in crates/commol-model/src/system.rs). Several impulses at one step Every jump is computed from the state before any of them. Steps A DifferentialEquations model takes any steps, such as 0.5: the engine stops there, applies the jump and restarts. A DifferenceEquations model needs integer steps (ValidationError names the transition). Units The rate of an impulse is an amount, <bin unit>, not a flow per step (Units and Equations). print_equations Lists impulses apart from the equations, with their steps.

An impulse is not a pulse rate. A AxisPattern.pulse is a rate: a difference model applies it for one step with the other flows, and a differential model applies it as a constant rate for one time unit, so it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source. An impulse moves exactly p of its source in both engines.

docs.title: What building checks
docs.text:
build plans every flow in the engine and rejects a transition it cannot simulate as written:

Rejected Message names A source or target that is neither a bin nor a category of one stratification The transition A category transition without exactly one source and one target The transition A rate variable that is not a parameter, bin, compartment or special variable The variable and the available names Several sources with a per-capita rate The transition; use an absolute rate or $compartment A stratified rate whose category conditions match no source compartment The categories; use to to reach another stratification A flow that ends in categories no compartment has The transition; add a to condition impulse_at and impulse_every together, a negative step, or a period that is not positive The transition A non-integer impulse step in a DifferenceEquations model The transition and the step

docs.title: Units and Equations
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

Commol can check that every rate has the right units, and can print the equations that the engine simulates, as text or LaTeX. Both work on a built Model.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import ModelBuilder

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Model with Units", bin_unit="item")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="1/day")
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[
            {"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9},
            {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.1},
            {"bin": "C", "fraction": 0.0},
        ],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.
model.print_equations()

docs.title: Unit checking
docs.text: Model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=False) checks that every flow has the unit <bin unit>/<step unit>, every impulse the unit <bin unit>, and that every function receives a plain number. It checks DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations models alike: in both, a rate is per unit of the axis. It raises UnitConsistencyError (from commol.utils.equations) and lists every transition that fails.

docs.title: What needs a unit
docs.text: Item How it gets a unit Bins ModelBuilder(bin_unit=...), or add_bin(unit=...) for one bin. Required: the check names every bin without one. total, total_<category>… The bin unit, automatically Constant parameters add_parameter(unit=...). Required: the check raises if one is missing. Formula parameters Inferred from the formula; a unit is optional step, t, pi, e Dimensionless, automatically Unit Use for "1/day", "1/week", "1/step" Rates "dimensionless" Ratios, fractions, amplitudes, function arguments Any word, such as "item" A custom unit for bins; Commol registers it

docs.title: The step unit
docs.text:
The engine applies every flow once per step and converts no value between units. So one step has one unit, and every rate must use it (UnitChecker._step_unit in py-commol/commol/context/_model/units.py).

The axis of a model is its independent variable: the quantity the model steps along or differentiates over. Time is one case; a length, a dose or any other quantity is another. So the step unit may have any single dimension. Declare it with ModelBuilder(..., step_unit="meter") (Model.step_unit); check_step_unit accepts one unit of one dimension with exponent 1, such as day or meter, and rejects 1/day or meter**2. When it is not declared, the check infers it from the parameters:

Parameter units Step unit Result All in one unit of time, such as "1/day" and "day" day Flows must be <bin unit>/day All in "1/week" week Accepted: one step is one week All in "1/step" step Accepted No unit of time step Flows must be <bin unit>/step "1/day" and "1/week", or "1/day" and "1/step" — Error that names each parameter and its unit

Inference looks only at units of time: a unit of dimension [time] (second, hour, day, week, month, year, …) or step. A rate in 1/meter needs step_unit="meter"; without it the step unit is step and the flow fails. Two names of one unit, such as d and day, are one unit. A flow must have exactly the expected unit: person/week does not match person/day, because the engine would apply a weekly rate every day.

along_a_line = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Along a line", bin_unit="item", step_unit="meter")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.01, unit="1/meter")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 1.0}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.0}],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferentialEquations")
)
along_a_line.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.

TimeScale.from_step_unit(unit) gives the time scale of a step unit of time, and raises ValueError for a unit of another dimension, such as meter.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text: An impulse moves an amount at once, so its rate must have the bin unit: p * A with p in "dimensionless" is an amount of <bin unit>; k * A with k in "1/day" is a flow and fails with expected '<bin unit>'.

docs.title: What the check catches
docs.text:
from commol.utils.equations import UnitConsistencyError

wrong_units = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Wrong units", bin_unit="item")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="day")  # should be "1/day"
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_ba", source=["B"], target=["A"], rate="k2 * sin(B) * B")
    .set_initial_conditions(
        total=1000,
        bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9}, {"bin": "B", "fraction": 0.1}],
    )
    .build(engine="DifferenceEquations")
)

try:
    wrong_units.check_unit_consistency()
except UnitConsistencyError as error:
    print(error)
Error Cause Unit mismatch: equation '…' has unit 'day * item' but expected 'item/day' A rate with the wrong unit Cannot convert from 'item' to 'dimensionless' A function such as sin, exp or log received a quantity with a unit The following constant parameters are missing units: … A constant parameter has no unit The following bins have no unit: … A bin has no unit (set bin_unit) the parameters use more than one unit of time ('k1' in '1/day', 'k2' in '1/week') Rates in two units of time; see The step unit Variable '…' … has no defined unit A variable of a rate has no unit

To pass a quantity to a function, make it dimensionless first, for example sin(2 * pi * step / 365) or exp(-decay * step) with decay in "dimensionless".

docs.title: Printing equations
docs.text:
Model.print_equations(output_file=None, format="text") prints the flows that the engine plans, after it has decided which rates are per-capita (see Transitions). It has three parts:

Part Content Model information Name, engine, and the number of bins, stratifications, parameters and transitions Compact form Each transition and its flows, source -> target: rate. With units, each symbol shows its unit and each flow its resulting unit. Expanded form One difference equation per compartment: [A(t+Dt) - A(t)] / Dt = …

For the model above, the compact form is:

t_ab (A -> B):
  A -> B: k1(1/day) * A(item) * B(item) / total(item) [item / day]
t_bc (B -> C):
  B -> C: k2(1/day) * B(item) [item / day]

and the expanded form is:

[A(t+Dt) - A(t)] / Dt = - (k1 * A * B / total)
[B(t+Dt) - B(t)] / Dt = (k1 * A * B / total) - (k2 * B)
[C(t+Dt) - C(t)] / Dt = (k2 * B)
Argument Values Effect format "text" (default), "latex" LaTeX writes inline math for the compact form and display math (\[…\]) for the expanded form. output_file None (default) or a path Writes to the file instead of printing. 
model.print_equations(format="latex", output_file="equations.tex")

Units appear only when every bin and every constant parameter has one. If only some parameters have a unit, print_equations raises ValueError ("Some parameters have units but not all").
